From lab, using the same frozen creatinine vocabulary but without requiring a rise, define (a) any valid creatinine result in 360–2880 and (b) minutes from 360 to the first such result. Fit the same B0/B1 feature blocks to this endpoint using an observation-process loss and censoring rule. This endpoint is not a clinical outcome and is not assumed independent of hypotension: a strong duration association is evidence that clinical concern/measurement intensity may create ascertainment. Report the joint pattern rather than treating it as proof of bias. Use inverse-probability-of-observation weights estimated in training hospitals from baseline severity, early BP coverage/modality, labs, recorded treatment, and early discharge/EOL process features; never use post-index creatinine values or post-index EOL fields to construct predictors.

2. Pre-index negative-control process check. Preserve the parent’s frozen pre-index check: among stays with a valid creatinine in -48–-24 and a distinct result in -24–0, use the same 0.3-mg/dL rise rule. The primary contrasts are held-out incremental log loss, Brier score, calibration intercept/slope, and risk curves; AUROC/AUPRC are secondary. The dataset lacks clinician-adjudicated AKI, reliable pre-ICU kidney function, verified laboratory units, complete fluid balance, calibrated raw BP waveforms, validated renal-replacement intent, staffing/bed context, and independent external validation. Even a positive, process-robust result remains a transportable prognostic association requiring clinical adjudication and external validation.

Status: proposed substantive child of candidate-5e34d7c66f47264a743e91eb. No full cohort, label audit, fit, or result has been computed.

## Scientific bottleneck and revised question

The parent asks whether cumulative systemic MAP time below 65 mmHg in ICU minutes 0–360 adds transportable prognostic information for a new creatinine-defined event in minutes 360–2880, beyond nadir and early severity. That question remains clinically useful, but the parent’s process and treatment checks are primarily ablations. A duration variable can still look incremental if the same unmeasured deterioration causes more BP checks, more creatinine orders, pressor treatment, and AKI ascertainment. Conversely, recorded treatment can be a response/mediator rather than a nuisance confounder. The eICU fields cannot identify either mechanism or a treatment effect.

The revised falsifiable question is:

> Within adult first eICU stays with common support on early severity, BP observation, treatment recording, and creatinine ascertainment, does early cumulative hypotension duration provide reproducible held-out prognostic information for subsequent creatinine rise that is not mirrored by the observation process and does not disappear after cross-fitted adjustment for recorded treatment/process variables?

This is a prognostic/descriptive estimand, not a causal effect of hypotension or a treatment recommendation. The strongest evidence currently supports only that temporal hypotension summaries can be prognostic in a prior cohort [K1], that a 0.3-mg/dL creatinine rise is part of a KDIGO-style AKI definition [K2], and that randomized BP-target evidence does not license interpreting an observational MAP association as a pressor benefit or harm [K3]. An automatic verifier can check source hashes, exact joins, time-window separation, EOL leakage guard, feature construction, split integrity, nuisance fitting without leakage, held-out metrics, uncertainty, and whether reported claims match outputs. It cannot adjudicate creatinine units/vocabulary, BP modality semantics, urine/dialysis meaning, EOL intent, residual unmeasured severity, mechanism, causal treatment effects, or clinical benefit. Those require expert review or another study.

## Actual deliverable and deferred alternatives

Completion requires newly fitted B0, B1, the residualized contrasts, the observation-process model, and M when label readiness/support permit; held-out predictions and uncertainty; the flow and label audit; common-support and fixed-nadir plots; treatment/coverage/common-density ablations; the pre-index check; and resource logs. A planned study is not a result.

The parent’s simpler B0/B1/M comparison remains the transparent baseline. A latent trajectory/state-space model is deferred because class-shape choices and perfusion/congestion/biomarker data are unavailable. A large transformer is deferred because it adds capacity without a distinct scientific question. A causal treatment model is deferred because treatment timing, dose units, clinician intent, and confounding are not adequate. The image/multimodal demonstration is not reproducible with configured eICU data. These alternatives should be revisited only if expert-adjudicated labels, validated drug units/intent, richer physiologic data, or independent external data become available.

## Three inspected key works

The parent’s attached frozen key-references.json and UTF-8 excerpts are reused unchanged; no new inspection is claimed and the three mappings remain:

- [K1] Ren Y, Liu C, Wang X, Zhang M, Li H. “Intraoperative hypotension trajectories and their predictive value for major postoperative complications: a retrospective cohort study.” Frontiers in Medicine, 2025;12:1739832. DOI: 10.3389/fmed.2025.1739832; PMID: 41613310. Full-text excerpt inspected. It supports the premise that duration/recurrence trajectories can be prognostic, but its surgical, single-cohort setting and observational adjustment do not establish eICU transportability or separation from measurement/treatment process. The new design adds explicit observation-process and common-support checks.
- [K2] Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Acute Kidney Injury Work Group. “KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury.” Kidney International Supplements, 2012;2(1):1–138. Abstract/metadata-level inspection only in the inherited evidence. It bounds the creatinine threshold language; it does not validate eICU laboratory units, vocabulary, urine semantics, or this primary label.
- [K3] Asfar P, et al. “High versus Low Blood-Pressure Target in Patients with Septic Shock.” New England Journal of Medicine, 2014;370:1583–1593. DOI: 10.1056/NEJMoa1312173; PMID: 24635770. Abstract/metadata-level inspection only in the inherited evidence. It bounds interpretation of BP-target evidence and treatment claims; it does not answer whether an observational duration summary is prognostic after process adjustment.

The attached parent support files are the authoritative frozen receipts/excerpts, including their original source URIs, retrieval timestamps, and byte hashes. Reuse them unchanged for this child; do not replace them with the new search metadata.

## Limits

The dataset lacks clinician-adjudicated AKI, reliable pre-ICU kidney function, verified laboratory units, complete fluid balance, calibrated raw BP waveforms, validated renal-replacement intent, staffing/bed context, and independent external validation. Even a positive, process-robust result remains a transportable prognostic association requiring clinical adjudication and external validation.

# MIMIC-IV renal-discordance repair: feasibility and design note

Status: repair-branch design plus bounded source availability probe. No patient cohort was built, no outcome counts were computed, no model was fitted, and no clinical conclusion is claimed.

Parent: candidate-c159494b2a5a9eb3f24ae450. This branch preserves its non-causal clinical question, ICU-discharge landmark, and 48-hour prognostic estimand while correcting the mounted source spelling and binding several fields directly to the verified schemas.

## 1. Scientific opening and claim boundary

The clinical question is whether an observed fall in serum creatinine without adequately observed urine-output recovery immediately before ICU discharge identifies a short-horizon prognostic phenotype, and whether a repeated longitudinal pattern is distinguishable from a brief low-documentation episode. The estimand remains prognostic, not causal: it is a standardized observational risk contrast at the ICU-discharge landmark, not the effect of delaying discharge, changing diuretics, or restoring urine output.

The strongest evidence inspected supports narrower claims. [K1] describes AKI definition/staging and evaluation as an evidence-based clinical assessment with creatinine and urine information but does not test this landmark phenotype. [K2] reports in a small mechanically ventilated cohort with iohexol clearance that creatinine-based eGFR can overestimate measured kidney function near ICU discharge as muscle is lost; it does not show that MIMIC discordance is prognostic. [K3] reports that dynamic kinetic-eGFR changes can aid renal-risk stratification while additional biomarkers provide modest/inconsistent incremental benefit. None establishes whether an EHR-defined creatinine/urine discordance is reproducible after urine-documentation and discharge-selection checks.

The falsifiable claim is:

> Among adults surviving a first ICU stay of at least 48 hours, and primarily among stays with dense, valid urine documentation, creatinine improvement in [t0-24 hours,t0) without recovery of measured urine output is associated with higher first 48-hour post-ICU-discharge risk of ICU readmission or in-hospital death after adjustment for measured pre-t0 severity and discharge-selection proxies; if the same pattern recurs in earlier 6-hour bins, its held-out risk contrast is larger and more stable than for a final-bin-only episode.

This would advance the question by separating three alternatives: residual illness/discharge selection, urine ascertainment/charting density, and a persistent observed longitudinal pattern. It cannot establish true GFR, complete urine collection, CKD, renal reserve, fluid balance, tubular injury, a renal mechanism, causality, treatment benefit, or transportability.

The successful managed check was job-ec3c38f9db68785f697ab709; it checked archive existence, size, member names, and streamed dictionary rows without reading patient rows. The archive SHA is carried by the configured input receipt and was not recomputed by loading the 10.55-GB object into memory.

## 3. Population, landmark, predictors, and outcomes

Select adults with patients.anchor_age >= 18 whose first ICU stay per subject_id has valid intime < outtime, los >= 2 days, and is linked to an admission. Set t0 = icustays.outtime. Retain only patients alive at t0: admissions.deathtime is null or later than t0; rows with an inconsistent death time are a readiness failure. Require t0 <= admissions.dischtime. The subject-level first-stay rule is frozen before feature construction.

The primary outcome is the first event in (t0,t0+48 hours] and before/equal to admissions.dischtime:

1. in-hospital death at admissions.deathtime; or
2. a later icustays.intime for the same subject_id,hadm_id with intime > t0.

Keep the component outcomes separate. Secondary outcomes are ICU readmission alone, death alone, a 7-day in-hospital composite, and time to the primary component. An hospital_expire_flag=1 row without a usable deathtime is not silently assigned an event time; report it as a data-quality exception and prespecify whether it is excluded from time-to-first analyses.

All predictors are strictly pre-t0. The primary feature window is [t0-24 hours,t0). Longitudinal bins are non-overlapping 6-hour bins from ICU intime through t0; a partial first bin is retained with its duration recorded. Cross-subject calendar alignment is not used because the catalog states that timestamps are subject-shifted.

Creatinine: use only labevents.itemid=50912, valuenum finite and positive, and a verified compatible valueuom (canonical mg/dL; incompatible or unitless rows are reported and excluded rather than converted silently). Require at least two observations at least six hours apart, with the final observation in the 24-hour window. Let C_peak be the maximum and C_last the final valid value in the window; define creatinine improvement as C_peak-C_last >= 0.3 mg/dL. Retain count, observation span, time since peak, and the continuous values.

Urine: use only outputevents.itemid 226559/226560/226561, value finite and nonnegative, valueuom=mL, and charttime in the relevant stay/window. Sum valid row values; do not treat absent rows as zero. Record total volume, valid-row count, source-type indicators, zero fraction, earliest/latest chart time, and an observed-span proxy. The span is documentation timing, not proof of continuous collection. The primary dense-observation cohort requires at least two valid rows in each of the four final 6-hour bins and at least one verified source type. The sensitivity ladder is: any valid row; at least two final-window rows; at least one row in each final 6-hour bin; and the strict two-rows-per-bin rule. Report the full eligible cohort separately with documentation variables. Use <400 mL/24h as the unweighted low-output threshold; no weight-indexed claim is made.

Define four descriptive final-window groups: improved/high-output, improved/low-output (the discordant group), not-improved/high-output, and not-improved/low-output. These groups are not diagnoses.

Verified pre-t0 severity/selection proxies are age, gender, admission type, ICU LOS, admission-to-t0 duration, first/last ICU care unit, transfer-event context, creatinine level/trajectory and observation intensity, urine documentation variables, MAP item 220052 with last and preceding 6-hour summaries, vasopressor exposure from the four resolved input items, and invasive ventilation from item 225792. Support exposure uses starttime,endtime,statusdescription; ventilation uses procedure starttime,endtime,statusdescription.

Lactate/platelet item IDs in chartevents and renal-replacement-therapy item IDs were not resolved by this bounded probe. They are not primary predictors. If a future readiness manifest resolves them, they may be added only in a declared sensitivity model using their actual table and item dictionary rows; otherwise they remain deferred. In particular, labevents/d_labitems must be used for lab items, not an assumed chartevents binding.

## 4. Baseline and substantive learned alternative

The scientific deliverable is newly fitted, held-out evidence for whether the discordance and its persistence add information beyond measured severity and ascertainment—not a completed prediction leaderboard.

### Transparent baseline B0/B1

B0 is penalized logistic regression for the primary 48-hour composite with exact verified inputs: age, gender, admission type, ICU LOS, admission-to-t0 duration, first/last care unit, C_peak, C_last, continuous creatinine change, creatinine observation count/span/time-since-peak, 24-hour urine volume and low-output indicator, urine row count/observed-span/source indicators/zero fraction, MAP summaries and measurement indicators, vasopressor/ventilation indicators and duration/last-active status, and all corresponding missingness indicators.

B1 adds the four-level final-window group while retaining the continuous component measurements. The B1-versus-B0 contrast tests whether the clinically stated discordance grouping contains information beyond its raw ingredients and measured observation intensity. Do not select a model based only on AUROC: report held-out standardized group risks, risk difference and risk ratio, Brier score, log loss, AUROC/AUPRC as descriptive discrimination, calibration slope/intercept, and calibration plots.

Use a fixed patient-level 70/15/15 train/tune/test split, created once before fitting and reused by both methods. Fit preprocessing on train only, select the logistic penalty on tune only, and do not inspect test outcomes for feature or threshold changes. Use 200 patient-level bootstrap resamples of held-out predictions for uncertainty; report the number of test patients and events and avoid treating an interval crossing zero as proof of no association.

### Masked longitudinal HMM alternative

The substantive alternative is a three-state masked HMM over the 6-hour bins from ICU admission to t0. It uses the same channels as B0: creatinine level/change, urine volume, urine row count/source indicators/zero fraction/observed-span, MAP, support indicators, and explicit observation masks. Missing urine bins are missing emissions, not zero urine. The model is fitted on training subjects only; regularization/emission variance settings are selected on tune, and the test set remains untouched.

The scientific outputs are posterior state probability per bin, occupancy, transition count and timing, time since transition, posterior probability that final-window discordance persists across at least two earlier bins, and held-out outcome risk conditional on these summaries. State labels are assigned after fitting by their observed emission patterns and are not called biological renal states.

The discriminating comparison is repeated discordance versus final-window-only discordance, matched as closely as feasible on final-window observed discordance and B0 risk. A charting-noise explanation predicts concentration in low-density bins, low posterior persistence, unstable state assignments, and attenuation after documentation/support adjustment. A persistent observed-physiology explanation predicts reproducible persistence and a held-out risk contrast after those checks. Neither establishes renal mechanism.

Do not fit or interpret the HMM if the test set has fewer than 200 patients or 30 primary events, if observation masks cannot be represented without imputation, or if convergence/state separation fails. A pre-specified inconclusive rule is median maximum posterior state probability below 0.60, any fitted state occupying less than 5% of training bins, or failure of label-matched state summaries to remain directionally stable in at least 80% of bootstrap refits. These are feasibility criteria, not evidence for either rival.

A deterministic filtration/fluid-balance model was considered and deferred: the bound data lack measured GFR, reliable body weight for this design, fluid composition, complete diuretic exposure, and a validated creatinine-generation parameter. A transformer/LSTM was also deferred because its extra capacity would not yield a more direct observable for the repeated-versus-transient question; this is a scientific selection decision, not a blanket rejection of neural networks or GPUs. The HMM is retained because persistence, transition timing, and observation masking are directly interpretable outputs.

Approximate future solver envelope: CPU 8 cores, 64 GB RAM, and up to 4 hours for streaming extraction, fitting, bootstrap prediction, and diagnostics; the campaign planning envelope allows up to 16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB memory, and 28,800 seconds. These are planning estimates, not measured full-study timings. The bounded dictionary probe used 2 CPUs/8 GB and completed in 0.55 seconds, but it did not scan patient rows. Logistic regression and a small HMM should run on CPU; no GPU is required. If extraction or HMM fitting exceeds the CPU/time envelope, retain the complete B0/B1 analysis and defer the HMM rather than change the scientific estimand.

## 5. Falsification, interpretation, and next decisions

Supportive evidence requires all of the following: the dense-cohort discordant contrast is directionally stable and calibrated in held-out data after measured severity/support adjustment; the full-cohort result does not depend entirely on absent urine rows; repeated discordance has reproducible posterior persistence and a held-out risk contrast beyond final-window discordance at comparable B0 risk; and the direction is not destroyed by the pre-specified coverage, support, ICU-care-unit, RRT-available, and pseudo-landmark checks. This supports an observable prognostic phenotype and justifies external validation or adjudicated urine completeness. It does not justify changing discharge practice or claiming a renal mechanism.

Adverse evidence is attenuation to the null or reversal after documentation-density adjustment, concentration in sparse urine or heavily supported stays, disappearance in the no-support restriction, a permutation contrast comparable to the observed contrast, or an HMM pattern dominated by isolated low-density transitions. This supports ascertainment, residual severity, or discharge-selection explanations and should stop this direction unless a better measurement source is obtained.

Inconclusive evidence includes missing archive members, hash/schema mismatch, absent or duplicate dictionary labels, incompatible units, invalid time order, unresolved outcome timestamps, fewer than 30 test events, wide imprecision, calibration failure, unstable HMM states, or a dense cohort too small to distinguish patterns. Report the exact failure and do not convert it to a favorable subgroup or a null conclusion.

Falsification/robustness outputs are frozen before outcome review: discordance permutation within ICU-LOS/admission/B0-risk strata; 12-hour versus 48-hour follow-up; continuous creatinine change; final-window documentation ladder; measurement-density and care-unit strata; no-support restriction; optional RRT exclusion only after item resolution; creatinine-only and urine-only models; discordance interaction; and a pseudo-landmark 24 hours before t0 using only data before that pseudo-landmark. The pseudo-landmark is a timing diagnostic, not a second primary analysis.

Computationally checkable claims are archive/member/schema/item availability, cohort construction, leakage-free split, model fitting, held-out metrics, bootstrap uncertainty, persistence summaries, and whether conclusions match those outputs. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for complete urine collection, true filtration/GFR, CKD/renal reserve, mechanism, causal interpretation, clinical utility, and external transportability. The next decision is continue to external/adjudicated validation only after supportive held-out results; revise data measurement if results track documentation; defer if feasibility is inconclusive; abandon the direction if the dense and support-restricted phenotype is absent and no better measurement source is available.

## 6. Inspected works and attached evidence

The three distinct works are attached as UTF-8 abstract excerpts and indexed in key-references.json. No full text or supplement is claimed:

- [K1] Kellum JA, Lameire N, KDIGO AKI Guideline Work Group. Diagnosis, evaluation, and management of acute kidney injury: a KDIGO summary (Part 1). Critical Care, 2013. PMID 23394211, DOI 10.1186/cc11454. Supports the complementary assessment premise; it does not test this phenotype.
- [K2] Haines RW et al. Comparison of Cystatin C and Creatinine in the Assessment of Measured Kidney Function during Critical Illness. CJASN, 2023. PMID 37256861, DOI 10.2215/CJN.0000000000000203. Bounds interpretation of creatinine near ICU discharge; it does not test MIMIC ascertainment or prognosis.
- [K3] Neumann C et al. Predictive performance of kinetic eGFR, midregional proadrenomedullin, and H3.1 nucleosomes for acute kidney disease in sepsis: a secondary analysis of a large multicentre randomized controlled trial. Journal of Intensive Care, 2026. PMID 42618952, DOI 10.1186/s40560-026-00926-y. Supports dynamic risk assessment but also limits claims of incremental biomarker value.

Attached evidence files are work/generation-renals/key-references.json, K1_kellum_kdigo_abstract_excerpt.txt, K2_haines_clearance_abstract_excerpt.txt, K3_neumann_kinetic_egfr_abstract_excerpt.txt, and source-check.json. Their hashes and receipt timestamps are recorded in the JSON/probe output.

## 7. Completion criteria and unavailable evidence

The future study is complete only when it produces: a frozen item/label/unit manifest; archive/member/schema checks; cohort/exclusion flow; observation-density ladder; outcome table; fixed split; B0/B1 fits and held-out predictions; calibrated standardized contrasts with bootstrap intervals; HMM emissions/transitions/masks/persistence and fit diagnostics if its gate passes; every falsification result; and an interpretation table mapping each conclusion to a computed output.

Unavailable or inadequate evidence includes complete urine collection, body weight suitable for a validated indexed urine threshold, fluid composition, complete diuretic exposure, baseline CKD/renal reserve, measured GFR/cystatin C in the bound cohort, discharge rationale, clinical adjudication of true renal recovery, and external validation. These limitations prevent stronger clinical or mechanistic claims but do not prevent the bounded observational question above.

# Episode 5 child: scalar hypotension summaries versus temporal recovery trajectories

Status: proposed substantive child of `candidate-614b41a73600883413318c65`. The schema/binding audit is complete; the full creatinine vocabulary/scale audit is a readiness diagnostic, not a cohort result. No clinical event rate or model performance is claimed.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The selected parent asks whether cumulative systemic MAP time below 65 mmHg in ICU minutes 0–360 has reproducible prognostic information for a later creatinine rise beyond nadir and recorded process/treatment variables. The remaining decisive uncertainty is whether that question can be computed with a reproducible creatinine label and whether a scalar burden really captures the clinically relevant temporal pattern.

The strongest inspected evidence supports that hypotension duration/trajectory summaries can be prognostic in a different, surgical cohort [K1]; abstract evidence shows that KDIGO-criteria AKI can disagree substantially with clinical coding and depends on baseline/measurement choices [K2]; and randomized BP-target evidence does not turn an observational association into a pressor benefit or harm [K3]. None establishes an eICU creatinine scale, an eICU transportable signal, a mechanism, or a treatment effect.

The falsifiable estimands are deliberately noncausal:

1. Within first adult eICU stays with common support, does early MAP<65 duration add held-out prognostic information beyond early severity, BP ascertainment, baseline creatinine, and MAP nadir?
2. Conditional on that same information and scalar duration/nadir, does the ordering of low MAP, recovery, oscillation, and observation/treatment coupling add transportable prognostic information for a subsequent creatinine event?

The clinical advance would be to determine whether a compact duration summary is transportable enough to justify external validation, or whether prognosis depends on temporal recovery patterns that a scalar duration loses. Either a robust null or an artifact-dominated result would prevent a misleading duration-based interpretation. These are prognostic/descriptive claims, not evidence that hypotension causes renal injury or that raising MAP improves outcomes.

## Label-readiness gate (must precede fitting)

Use the catalog-verified eICU 2.0 snapshot `896e1fb70d4e2d1a59c9fd87c64735dcfaff476e89543643c08b7df637a15ec` and catalog SHA-256 `802870bc57f60a7adfb12f5a59267b7cba5e1d61896adb7c6b74a58a1219f14e`. The exact source directory is:

`[private-path]/EICU 2.0数据/`

Source files are read-only; derived files stay in this branch.

The primary outcome is a creatinine-only, not full KDIGO, event:

- From `lab.csv.gz`, table `lab`, use `patientunitstayid`, `labresultoffset`, `labname`, `labresult`, `labresulttext`, `labmeasurenamesystem`, `labmeasurenameinterface`, and `labresultrevisedoffset`.
- Freeze a case-insensitive, whitespace-normalized serum-creatinine vocabulary using all three name fields. The vocabulary must exclude BUN/urea and non-serum variants; map aliases only by an auditable, versioned rule table. Use numeric `labresult` only; never parse `labresulttext`, use `apacheApsVar.creatinine` as a time-aligned result, or infer units.
- Deduplicate records at the same `patientunitstayid, labresultoffset, vocabulary member` by greatest `labresultrevisedoffset`, with a deterministic tie break. The baseline is the last valid result in ICU offset -24 through 0.
- Define the event as the first valid result in offsets 360 through 2880 at least 0.3 mg/dL above that baseline. A 1.5-times-baseline/7-day rule is a separate sensitivity, never a replacement or claim of full KDIGO.
- If the audit finds mixed/unstable vocabulary, nonnumeric eligible results, or evidence that the numeric scale cannot be made consistent without a missing units field, stop the primary event model and do not fit the GRU.

Observed readiness diagnostic (job job-b90ed2f79ccdb25af985cbf1, output label-audit-full.json, SHA-256 7ae46f58a71f6596b6633b0d3e0a2028913a164839eb651399af44bcfa4f7e14; exact-creatinine audit output creatinine-audit.json, SHA-256 b93ec8e03c0d03e6ba07763b18fbe40f4df21e1ab53f395d7374d4c7281ca8ca): the full scan found 1,277,760 rows with exact labname=creatinine; 1,275,796 had numeric labresult and normalized system/interface measures mg/dL, 1,962 had blank numeric results, and 2 had blank interface measures and blank numeric results. It also found distinct urinary creatinine, BUN, and 24-hour urine urea nitrogen names. Therefore the computational gate passes for the narrow rule exact labname=creatinine, normalized labmeasurenamesystem=mg/dL, normalized labmeasurenameinterface=mg/dL, numeric labresult; it excludes all other names, blank/non-numeric results, and any non-mg/dL system measure. This does not verify that the source measure labels are clinically reliable units or establish a KDIGO diagnosis; laboratory/nephrology review remains required. Report the exact failing fields and the minimum required expert resolution: laboratory medicine/nephrology adjudication of aliases, units/scale, and whether each candidate analyte is serum creatinine; if adjudication cannot resolve it, obtain a source with an explicit unit/analyte dictionary or use a different, explicitly narrower outcome.

Required ascertainment and censoring checks use the same frozen vocabulary but no rise requirement. Follow-up is divided into 360–720, 720–1440, and 1440–2880 minutes. A first qualifying creatinine is the event; death before event is a competing endpoint when `patient.unitdischargestatus` and `unitdischargeoffset` support it; discharge/transfer without the required observation is right-censoring, not a negative. A stay must be alive/in ICU through 360, have a valid baseline and prespecified minimum follow-up/endpoint evidence. Apache APS fields `creatinine`, `dialysis`, and `urine` have no time field and are baseline/readiness sensitivities only. `intakeOutput` fields `intakeoutputoffset`, `outputtotal`, `dialysistotal`, `nettotal`, `intakeoutputentryoffset`, `cellpath`, `celllabel`, `cellvaluenumeric`, and `cellvaluetext` cannot be called urine or dialysis events without label/unit/timing adjudication.

## Exact data binding and population

Use only these catalog sources and ordinary CSV archive members (there are no additional archive members):

| table | source file and SHA-256 | required columns / time | join |
|---|---|---|---|
| `patient` | `patient.csv.gz`, `2acf25f75144c5fc8a2a5b68c6741edac2dc7ca51021127f73e12f7428dc392b` | `patientunitstayid`, `uniquepid`, `patienthealthsystemstayid`, age, gender, ethnicity, hospitalid, unitadmittime24, unitvisitnumber, unitstaytype, unitdischargeoffset, unitdischargestatus | first-stay selection, index, censoring |
| `vitalPeriodic` | `vitalPeriodic.csv.gz`, `329b522f97f7d3d0cb4541e4fc4afc32048eb8fd0f8c9b156907f845a992906c` | `patientunitstayid`, `observationoffset`, `systemicmean`, heart rate, respiration | primary BP sequence |
| `vitalAperiodic` | `vitalAperiodic.csv.gz`, `8b23e5a50f8aabc6cb62fc69e2dcdf755a2e5649b1439a7ca413a7c5b2d5a9a0` | `patientunitstayid`, `observationoffset`, `noninvasivemean` | fallback BP modality |
| `lab` | `lab.csv.gz`, `91b55ed330015d31c424499cdae3b68e3b4cfe0c10e542548b5461520d93bc7a` | `patientunitstayid`, `labresultoffset`, name fields, numeric result, revision offset | label/ascertainment |
| `infusionDrug` | `infusionDrug.csv.gz`, `f1c958b92a676b932626638f52d0cd5bb13fa53bf5a0ec25606ff4beefc9fc3b` | `patientunitstayid`, `infusionoffset`, `drugname`, drugrate, infusionrate, drugamount, volumeoffluid, patientweight | conservative treatment/process proxy |
| `hospital` | `hospital.csv.gz`, `16684f45680921fb263fdd057ac9217093a9e81fc663228480e0d6a4665390a6` | hospitalid, numbedscategory, teachingstatus, region | hospital grouping/context |
| `apacheApsVar` | `apacheApsVar.csv.gz`, `4dfa6d3d36c3f9a1853027e0ca84668cd6dd4dfae24c330e0ceae324cbfc41b4` | patientunitstayid, admission creatinine/dialysis/urine/meanbp; no time | baseline sensitivity only |
| `carePlanEOL` | `carePlanEOL.csv.gz`, `8c776d15fd944507c0b57e3e7974db03ad87ac435d27b3f406b3d1afd046ecb0` | patientunitstayid, cpleolsaveoffset, cpleoldiscussionoffset, activeupondischarge | index process markers only if offset <=360 |
| `intakeOutput` | `intakeOutput.csv.gz`, `f809b425ea89b25c735fa8a7486e204717a3bb4d5f256af0170318ce9baa5121` | offsets, output/dialysis totals, cell label/value fields | descriptive/adjudication sensitivity only |

The source schemas were inspected from the complete eICU catalog and table JSONs: `lab` has no units column; `vitalPeriodic` contains `systemicmean` and a distinct pulmonary-artery `pamean`; `vitalAperiodic` contains `noninvasivemean`; `infusionDrug` has an offset but no explicit stop time or verified unit/indication; and `carePlanEOL` has offset fields but `activeupondischarge` is an end-of-stay field. Use `systemicmean`, never `pamean`, and join tables only on `patientunitstayid`.

Select one ICU stay per `uniquepid`: lowest `unitvisitnumber), then earliest `unitadmittime24`. Include age >=18, preserve >89 as a category, and keep each `hospitalid` intact for splitting. Index is ICU admission because there is no unit-admit offset. Require at least 12 valid 5-minute BP bins and at least 240 minutes between first and last covered bin in 0–360. Report a flow table with every exclusion.

## Exposure representations

Create 72 fixed bins `[5k,5(k+1))), k=0,...,71. Within a bin, use the median valid `systemicmean`; if no valid systemic value exists, use the median valid `noninvasivemean` and mark modality=noninvasive. Do not interpolate across gaps >10 minutes or turn missingness into normal physiology. Retain value mask, modality, time since last observation, covered-bin count, median gap, and early BP missingness. Exposure summaries are covered minutes with MAP<65 (primary), low-time fraction, area below 65, episode count, first-low offset, recovery slope, and nadir; use 60/70 thresholds and 30–180 minutes only as frozen sensitivities.

## Matched scalar baseline versus temporal alternative

All models target the same three-interval competing-risk prediction task and use identical hospital splits, censoring weights, and feature normalization rules. The baseline comparison is:

- **B0 (severity/process baseline):** regularized discrete-time cause-specific regression with age, gender, ethnicity, hospital/ICU type, baseline creatinine, admission APS meanbp/creatinine where available, initial MAP/heart rate/respiration, pre-index creatinine/BP counts, BP coverage/missingness/modality/gaps, and prespecified <=360-minute EOL/process markers. It contains no early MAP duration, nadir, or trajectory shape.
- **B1 (scalar estimand model):** B0 plus covered minutes MAP<65, low-time fraction, area, episode count, first-low offset, recovery slope, and restricted spline of duration, with fixed-nadir bands and common-support restrictions. The primary contrast B1-B0 estimates incremental prognostic value of the early duration/nadir summary, not a causal effect.
- **M (temporal alternative):** a one-layer GRU with hidden width 32 and dropout 0.1, with one sigmoid/softmax head for the same three follow-up intervals. It receives the same 72-bin sequence of MAP, heart rate, respiration, modality, observation mask, time-since-last-observation, and early recorded-pressor indicators only in a treatment-inclusive ablation; the primary M masks treatment inputs. It receives B0 baseline covariates through the head. It is trained only in training hospitals, early-stopped/calibrated in validation hospitals, and evaluated once in held-out hospitals.

M is scientifically substantive because two stays can have the same duration and nadir but differ in repeated isolated lows versus one persistent episode, order of recovery, oscillation, and whether a low precedes renewed observation. B1 discards that order; M can test whether the distinction changes later risk after matching scalar burden. To prevent a small predictive gain from becoming the scientific claim, report an order-destroying sensitivity that permutes complete observed bin tuples (value, mask, modality, time-since-last-observation, treatment proxy) within each stay while retaining the scalar summaries. If original and permuted M perform similarly, any gain is not evidence for temporal ordering.

Training target: discrete-time three-state prediction for each interval (creatinine event, death/competing endpoint, no event), with inverse-probability-of-censoring/observation weights fitted in training hospitals only. Fit B0, B1, and M with the same weighted proper loss; use the same risk-set definition. M is not fit if the label gate or minimum event/hospital-support criteria fail.

Use deterministic whole-hospital splits: hash `episode5|hospitalid` with SHA-256, assign sorted hashes 60% train, 20% validation, 20% test; every `uniquepid` and all its stays remain in one split. If the prespecified minimum hospital/event counts make one split infeasible, use five-fold grouped-hospital cross-validation with one untouched fold for final evaluation and report that deviation before viewing test performance. Fit scalers, vocabulary, model selection, calibration, nuisance models, and censoring/observation weights on training data only.

Primary uncertainty and scores: hospital-cluster bootstrap (at least 1,000 resamples) of held-out differences in Brier score and log loss at 720, 1440, and 2880 minutes, calibration intercept/slope, calibration curves, and cumulative-incidence risk curves. AUROC/AUPRC are secondary. Report hospital, stay, event, competing-event, censoring, and label-readiness counts. No threshold is selected from test results.

## Process/treatment rivals and falsification

Fit a separate observation-process model for any valid post-360 creatinine measurement and time to first measurement, using the same frozen vocabulary without the rise requirement. Strong duration-to-testing association is evidence compatible with ascertainment/clinical-concern coupling; it is not proof of bias. Apply observation weights only when their positivity/support diagnostics pass.

Use a pre-index negative-control event: among stays with valid creatinine in -48 to -24 and a distinct result in -24 to 0, apply the same +0.3 rule before the exposure window. A comparable or stronger association is adverse evidence for baseline severity/measurement process, not causal proof. Use common-support strata fixed before test evaluation: nadir band, covered count, baseline creatinine band, initial vitals, BP modality/missingness, and S/O/T propensity overlap. Refit all nuisance models in each training fold; never residualize or select strata with test information.

The infusion table supports only conservative recorded-pressor indicators/timing and possibly raw-field summaries after a name/field audit; it has no verified stop time, dose unit, or treatment indication. Compare treatment-masked primary models with treatment-inclusive ablations. Loss after treatment inclusion is compatible with treatment-response/recorded-severity coupling; persistence does not identify a causal effect.

Use `carePlanEOL.cpleolsaveoffset` and `cpleoldiscussionoffset` only when <=360 for index predictors. Never use post-index EOL rows or `activeupondischarge` as predictors; post-index EOL may be descriptive censoring context only. A broken-linkage negative control may permute complete early BP trajectories within hospital x nadir band x coverage stratum while keeping outcomes/B0 fixed; the incremental temporal signal should disappear.

## Falsification and interpretation

Supportive scalar result: label gate passes; B1 improves held-out Brier/log loss over B0 with hospital-cluster uncertainty excluding no improvement; duration-risk is coherent within fixed-nadir/common-support strata; the gain survives density thinning, modality and threshold sensitivities, process weighting, and hospital holdout; and no comparable pre-index negative-control association is present. This supports an independently useful prognostic scalar summary only.

Supportive trajectory result: M improves the same held-out scores over B1, is calibrated across hospitals, and original-versus-order-permuted M shows a prespecified loss of temporal information. This supports useful ordering/recovery information beyond duration/nadir. If M adds no stable information while B1 is stable, the scalar summary is adequate for this question. If M adds information but B1 does not, the duration estimand is insufficient and the next study should focus on trajectory descriptors. Neither outcome establishes renal hypoperfusion, causality, a MAP target, or treatment benefit.

Adverse result: label readiness fails; B1's gain is matched by the observation-process model or pre-index control; gain disappears after observation weighting, density thinning, common-support restriction, hospital holdout, or recorded-treatment adjustment; M learns only masks/treatment; or original and order-permuted M are equivalent. These favor ascertainment, selection, treatment-response, severity, or non-temporal explanations.

Inconclusive result: missing units leave scale unresolved, eligible events are too few, hospital support is inadequate, censoring/observation positivity fails, intervals are wide, or model rankings reverse across prespecified splits. Do not call an imprecise null a refutation. Obtain clinical laboratory/nephrology adjudication, validated treatment and urine/dialysis semantics, and independent external data before stronger claims.

The verifier can check snapshot/source hashes, joins, exact windows, first-stay selection, binning, no future EOL leakage, split integrity, training-only preprocessing, held-out predictions, uncertainty, and conclusion-to-output linkage. It cannot adjudicate laboratory units/analyte identity, BP modality validity, clinical intent, residual unmeasured severity, mechanism, or causal benefit. Those require expert review or another study.

## Alternatives, resource budget, and deliverable

A simple scalar regression is retained because it directly estimates the parent’s duration-versus-nadir question and is auditable. The GRU is retained because it can test a distinct ordering/recovery hypothesis on the exact same inputs and target, not because it is more complex. A temporal convolution of two width-3 layers with 32 channels is the preregistered implementation substitute if GRU library/runtime support fails; it receives the identical sequence and loss. A latent state-space model is deferred because perfusion/congestion/renal biomarkers and validated state labels are unavailable. A transformer is deferred because it adds capacity without a distinct scientific uncertainty. A causal vasopressor model is deferred because dose units, stops, indications, and assignment are unavailable. Revisit these choices only with validated units/intent, adjudicated labels, richer physiologic data, or external validation.

Task-specific deliverable: newly fit B0, B1, residualized/common-support contrasts, observation-process model, and M when the label/support gate passes; held-out predictions, calibration, hospital-cluster uncertainty, flow/label audit, fixed-nadir and temporal-order checks, process/treatment/negative-control outputs, and resource logs. Discovery inspected schemas and ran a bounded full streaming vocabulary/scale diagnostic; it did not fit the proposed clinical models. Future solver planning envelope is 16 CPU, up to 8 GPU, 262144 MiB, 28800 seconds. Use CPU for B0/B1; request one allocated GPU for M only if a measured bounded probe shows a material runtime benefit, and use `cuda:0` inside the allocation. This discovery run does not authorize solver training.

## Three inspected works

- [K1] Ren Y, Liu C, Wang X, Zhang M, Li H. “Intraoperative hypotension trajectories and their predictive value for major postoperative complications: a retrospective cohort study.” Frontiers in Medicine 2025;12:1739832. DOI 10.3389/fmed.2025.1739832; PMID 41613310. Full-text excerpt inspected. It supports the trajectory/duration premise but does not establish eICU transportability or separation from observation/treatment artifacts.
- [K2] Chanda AK, Talebianaraki E, Mahzoon V, Vucetic Z, Vucetic S. “Concordance Analysis Between KDIGO Definition of Acute Kidney Injury and Its Coding in Clinical Practice.” Kidney Medicine 2026;8(7):101374. Abstract-only inspection. It supports the label/ascertainment caution; it does not validate eICU units, vocabulary, or urine/dialysis semantics.
- [K3] Yoshimoto H, Fukui S, Higashio K, Endo A, Takasu A, Yamakawa K. “Optimal target blood pressure in critically ill adult patients with vasodilatory shock: A systematic review and meta-analysis.” Frontiers in Physiology 2022;13:962670. DOI 10.3389/fphys.2022.962670; PMID 36051909. Abstract-only inspection. It bounds treatment-target interpretation but does not answer the prognostic comparison.

The three attached UTF-8 evidence packets are local excerpts/provider responses with their inspection limits recorded in key-references.json; no unavailable full text or supplementary method is claimed. The saved child attaches key-references.json, all three evidence packets, and the branch audit outputs.

# Context-specific MerTK target prioritization in rheumatoid-arthritis synovial coculture

Status: Lead design, planned experiment; no scientific screening result has been executed. Episode 1, crossover of D2-T1 and D2-T2.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The available evidence supports two facts but leaves an actionable boundary unresolved. MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with remission and can induce a fibroblast repair response; the inspected source also reports that MerTK inhibition increases FLS IL6 and MMP1/3/14 [K1]. Separately, HBEGF-positive macrophages can drive an invasive FLS program [K2], and fibroblast pathology is heterogeneous across immune-interacting and vascular-interacting states [K3]. These findings do not establish that MerTK perturbation has the same consequence in every macrophage context, nor that a MerTK-directed intervention should be selected without stratifying protective versus inflammatory macrophage states.

Falsifiable hypothesis: in rheumatoid-arthritis synovial FLS coculture, MerTK inhibition produces a larger inflammatory FLS response when the macrophage context is MerTK/CD206-positive (resolution-like) than when it is MerTK/CD206-negative, after accounting for contributing FLS/macrophage donors and generic LPS stimulation. The clinically consequential extension is that a MerTK-preservation or activation strategy should be considered state-stratified: patients or cocultures enriched for the MerTK-positive/CD206-positive resolution context should show the greatest avoidable fibroblast harm from MerTK loss. This is a hypothesis about a perturbation-by-context interaction, not a claim that MerTK activation is already an effective treatment.

The strongest available claim is a broad protective association/perturbational effect, not clinical efficacy or direct target causality. The strongest rival is that the observed FLS changes are generic inflammatory or stress responses, cell-composition/sorting proxies, donor/reuse artifacts, or assay timing effects; under that rival, inhibitor effects should not show a reproducible CD206-context interaction after donor-aware adjustment. [K2] makes the macrophage-state alternative consequential, while [K3] motivates separating FLS state readouts from mere bulk expression changes. The proposed advance over [K1] is a state-by-perturbation safety/selection test, not another broad MerTK expression association.

## Population, boundaries, and exact data bindings

Primary population: all 33 recorded pseudobulk FLS samples in the prepared E-MTAB-8873 matrix, restricted to samples whose design row has cell_type=type B synovial cell, tissue=synovial membrane, and a documented co-culture condition. Primary contrasts are macrophages pre-treated with MerTK inhibitor versus no treatment within condition=co-cultured with MerTK/CD206pos macrophages and, as the context comparator, the corresponding CD206neg condition. No raw cell is treated as an independent donor.

Required primary inputs and keys:

- [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz (catalog SHA-256 d218d3c46b652d533673c9ffc7876585bc51a39371f036e92d3ce568f28a4c0f): table with feature row key and 33 sample-ID columns. Verified measured feature columns include MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end, MRC1|NM_002438.3|Reference_end, TREM2|NM_018965.3|Reference_end, SPP1|NM_000582.2|Reference_end, IL1B|NM_000576.2|Reference_end, IL6|NM_000600.4|Reference_end, MMP1|NM_002421.3|Reference_end, MMP3|NM_002422.4|Reference_end, MMP12|NM_002426.5|Reference_end, MMP13|NM_002427.3|Reference_end, and MMP14|NM_004995.3|Reference_end.
- [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.design.json (SHA-256 fd2ae05bd0e31a8ba72454b97e22a48f5e53c179370e5f4b5343f5382b217ae4): one row per matrix column with required fields sample_id, donor_id, donor_status, age, sex, tissue, cell_type, condition, treatment, source_metadata, and cells. Join design.sample_id to the matrix header exactly. Parse the comma-separated contributing IDs in donor_id as separate FLS/macrophage random-effect memberships; do not silently repair the malformed/ambiguous R1_SA256A_FLS_SA260R_Mpos label.
- [private-path]/assay-registry.json (SHA-256 e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f): registry table documenting 33 samples, 445 measured features, no verified single donors, and the explicit prohibition on ordinary donor t-tests.
- Audit lineage/source members, read-only and not treated as independent replicates: E-MTAB-8873/E-MTAB-8873.sdrf.txt (SHA-256 4e564426bb68e05d93e997a9124d42f252a19680abfe54315676893ae479f719) plus the registered R1/R2/R5 R*_SA*_..._RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz members listed in datasets/therapeutic_targets/metadata.json; inhibitor members include R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor, R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor, R1_SA256A_FLS_SA260R_Mpos_Inhibitor, R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos_preInhibitor, and R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos_preInhibitor. The prepared pseudobulk table is the analysis table; individual cells are not additional independent observations.

The primary design has five inhibitor-treated samples (one CD206neg and four CD206pos) and 23 untreated samples, plus LPS-treated context controls and six FLS-only samples. This sparsity is itself a falsification/deferral condition: a state interaction can be estimated only as exploratory with uncertainty and donor-cluster sensitivity, not as a definitive clinical effect.

Secondary context inputs, never joined by matching patient IDs:

- E-MTAB-8316 prepared matrix [private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.counts.tsv.gz (SHA-256 9ceb4b7cf3d52d7f6e3800c827d491b174b646826fae9c6d1433c5d64b219645) and design [private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.design.json (SHA-256 ca011580853bbea30b4f68f21bb5b017721c3e47bfefee6e9083b44da04c4c81). Its 12 columns are MK11/MK12, MK15/MK16, MK19/MK20, MK23/MK24, MK3/MK4 and MK7/MK8: six verified within-other_donor_id none versus UNC106238 pairs nested in four verified donor IDs (SA114, SA051, SA104, SA049). Use only as a paired exploratory perturbation/state check after reconciling its monocyte labels and protocol readout; do not claim twelve independent donors or FLS-specific effects. No time field is present.
- E-MTAB-8322 prepared matrix [private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz (SHA-256 95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36) and design [private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.design.json (SHA-256 4ef38a7031542ec07551d585e9a2218f2620320018b3d56a86bde5a0b672a3da). It has 27 macrophage pseudobulk columns across healthy (4), treatment-naive RA (6), remission (7), resistant RA (6), and undifferentiated arthritis (4); exclude SA149P and UPASA149 from independent-donor inference. Its matrix uses Ensembl feature IDs and no configured feature-map file, so target-module/state scoring is blocked pending a named, frozen human annotation release. Use design-state metadata descriptively and do not call cross-sectional groups transitions.
- GSE95588 prepared coculture matrices and designs are available, but donor-to-GSM mapping is unresolved and the coculture branch includes earlier GSE57723 material. It is retained as an exploratory/rival context only; no donor-aware inferential claim or independent validation will use it.

There are no longitudinal time fields or patient treatment transitions in these molecular tables. treatment, condition, and source metadata are assay conditions, not clinical time. No source namespace is joined across assays.

## Computable Harbor experiment

1. Freeze the eligible E-MTAB-8873 rows and an analysis manifest recording the exact filtering above, sample IDs, donor memberships, and all excluded/ambiguous rows. Normalize each sample's measured feature counts to log2(CPM + pseudocount), using the matrix's feature and sample columns; do not merge duplicate identifiers or infer absent genes.
2. Prespecify two outcomes. The primary harm score is the mean of z-scored IL6, MMP1, MMP3 and MMP14 across measured features; secondary harm components are IL1B, MMP12 and MMP13. The context/state panel is MERTK, MRC1, TREM2 and SPP1. If a planned repair marker is not present in the exact header, it is unavailable rather than imputed.
3. Fit the simple baseline: feature-wise and harm-score linear models with inhibitor, macrophage context (CD206pos/neg), inhibitor-by-context interaction, LPS indicator, FLS-only indicator, age, and assay batch/round when identifiable. Use cross-classified donor-cluster random intercepts or cluster-robust inference for every contributing donor; average repeated context measurements only when the documented donor/condition definition warrants it. Generate donor-cluster bootstrap intervals and leave-one-donor-cluster-out sensitivity, not ordinary donor t-tests. The estimand is the inhibitor contrast within context and their difference, on the FLS harm score.
4. Fit a substantive mechanistic alternative on exactly the same inputs: a hierarchical multivariate latent-state model in which a macrophage-resolution score is a weighted latent factor of MERTK/MRC1/TREM2 (with SPP1 and IL1B as an inflammatory contrast) and FLS harm is a latent factor of IL6/MMP1/MMP3/MMP14. Estimate the inhibitor-by-context interaction jointly with crossed FLS and macrophage donor effects, allowing feature-specific residual covariance. The model's target is not a predictive label; it is the posterior distribution of the context-specific perturbation effect and the probability that the interaction exceeds a prespecified scientifically meaningful direction. Fit by CPU using a reproducible Bayesian or penalized-likelihood implementation; no GPU is needed for this small table. If the donor design is too sparse to identify the latent model, defer it and report the baseline only.
5. Compare the baseline and mechanistic alternative on scientific information: sign and uncertainty of the same interaction estimand, leave-one-donor-cluster-out stability, posterior/cluster-bootstrap predictive checks, and whether the alternative changes interpretation by separating a correlated macrophage state from the FLS harm outcome. Do not rank by small predictive improvement. No random train/test split is appropriate for this finite hypothesis test; the held-out unit is a donor cluster. The future solver must report coefficient/effect tables, donor membership and exclusions, uncertainty intervals or posterior intervals, feature-level and score-level outputs, sensitivity analyses, and diagnostic plots/data.
6. Compute a bounded negative control: the LPS-treated versus untreated contrast within the same macrophage context where present. A selective MerTK interaction should not be reproduced identically by the LPS contrast. FLS-only samples assess whether an apparent response is present without macrophages; this is a control, not evidence of direct MerTK action.
7. Contextualize, do not pool, E-MTAB-8316 paired UNC106238 versus none at the verified donor/other-donor unit and E-MTAB-8322 condition proportions/state metadata. A consistent direction can motivate a balanced follow-up, but it cannot be called external validation because the datasets derive from the same literature program and have different biological units.

Supportive result: the inhibitor-by-context interaction is positive and materially larger in CD206pos coculture for the prespecified harm score, stable in donor-cluster sensitivity, while LPS and FLS-only controls do not reproduce it. This supports state-stratified MerTK preservation/activation as a next target-development experiment, not a clinical treatment claim.

Adverse result: no interaction, a larger CD206neg effect, the same signal under LPS, or a signal confined to FLS-only samples. This refutes the proposed selectivity claim and favors generic inflammatory/cell-composition explanations; do not prioritize MerTK state targeting on this evidence.

Inconclusive result: sparse inhibitor cells, unresolved contributing-donor mappings, nonidentifiable latent model, contradictory donor clusters, or missing annotation/feature coverage. Acquire balanced paired Mpos/Mneg cocultures with matched FLS and macrophage donors, inhibitor dose/viability data, MerTK protein/activation and efferocytosis readouts, secreted mediators, and direct FLS invasion/matrix degradation. Clinical treatment benefit, patient selection, and mechanism require expert review, orthogonal perturbation (e.g., agonism or genetic perturbation), and an independent cohort; Harbor QA can check computation and whether conclusions follow from outputs but cannot establish those claims.

## Alternative methods and selection

The pathway/paired-score baseline is transparent and appropriate to the sparse, repeated-donor table. The hierarchical multivariate latent-state alternative could reveal whether the apparent interaction is a shared macrophage-to-FLS program rather than a single-gene artifact, and it propagates uncertainty across correlated markers; that information is lost by the baseline. It is deferred as secondary because five inhibitor-treated samples and unresolved contributing-donor structure may not identify crossed latent effects. Both methods use the same exact inputs, estimand, donor-cluster held-out sensitivity and uncertainty outputs. A CPU future solver envelope of 16 CPUs/262144 MiB and 8 GPUs is available in inputs.json, but this study is small and does not justify GPU; the discovery diagnostic jobs completed in under a second, while full solver fit time is unmeasured and should be budgeted as a bounded CPU job. No neural model is required because the scientific uncertainty is mechanistic interaction/selectivity, not prediction.

## What must be newly fitted and completion deliverable

The solver must newly fit the context-by-MerTK-inhibitor effect and its uncertainty from E-MTAB-8873, fit or explicitly defer the hierarchical latent alternative, and produce the frozen analysis manifest, donor-aware effect/uncertainty tables, prespecified harm/state scores, LPS/FLS-only controls, leave-one-donor-cluster-out results, and a conclusion linked to those computed outputs. Completion is not a polished hypothesis or a readiness probe: it requires these computed outputs and an interpretation that distinguishes supportive, adverse and inconclusive cases.

## Evidence and prior-work mapping

[K1] establishes the broad MerTK-positive resolution/repair claim and the reported inhibitor FLS response; the proposed state-specific interaction and donor-aware target-selection test are new relative to that inspected work.
[K2] supplies the strongest biological rival: inflammatory macrophage state can drive fibroblast pathology independently of the proposed MerTK-selective explanation.
[K3] bounds the fibroblast outcome interpretation by showing that inflammatory FLS states are heterogeneous and niche-linked; the proposal therefore prespecifies multiple measured FLS outputs and does not treat one marker as mechanism.

Key references and attached inspected excerpts are in work/lead/key-references.json and work/lead/evidence/.

## Demonstration and seed dispositions

- D2-T1 retained: context-specific intervention response becomes the inhibitor-by-CD206 context interaction, with direct-target claims explicitly deferred.
- D2-T2 retained: benefit versus harm is operationalized as FLS inflammatory harm plus preservation of the resolution-like macrophage context.
- Natural-history transformer demonstration: not pursued as a molecular topic; its lesson is to distinguish observed structured histories from a proposed learned representation. It adds no necessary information to this small assay.
- Cancer multimodal demonstration: full text and images are unavailable and the configured molecular sources contain no imaging/longitudinal oncology outcomes; no adaptation is scientifically grounded here.

# Context-specific MerTK target prioritization in rheumatoid-arthritis synovial coculture

Status: frozen Lead design; planned experiment. No scientific screening result has been executed. The solver must compute the experiment and must not treat this instruction, a readiness probe, or a positive fixture as a result.

## Scientific question and claim boundary

Available evidence supports a broad protective/resolution association for MerTK-positive synovial macrophages and a fibroblast inflammatory response after MerTK inhibition [K1]. HBEGF-positive macrophages establish a consequential rival in which macrophage state can drive fibroblast pathology through intercellular signaling [K2]. Fibroblast pathology is heterogeneous and niche-linked, so multiple FLS readouts are needed rather than one marker [K3]. These works do not establish a MerTK-by-context interaction, a clinical treatment-selection rule, or direct target causality in the configured assay.

Falsifiable hypothesis: in rheumatoid-arthritis synovial FLS coculture, MerTK inhibition produces a larger inflammatory FLS response in the MerTK/CD206-positive, resolution-like macrophage context than in the CD206-negative context, after accounting for contributing FLS/macrophage donors and generic LPS stimulation. The proposed clinical-development implication is a state-stratified MerTK-preservation/activation follow-up, not a claim that MerTK activation is an effective treatment.

The strongest existing claim is a broad protective association/perturbational effect, not clinical efficacy or context selectivity. The leading rivals are generic LPS/inflammatory stress, cell-composition or sorting proxies, donor/reuse structure, and assay timing. A selective interaction should persist after donor-aware adjustment and should not be reproduced identically by the LPS contrast or FLS-only samples. An association in this expression assay is not a mechanism or causal clinical effect.

## Computation and estimands

1. Freeze the eligible rows, sample IDs, donor memberships, exclusions, ambiguous labels, measured features, and input hashes in analysis_manifest.json. 3. Fit the transparent baseline on the same rows/features: feature-wise and harm-score models with inhibitor, macrophage context (CD206pos/neg), inhibitor-by-context interaction, LPS indicator, FLS-only indicator, age, and identifiable assay batch/round. Use crossed FLS and macrophage donor random intercepts or cluster-robust inference for every contributing donor. Use donor-cluster bootstrap intervals and leave-one-donor-cluster-out sensitivity; ordinary donor t-tests are prohibited. The primary estimand is the inhibitor contrast within each context and their difference on the FLS harm score.
4. Fit the substantive alternative on exactly the same inputs when identifiable: a hierarchical multivariate latent-state model with a macrophage-resolution factor from MERTK/MRC1/TREM2 (SPP1 and IL1B as inflammatory contrast) and an FLS-harm factor from IL6/MMP1/MMP3/MMP14. Estimate the same inhibitor-by-context interaction jointly with crossed donor effects and feature-specific residual covariance. Report the posterior or penalized-likelihood uncertainty for the interaction and posterior/interval probability of the prespecified direction. If the donor structure is too sparse to identify it, explicitly defer it and report the baseline; do not replace it with a different estimand.
5. Compare methods by the same interaction sign and uncertainty, donor-cluster held-out stability, and posterior/cluster-bootstrap predictive checks. Explain whether the latent alternative reveals a shared macrophage-to-FLS program or changes interpretation beyond a single-gene association. Do not rank methods by small predictive improvement. A random train/test split is inappropriate; the held-out unit is a donor cluster.
6. Compute the negative control contrast of LPS-treated versus untreated within each macrophage context where present. A selective MerTK interaction should not be reproduced identically by this contrast. FLS-only samples test whether an apparent response occurs without macrophages; this is a control, not evidence of direct MerTK action.
7. Contextualize E-MTAB-8316 at its verified paired donor/other-donor unit and E-MTAB-8322 descriptively. Do not pool them with E-MTAB-8873 or call them independent validation.

## Required outputs

The solver must newly compute, not copy, the following under /workspace:

- results.json: valid JSON containing the estimand, model status, primary and secondary effect estimates, uncertainty intervals/posterior intervals, donor membership and exclusions, method comparison, controls, sensitivity summary, and one of supportive, adverse, or inconclusive conclusion labels with evidence paths.
- analysis_manifest.json: exact input target paths/hashes, filters, eligible/excluded sample IDs, feature availability, donor memberships, and any unresolved mapping.
- effects.csv: coefficient/effect rows for the primary harm score, secondary components, and context-specific contrasts, including estimates and uncertainty.
- controls.csv: LPS and FLS-only control results.
- sensitivity.csv: donor-cluster leave-one-out and uncertainty/stability results.

A result is complete only if it links every substantive conclusion to computed output rows/plots/tables and states uncertainty. Do not manufacture scientific outputs in readiness checks or fixtures.

## Interpretation and falsification

Supportive: the inhibitor-by-context interaction is positive and materially larger in CD206-positive cocultures for the prespecified harm score, stable under donor-cluster sensitivity, while LPS and FLS-only controls do not reproduce the same selective pattern. This supports a state-stratified MerTK preservation/activation follow-up, not a clinical treatment or direct-mechanism claim.

Adverse: no interaction, an interaction larger in CD206-negative cocultures, the same signal under LPS, or a signal confined to FLS-only samples. This refutes the proposed selectivity claim and favors generic inflammatory, composition, donor, or assay explanations; do not prioritize MerTK state targeting on this evidence.

Inconclusive: sparse inhibitor cells, unresolved donor mappings, nonidentifiable latent model, contradictory donor clusters, imprecise estimates, or missing annotation/feature coverage prevent a discriminating conclusion. A null with wide uncertainty is not proof of no effect.

Harbor QA may check data loading, required computations, numerical uncertainty, output linkage, and whether the conclusion follows from reported results. It cannot establish clinical benefit, direct target mechanism, viability/safety, a therapeutic window, or novelty. Those require expert review and another study with balanced paired Mpos/Mneg cocultures, matched donors, dose/viability and time-course data, MerTK protein/activation and efferocytosis, secreted mediators, FLS invasion/matrix function, orthogonal agonism or genetic perturbation, and an independent cohort.

The transparent donor-aware score/interaction baseline is primary because it is interpretable and appropriate to 33 sparse pseudobulk samples with five inhibitor-treated samples (one Mneg and four Mpos). The hierarchical multivariate alternative is scientifically substantive because it can distinguish a shared macrophage-state program from a single-gene artifact and propagate covariance uncertainty; it is secondary/deferred if crossed latent effects are not identifiable. # Donor-aware identifiability of context-selective MerTK harm in RA synovial coculture

Status: substantive child of candidate-8d4724c711ef0520a9b2f872; planned Harbor experiment only. No molecular screening or result has been executed.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The inspected evidence supports a broad claim: MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with remission/repair, and MerTK inhibition has been reported with increased FLS inflammatory transcripts [K1]. It does not establish that the perturbation is more harmful in the MerTK/CD206-positive context than in the CD206-negative context. That unresolved boundary matters for target prioritization: a MerTK-preservation or activation strategy could be selectively attractive only if loss of the resolution-like macrophage context produces a materially larger fibroblast harm program, rather than a generic response to perturbation or assay stress.

The falsifiable hypothesis is unchanged: in RA type-B synovial FLS coculture, macrophage MerTK inhibition produces a larger FLS inflammatory harm response in the MerTK/CD206-positive context than in the CD206-negative context, after accounting for contributing FLS and macrophage memberships. The clinical-research implication is a context-stratified next-step decision, not a claim of clinical efficacy or that MerTK activation is already a treatment.

The strongest rival explanations are generic LPS/stress signaling, altered cell composition or capture, donor and assay-round confounding, and timing or preparation-label artifacts. They predict either a similar effect under LPS, a signal in FLS-only samples, instability after donor-aware mapping, or no coherent marker-level interaction. [K2] makes an inflammatory macrophage-state explanation consequential; [K3] cautions that FLS inflammatory programs are heterogeneous and niche-linked. [K1] supports the starting perturbational observation, but does not identify this state-by-perturbation interaction. The substantive advance is an explicit identifiability and decision-usefulness test under the actual sparse design.

## Population and exact data bindings

The primary population is the 33 recorded pseudobulk columns in:

- [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 d218d3c46b652d533673c9ffc7876585bc51a39371f036e92d3ce568f28a4c0f. It is a feature-row table with the sample IDs in the header and 445 measured features. Required measured transcript columns are MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end, MRC1|NM_002438.3|Reference_end, TREM2|NM_018965.3|Reference_end, SPP1|NM_000582.2|Reference_end, IL1B|NM_000576.2|Reference_end, IL6|NM_000600.4|Reference_end, MMP1|NM_002421.3|Reference_end, MMP3|NM_002422.4|Reference_end, MMP12|NM_002426.5|Reference_end, MMP13|NM_002427.3|Reference_end, and MMP14|NM_004995.3|Reference_end.
- [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.design.json, SHA-256 fd2ae05bd0e31a8ba72454b97e22a48f5e53c179370e5f4b5343f5382b217ae4. It has one row per matrix column and the fields sample_id, donor_id, donor_status, age, sex, tissue, cell_type, condition, treatment, source_metadata and cells. Join only on design.sample_id = counts header sample ID. The comma-separated donor_id memberships are dependence annotations, not a single donor identifier.
- [private-path]/assay-registry.json, SHA-256 e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab1bd1a31c77b7f70f. This records 33 samples, 445 measured features, no verified single donors, and prohibits ordinary donor t-tests.
- E-MTAB-8873/E-MTAB-8873.sdrf.txt, SHA-256 4e564426bb68e05d93e997a9124d42f252a19680abfe54315676893ae479f719, plus the registered R1, R2 and R5 R*_SA*_..._RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz archive members listed in datasets/therapeutic_targets/metadata.json. Eligible rows must have tissue=synovial membrane, cell_type=type B synovial cell and a documented co-culture condition. The primary context variables are MerTK/CD206pos versus MerTK/CD206neg. The mixed rows R2_SA258R_FLS_SA267R_1Mpos_SA266A_3Mneg, R2_SA258R_FLS_SA267R_3Mpos_SA266A_1Mneg and R5_SA263R_FLS_SA278R_1Mpos_SA277A_3Mneg are context-ambiguous and are excluded from the primary interaction, retained as descriptive composition controls. The exact treated rows are R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor, R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor and R1_SA256A_FLS_SA260R_Mpos_Inhibitor. The parent’s count of five treated rows is retained, but the tiers are never silently merged: exact inhibitor is primary; preInhibitor is secondary only if protocol metadata establishes equivalence.
