- E-MTAB-8316 counts [private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 9ceb4b7cf3d52d7f6e3800c827d491b174b646826fae9c6d1433c5d64b219645, and design [private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.design.json, SHA-256 ca011580853bbea30b4f68f21bb5b017721c3e47bfefee6e9083b44da04c4c81. Its six verified within-other_donor_id none versus UNC106238 pairs are nested in four verified donors (SA114, SA051, SA104, SA049); use only as a paired exploratory state/perturbation context after reconciling labels and protocol. It has no time field.
- E-MTAB-8322 counts [private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36, and design [private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.design.json, SHA-256 4ef38a7031542ec07551d585e9a2218f2620320018b3d56a86bde5a0b672a3da. It has 27 macrophage pseudobulk columns across healthy, treatment-naive RA, remission, resistant RA and undifferentiated arthritis. Its Ensembl feature IDs lack a configured feature map, so target-module scoring is blocked pending a named frozen annotation release; use state metadata descriptively only and exclude SA149P and UPASA149 from independent-donor inference.
- GSE95588 source and prepared tables remain bound for provenance/rival context: GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.txt.gz, GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.txt.gz, series.soft, samples.soft, and their registered prepared matrices/designs/feature maps. Donor-to-GSM mapping is unresolved and the coculture branch includes earlier GSE57723 material; no donor-aware inferential claim or independent validation uses it.

## Estimand and identifiability gate

Normalize the measured feature rows per sample to log2(CPM + pseudocount), preserving transcript identifiers and without imputing unmeasured genes. Before modeling, emit a manifest with every included row, exposure tier, round, FLS membership, macrophage membership, context, cells, exclusions and mapping scenario.

The primary outcome is a prespecified FLS harm score H: the mean of feature-standardized IL6, MMP1, MMP3 and MMP14. Standardization parameters are frozen from the eligible untreated coculture reference rows; if a required feature is absent from the exact header, the score is unavailable rather than repaired. Secondary outcomes are IL1B, MMP12, MMP13 and each primary component. The context panel is MERTK, MRC1, TREM2 and SPP1; it is descriptive of the state and cannot prove direct target engagement.

The primary estimand is

  Delta = [E(H | exact inhibitor, Mpos) - E(H | untreated, Mpos)]
          - [E(H | exact inhibitor, Mneg) - E(H | untreated, Mneg)]

with donor membership treated as crossed dependence, not as independent observations. Because the prepared design contains only one exact-inhibitor Mneg row and two unambiguous exact-inhibitor Mpos rows, only the R1 SA256A/SA259A pair supplies a complete same-FLS/macrophage-pair context comparison. Therefore the interaction is not automatically identifiable as a population-level causal effect. The solver must first report a rank/overlap gate: treatment-context cells, exact matched counterpart availability, donor membership overlap, and whether Delta can be estimated without using the ambiguous row or the preInhibitor tier. A rank-deficient or overlap-failing primary model returns inconclusive, not a zero effect.

The primary baseline is a transparent paired-score/interaction analysis. Construct within-round matched differences wherever the design explicitly supports the same FLS/macrophage membership, then estimate exact-exposure context contrasts with a small fixed-effects model including context, exposure, their interaction and assay round only when estimable. Represent every contributing FLS and macrophage donor with a membership incidence matrix; use a cross-classified random-intercept or penalized fixed-effect formulation only if its rank is documented. Do not include age or sex as if independently varying when age is round-confounded and all rows are female. Report feature-level effects, H effects, donor-cluster bootstrap intervals, leave-one-round-out and leave-one-membership-out sensitivity, and exact mapping scenarios. Ordinary donor t-tests, cell-level replication and random row splits are prohibited.

The LPS rows are a bounded generic-inflammatory control: compare preLPS with untreated within context where available and ask whether the marker pattern and context contrast are reproduced. FLS-only rows test whether a response appears without macrophages. Neither control establishes MerTK specificity; both can falsify a selective interpretation. Mixed-composition rows test whether changing Mpos:Mneg mixture alone tracks H and are not used as clean context labels.

## Substantive alternative on the same inputs

The alternative is a cross-classified multivariate partial-pooling model, not a different question. On the same log-CPM outcome matrix and the same frozen manifest, model the primary and secondary FLS features jointly with feature-specific intercepts, exposure-tier effect, context effect, exposure-by-context effect, assay-round effect, and crossed FLS/macrophage membership effects. A shared latent FLS-harm factor loads on IL6, MMP1, MMP3 and MMP14; a separate macrophage-context factor uses MERTK, MRC1 and TREM2, with SPP1 and IL1B retained as an inflammatory contrast rather than forced into the resolution factor. Feature-specific residual covariance allows correlated markers to contribute uncertainty jointly.

Its fitting target is the posterior or penalized-likelihood distribution of the same Delta, the two context-specific exposure effects, the shared-harm loading coherence and the probability that Delta exceeds a material threshold. It is not trained to predict a label. Fit only after design-rank checks; if the one-Mneg treated cluster or the ambiguous memberships make the latent model non-identifiable, record the attempted model and defer it rather than replacing it with a simpler unannounced fit. Compare the alternative with the baseline by sign, interval width, donor/mapping stability and marker coherence. The information gained is whether a seemingly single-marker interaction is a correlated FLS program and whether partial pooling makes uncertainty widen or shrink appropriately; the score baseline loses that structure but is more transparent under sparsity.

The held-out unit is an assay round or donor-membership cluster for leave-one-cluster-out sensitivity. With only R1, R2 and R5 and unbalanced treatment, this is a stability diagnostic, not external validation. Use posterior predictive or residual checks for the fitted model, not predictive accuracy as the scientific criterion. The estimated future solver cost is 4–8 CPU cores, less than 16 GiB memory and minutes for this 33-by-11 feature table; full runtime is unmeasured and must be bounded in the solver job. GPU is deferred because the matrix is small and the scientific uncertainty is design/identifiability, not computational scale.

Deferred alternatives are: a neural expression predictor, because predictive improvement cannot answer whether the interaction is causal or decision-useful; a pooled analysis that merges exact inhibitor and preInhibitor, because protocol equivalence is unavailable; ordinary differential expression t-tests, because donor dependence is explicitly unresolved; E-MTAB-8322 target scoring, because the feature namespace lacks a configured map; and GSE95588 validation, because donor-to-GSM mapping is unresolved. These alternatives can be revisited only after the named missing dependency is supplied or the question changes.

## Supportive, adverse and inconclusive rule

Define a material harm threshold delta = 0.5 SD of H, fixed before fitting. A result is supportive only if the exact-exposure Delta is positive and its uncertainty supports Delta > delta (or the equivalent prespecified posterior probability is at least 0.90), the sign is unchanged across admissible donor mappings and round/membership holdouts, the primary marker components are directionally coherent, and neither LPS nor FLS-only controls reproduces the same selective pattern. This supports a balanced orthogonal follow-up to test state-stratified MerTK preservation/activation; it does not justify a clinical treatment or patient-selection claim.

A result is adverse if Delta is nonpositive or Mneg harm is at least as large, or if generic LPS/stress or FLS-only controls reproduce the apparent response. This weakens or refutes the context-selective prioritization rationale and favors generic inflammation, composition or timing explanations; do not advance the state-selective MerTK direction on this evidence.

A result is inconclusive if the rank/overlap gate fails, the mapping scenario changes the sign, uncertainty spans zero or delta, only one donor cluster drives the result, exact and preInhibitor tiers disagree without protocol resolution, or the partial-pooling alternative is non-identifiable. The next decision is to obtain balanced matched Mpos and Mneg perturbations across FLS/macrophage donor pairs, with dose, exposure time, viability, protein/phospho-MerTK, efferocytosis, secreted mediators and direct FLS invasion or matrix-degradation readouts.

Harbor can check source joins, feature selection, estimand computation, uncertainty outputs and whether the conclusion obeys these rules. It cannot establish clinical benefit, direct molecular mechanism, cell viability, spatial localization, therapeutic window or independent biological validity. Those require expert adjudication, orthogonal perturbation such as agonism or genetic loss-of-function, and an independent cohort.

## Completion deliverable and evidence boundary

The scientific deliverable is newly fitted Delta and context-specific effects with uncertainty from E-MTAB-8873, plus an explicit identifiability report, exposure-tier comparison, LPS/FLS-only controls, donor/mapping sensitivity, and a fit-or-defer record for the partial-pooling model. Completion requires effects.csv, controls.csv, sensitivity.csv, analysis_manifest.json and a results.json conclusion linked to those outputs. Readiness or a planned method is not a scientific result.

Status: substantive evolution of candidate-e2c88fac21f4420df13909b9; planned Harbor experiment only. No scientific screening result has been executed.

## Question, hypothesis and clinical importance

The inspected evidence supports three bounded claims. MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with remission biology and can induce fibroblast repair [K1]. A different inflammatory macrophage state can drive fibroblast invasiveness through tissue cross-talk [K2]. Fibroblast inflammatory programs are heterogeneous and niche-linked [K3]. None establishes the parent’s unresolved claim: that MerTK inhibition causes a larger FLS inflammatory harm response in a MerTK/CD206-positive context than in a MerTK/CD206-negative context, and that this interaction transfers to an independently verified perturbation assay.

The falsifiable hypothesis is therefore:

The clinically consequential decision is whether to prioritize state-stratified MerTK preservation/activation experiments. A supportive result justifies balanced orthogonal perturbation and functional testing; it does not establish a treatment, patient-selection rule, direct target engagement or clinical benefit. A source comparison may use only separately estimated, explicitly standardized effect summaries after compatibility checks; it may not pool rows, donors, feature IDs or raw counts.

## Estimands and identifiability gates

Normalize each source separately to log2(CPM + 1), preserving original feature IDs and never imputing absent genes.

Primary E-MTAB-8873 outcome:
`H_s` is the mean of feature-standardized IL6, MMP1, MMP3 and MMP14. Standardization parameters are frozen using eligible untreated, unambiguous co-culture reference rows. The primary estimand is

`Delta = [E(H | exact inhibitor, Mpos) - E(H | untreated, Mpos)] - [E(H | exact inhibitor, Mneg) - E(H | untreated, Mneg)]`.

The solver must emit a pre-fit gate with treatment/context cell counts, exact counterpart availability, donor-membership incidence rank, and estimability of the interaction. The gate fails if the model requires the ambiguous mixed rows, the preInhibitor tier, the metadata-conflicted untreated row, a random row split, or independent-donor assumptions. Given the verified design, only the R1 SA256A/SA259A pair supplies a complete same-membership exact-inhibitor Mpos/Mneg contrast; therefore a population-level causal interaction is not automatically identified. A failed or rank-deficient gate returns inconclusive, never a zero estimate.

The baseline is a transparent paired score/interaction analysis: calculate within-membership matched differences wherever explicitly supported, fit context, exposure and interaction with assay round only when rank permits, and represent FLS/macrophage memberships by an incidence matrix. Use cluster bootstrap or a bounded sign/permutation sensitivity over contributing membership clusters, leave-one-round-out and leave-one-membership-out analyses. Report H, each component, exact versus preInhibitor tiers, mapping scenarios, and controls. Ordinary donor t-tests and cell-level replication are prohibited.

The E-MTAB-8316 secondary estimand is source-specific:
`d_{f,m,g}=logCPM(UNC106238)_{f,m,g}-logCPM(none)_{f,m,g}`, for each of the six exact pairs, summarized within the four FLS donor clusters with monocyte donor nested dependence. It is not H, not Delta, and not an FLS outcome. A six-pair response can be reported only as exploratory paired evidence; it is not six independent donors.

The 8316 compatibility gate requires: (1) protocol/registry confirmation that UNC106238 is the intended perturbation and that the none/UNC106238 rows are paired units; (2) a named frozen Ensembl-to-gene annotation map if gene-level MERTK/MRC1/TREM2/SPP1 or inflammatory-marker claims are attempted; (3) verified correspondence of cell type and readout to the intended secondary question; and (4) no cross-source donor join. The currently inspected prepared files pass the pairing and donor-nesting checks but fail the configured feature-map requirement for gene-level target claims and do not expose an Mpos/Mneg context. The correct current plan is therefore bounded source-specific triangulation with an explicit non-pooling status, not a hierarchical cross-cohort Delta.

A shared hierarchical cross-cohort effect is scientifically identifiable only if both sources share a measured endpoint, intervention definition, context contrast, feature namespace/annotation and biological unit. They currently do not: 8873 measures targeted FLS coculture harm with transcript labels, while 8316 measures Ensembl-indexed monocyte samples under none/UNC106238 and has no context field. A model with source-specific intercepts cannot repair a missing common estimand. If a future named annotation and protocol adjudication make a common secondary signature defensible, fit source-specific effects with a hierarchical shrinkage sensitivity, never a forced pooled primary coefficient. Otherwise report non-pooling.

## Baseline versus substantive alternative

Both methods use the same source-specific normalized matrices, design fields, paired units and frozen manifests.

The baseline estimates the primary Delta transparently and the 8316 paired d contrasts without a learned prediction target. Its strength is auditable behavior under sparsity; it loses correlated marker structure and can be noisy when one membership drives a contrast.

The alternative is a source-stratified cross-classified multivariate model. For 8873, jointly model IL6/MMP1/MMP3/MMP14 with feature-specific exposure, context and interaction effects, crossed FLS/macrophage membership effects, and a shared harm factor; retain IL1B/MMP12/MMP13 and MERTK/MRC1/TREM2/SPP1 as contrasts. For 8316, fit a multivariate paired response only after the feature-map and protocol gates pass, with FLS-cluster and nested monocyte effects. The target is the same Delta (8873) and source-specific d-vector (8316), not a disease label. Compare signs, uncertainty, marker coherence and leave-cluster-out stability, not predictive accuracy. The alternative can reveal whether a response is a correlated program and whether partial pooling appropriately widens or shrinks uncertainty; the baseline loses that structure.

Do not fit the alternative if the 8873 rank gate fails or the 8316 feature map/units remain unresolved. This is a scientific deferral, not a mechanical simplification. Expected solver resources are 4–8 CPU cores, <16 GiB memory and minutes for the 33-by-11 primary feature table plus 12-by-feature paired secondary table; the estimate is unmeasured and must be bounded in the solver job. GPU is deferred because the bottleneck is identifiability and biological-unit compatibility, not matrix scale. A neural predictor is not selected: a predictive gain cannot distinguish context selectivity from donor/assay confounding and has no clinically meaningful target estimand here.

## Falsification and interpretation

Freeze material harm at 0.5 SD of H before fitting. Supportive requires a positive exact-exposure Delta above that threshold with uncertainty supporting Delta > 0.5 SD, stable admissible donor/mapping/round sensitivities, coherent primary components, no matching selective pattern in LPS or FLS-only controls, and a gated 8316 secondary response that is directionally compatible without asserting a shared effect. It supports balanced agonism/genetic-loss-of-function, protein/phospho-MerTK, viability, efferocytosis and fibroblast invasion or matrix-degradation follow-up.

Adverse means Delta is nonpositive, Mneg harm is at least as large, generic controls reproduce the apparent selectivity, or a validly gated 8316 perturbation response is discordant. This weakens the context-selective prioritization rationale and favors generic inflammation, composition, timing or assay-specific explanations.

Inconclusive means the primary rank/overlap gate fails, an admissible mapping changes sign, uncertainty spans zero or the material threshold, one membership cluster drives the result, exact and preInhibitor tiers disagree without protocol equivalence, or 8316 annotation/protocol compatibility remains blocked. The next decision is to obtain balanced matched Mpos/Mneg FLS–macrophage donor pairs with dose, exposure time, viability, protein/phospho-MerTK, efferocytosis, secreted mediators and direct FLS functional readouts.

Harbor can verify source-local joins, feature presence, paired contrasts, rank calculations, uncertainty outputs, compatibility status and rule-consistent conclusions. # MerTK-conditioned macrophage–fibroblast communication in rheumatoid arthritis

Episode 1; evolved as a targeted repair of expert seed D3-M2. This is a planned Harbor experiment, not an executed biological result.

## Scientific question and hypothesis

Rheumatoid-arthritis (RA) synovium contains macrophage and fibroblast states associated with either destructive inflammation or remission. The strongest inspected evidence supports three separate observations: HBEGF+ macrophages can induce an EGFR-linked inflammatory/invasive fibroblast response in human RA tissue [K1]; MerTK-positive synovial macrophage subsets are associated with remission and can induce a fibroblast repair response [K2]; and MERTK+ macrophage and fibroblast states are co-enriched in clinically distinct RA synovial tissue contexts [K3]. None of those observations establishes that a MerTK-conditioned macrophage state is the directional driver of a fibroblast transcriptional response, and co-enrichment can reflect shared tissue context or composition.

Hypothesis: among human RA FLS samples cocultured with MerTK/CD206-positive macrophages, macrophage pre-treatment with the recorded MerTK inhibitor will reduce a prespecified coherent inflammatory-FLS program relative to the matched untreated coculture. The reduction should be larger and more coherent than the available MerTK/CD206-negative control, should not be reproduced simply by LPS pre-treatment, and should remain after modeling the contributing FLS/macrophage donors. This is a directional perturbation hypothesis about an in-vitro molecular state, not a claim that MerTK blockade will improve RA clinically.

The key unresolved comparison is:

- MerTK-conditioned communication: Mpos macrophage pre-treatment changes the FLS program in a reproducible direction, with coherent reversal of an inflammatory score.
- Strong rival: generic macrophage activation, donor mixture, FLS composition, batch/cell-number effects, or inhibitor off-target pharmacology explains the same pattern. Those rivals predict no Mpos-specific, donor-consistent reversal or a comparable effect in Mneg/LPS controls.

What would change practice or research is not a small predictive gain. A positive result would justify target-engagement and functional coculture studies aimed at preserving or restoring a pro-resolving macrophage–stromal circuit in difficult-to-treat or relapsing RA. An adverse result would prevent MerTK state association from being promoted to a MerTK-directed fibroblast mechanism.

## Closest inspected work and substantive advance

[K1] established a human RA macrophage–fibroblast communication axis and an EGFR-dependent fibroblast consequence, but it did not test the configured MerTK-pretreated macrophage mixtures. The present experiment adds a matched perturbation boundary and explicitly acknowledges that HBEGF and EGFR are absent from the targeted E-MTAB-8873 panel.

[K2] associated MerTK-positive macrophage subsets with remission and fibroblast repair. The present experiment asks whether a recorded perturbation of the macrophage input changes a prespecified inflammatory FLS output, rather than treating a remission association as a directional mechanism.

[K3] defined clinically meaningful co-enriched MERTK+ macrophage and fibroblast states and candidate communication structure. The present experiment is a small, donor-aware perturbational test designed to distinguish communication from shared tissue context, selection and composition. It does not reproduce K3’s clinical cohort or spatial evidence.

The advance is therefore boundary testing: state association and inferred communication become a falsifiable, bounded perturbation hypothesis, with explicit failure criteria and a direct next experiment.

## Population, temporal boundary, and exact data binding

Primary population: the FLS sample columns in the prepared E-MTAB-8873 targeted matrix. The matrix is a gzipped TSV whose first column is feature and whose remaining 33 columns are the sample_id values in E-MTAB-8873.design.json. It has 445 measured feature rows (446 lines including the header). The design identifies human type-B synovial cells from RA synovial membrane, with condition, treatment, donor_id, donor_status, age, sex, and cells.

Primary matched Mpos inhibitor comparison uses only these design-matrix pairs, because both untreated and pre-inhibitor samples are present for the same recorded contributing-donor mixture:

- R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos vs R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor; donor string SA256A, SA259A; untreated versus macrophages pre-treated with MerTK inhibitor.
- R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos vs R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos_preInhibitor; donor string SA257A, SA266A.
- R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos vs R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos_preInhibitor; donor string SA266A, SA277A.

The R1 SA256A/SA260R Mpos samples have a conflicting donor representation in the prepared design (SA256A versus SA256A | SA256A, SA260R) and are excluded from the primary matched estimate until the SDRF/protocol resolves the contributing donor. The three mixed Mpos/Mneg samples (R2_SA258R_FLS_SA267R_1Mpos_SA266A_3Mneg, R2_SA258R_FLS_SA267R_3Mpos_SA266A_1Mneg, and the R5 analogue) are secondary composition controls, not pure Mpos observations. All E-MTAB-8873 records have donor_status=requires_contributing_donor_model; the FLS cells are not independent donors. No claim will call the 33 columns 33 independent biological replicates.

The matrix’s primary prespecified FLS outcome panel is restricted to measured, uniquely identified targeted rows:

Source files are read-only and derived matrices/results go to the workspace.

Normalize within matrix using a predeclared library-size/size-factor method, log-transform for score modeling, and retain raw counts for a negative-binomial sensitivity analysis. Do not merge duplicate identifiers. Report per-sample cell count, detected-feature count, library size, and all filtering decisions.

Secondary contrasts compare untreated Mpos with untreated Mneg where the FLS donor contribution is recorded; the one available R1 Mneg inhibitor/no-inhibitor pair is a negative-control check, not a stable estimate. Do not use an ordinary donor t-test on the 33 E-MTAB-8873 columns. With only three usable matched mixtures, report paired estimates, donor/mixture bootstrap or Bayesian posterior intervals, and effect directions; do not manufacture asymptotic p-values or call the result independently replicated.

The target is coherent FLS-state reversal under inhibitor, not prediction of a clinical label. Fit the alternative only on the training donor clusters and report a leave-one-cluster-out stress test across R1/R2/R5; with three clusters this is a fragility diagnostic, not external validation. Compare the baseline and alternative on signed paired effect, uncertainty coverage by donor/mixture resampling, coherence of gene-level reversal, and sensitivity to the conflicting donor record. The latent model is scientifically useful because the baseline can hide a distributed, partially correlated state behind noisy per-gene tests; it can also reveal that apparent reversal is driven by one technical module or donor. It is deferred if the sample-level design cannot support partial pooling without unstable factors.

E-MTAB-8316 is analyzed separately as a donor-paired compound-response context: average repeated other_donor_id contexts within each of the four verified donor_id clusters before any exploratory comparison, as required by the dataset guide. Use it to ask whether the compound produces a coherent monocyte transcriptional shift consistent with the proposed macrophage-state perturbation, not to confirm FLS direction or target specificity. No GPU is needed for the planned discovery or solver: the matrices are small enough for CPU linear/multivariate models, and a 16-CPU, 32–64 GB RAM allocation should be sufficient; this estimate is reasoned from the 33×445 targeted matrix and is not a measured fit benchmark. A bounded CPU fit should be under minutes, but convergence and model-library availability remain unverified. No full scientific screen was executed in this episode; only schema/header/design and source-literature inspection were performed.

## Falsification and interpretation

Supportive result: the three usable Mpos matched pairs show a negative inhibitor effect on the inflammatory score, the direction is coherent across the prespecified genes, the effect is not as large in the available Mneg control, donor-aware sensitivity does not erase it, and the multivariate alternative agrees without being driven by an unmeasured feature. This supports a MerTK-conditioned FLS communication hypothesis and justifies independent factorial coculture with target engagement and functional outcomes. It does not prove direct ligand–receptor binding, MerTK target specificity, clinical efficacy, remission causality, or a mechanism involving HBEGF/EGFR.

Adverse result: the score is unchanged or increases under Mpos inhibitor, the sign is inconsistent across matched mixtures, a comparable effect occurs in Mneg or LPS controls, the effect vanishes after donor/run adjustment, or the latent alternative localizes it to a technical/composition factor. This falsifies the proposed MerTK-specific directional interpretation for this assay and redirects work toward generic activation, donor-specific biology, or assay validity. It does not prove that MerTK is irrelevant in RA.

Inconclusive result: the three matched mixtures cannot be reconciled, the donor contribution is not identifiable, counts are too sparse, the panel is not measured reliably, or UNC106238/“MerTK inhibitor” identity and exposure cannot be verified. The correct action is to obtain protocol/target-engagement information and run a new balanced factorial coculture, not to interpret a null as biological refutation.

Computationally checkable claims are the header/design joins, measured-feature availability, normalization/model execution, paired estimates, uncertainty, sensitivity results, and whether the conclusion matches the prespecified outcome. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for direct target engagement, secreted cytokines, fibroblast invasion/matrix damage, tissue localization, treatment response, flare risk, and patient benefit. The verifier must reject both incorrect computation and unsupported claims that a QA result proves mechanism or clinical efficacy.

## Method alternatives and selection record

The simple donor-aware score/feature model was selected as the primary baseline because it is transparent, aligned to the limited matched design, and gives an interpretable falsification test. The hierarchical multivariate factor alternative is retained because it can reveal distributed state coherence and donor heterogeneity that separate gene tests lose; it is not selected as the sole method because three usable Mpos pairs and the targeted panel do not support an unconstrained latent model. A mechanistic ligand–receptor mediation model is deferred: the primary targeted matrix is FLS-focused and lacks HBEGF/EGFR, direct ligand abundance, protein secretion, target engagement and a balanced factorial design. Evidence that would justify revisiting it is a verified ligand-containing assay, independent FLS/macrophage donors, vehicle/washout details, direct MerTK engagement, and a functional FLS endpoint.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly fitted, donor-aware estimates of the Mpos inhibitor effect on the prespecified FLS score and feature panel, plus a fitted/assessed multivariate alternative and the binding/QC audit. Completion requires those outputs, uncertainty and the supportive/adverse/inconclusive classification; a readiness package alone is not a biological result.

The three clinical demonstrations were treated as ambition references, not topic requirements. Delphi’s learned dated-disease-history method is not pursued because these are molecular endpoint assays without longitudinal EHR histories; its lesson is to compare a substantive learned alternative against a simple baseline, which is applied here with a multivariate FLS-state model. Oncoformer is not pursued because the configured domain has no routine EHR or chest-X-ray modality; its lab-only adaptation would answer a different predictive question, not this mechanism question. ALADYNOULLI is not reproduced because genetic inputs and longitudinal patient trajectories are unavailable; a latent-factor adaptation is retained only as a compact descriptive alternative for the current perturbation question.

D3-M1 is deferred: E-MTAB-8322 is macrophage-only and E-MTAB-8873 is targeted FLS/coculture, so whole-tissue composition versus within-cell regulation cannot be identified without tissue composition or matched whole-tissue data. D3-M3 is deferred as a longitudinal persistence claim: E-MTAB-8322 has cross-sectional treatment-naive, resistant and remission groups and no transition times; it can later support a bounded state comparison, not persistence/remission transition inference. D3-M2 is developed because its MerTK-labeled pre-treatment contrasts provide the clearest bounded perturbation test, while the unresolved target-specific and functional evidence is explicitly retained.

# Harbor task: MerTK-conditioned macrophage–fibroblast communication in rheumatoid arthritis

This is a planned, open-ended Harbor experiment, not an executed biological result. The solver must compute the declared estimates from the bound read-only data and report uncertainty. Do not confirm the hypothesis by assumption.

## Scientific question and claim boundary

The strongest inspected evidence supports three separate observations: HBEGF+ macrophages can induce an EGFR-linked inflammatory/invasive fibroblast response in human RA [K1]; MerTK-positive synovial macrophage subsets are associated with remission and can induce a fibroblast repair response [K2]; and MERTK+ macrophage and fibroblast states are co-enriched in clinically distinct RA synovial contexts [K3]. Hypothesis: among human RA FLS samples cocultured with MerTK/CD206-positive macrophages, macrophage pre-treatment with the recorded MerTK inhibitor reduces a prespecified coherent inflammatory-FLS program relative to matched untreated coculture. The reduction should be more coherent than the available MerTK/CD206-negative control, should not be reproduced simply by LPS pre-treatment, and should remain after modeling contributing FLS/macrophage donors.

The strongest rival is generic macrophage activation, donor mixture, FLS composition, batch/cell-number effects, or inhibitor off-target pharmacology. A comparable Mneg/LPS effect, donor-specific sign reversal, or disappearance after contribution-aware modeling supports a rival and is adverse for the MerTK-specific interpretation. # MerTK specificity repair: a donor-blocked macrophage–FLS interaction test

Episode 4 child of candidate-5282fd53c9408f02e8752f4b. This is a planned Harbor experiment. No biological fit or wet-lab experiment was executed here.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The clinically important question is unchanged: can a MerTK-associated macrophage state condition rheumatoid-arthritis (RA) fibroblast-like synoviocyte (FLS) behavior in a way that could motivate resolution-restoring therapy for difficult-to-treat or relapsing RA? The strongest inspected evidence is not yet target-specific. [K1] reports an HBEGF+ macrophage–FLS axis with EGFR-dependent fibroblast invasiveness, but it is a different macrophage program. [K2] reports MerTKpos synovial macrophage subsets associated with remission and an in-vitro FLS repair response. [K3] shows that macrophage and fibroblast states are structured within clinically distinct synovial contexts. These observations support a plausible macrophage–FLS mechanism and its clinical importance; they do not establish that a compound-labeled MerTK perturbation changes FLS communication through MerTK.

Hypothesis: in the prepared E-MTAB-8873 endpoint matrix, the recorded inhibitor effect on a prespecified inflammatory FLS program is larger for MerTK/CD206-positive (Mpos) macrophage cocultures than for the matched MerTK/CD206-negative (Mneg) coculture. Formally, for a matched donor/run block k, let delta_g(k) = normalized FLS outcome under macrophage pretreatment with the recorded MerTK inhibitor minus the untreated outcome. The specificity observable is the interaction I_g = delta_g(Mpos) - delta_g(Mneg), with the same construction for the eight-gene inflammatory score. A MerTK-conditioned interpretation predicts negative I and coherent negative Mpos deltas; generic activation, compound-wide off-target effects, donor mixture, cell-composition differences or assay artifacts predict a comparable Mneg response, a response that tracks LPS rather than Mpos status, or loss of the effect after donor/QC adjustment.

This is a falsifiable molecular-state hypothesis, not a claim that MerTK blockade improves RA, that MerTK is a direct ligand–receptor mediator, or that the recorded compound is selective. The repair matters clinically because falsely treating an association or off-target drug response as MerTK causality could misdirect a resolution-restoring program, whereas a reproducible state-specific interaction would justify a target-engagement and functional coculture study.

## What is already supported versus unresolved

Supported by the inspected evidence:

- RA synovial macrophage programs can affect fibroblast behavior, including destructive invasiveness [K1].
- MerTK-positive macrophage subsets are associated with remission biology and can induce a fibroblast repair response in a separate in-vitro context [K2].
- Macrophage and fibroblast states can be co-structured by clinically meaningful synovial tissue context [K3].

Unresolved and tested here:

- Whether the E-MTAB-8873 inhibitor contrast is Mpos-specific rather than a generic compound effect.
- Whether the FLS response survives a matched Mneg comparison and donor/contributing-mixture sensitivity.
- Whether the inhibitor response is compatible with generic macrophage activation, as indexed by available LPS-pretreated samples.

Still not established by this experiment:

- MerTK target engagement, compound selectivity, direct binding, ligand identity, intracellular signaling, secreted mediator changes, FLS invasion or matrix damage, tissue localization, flare prediction, treatment response or clinical benefit.
- A temporal transition or persistence mechanism. The design JSONs have no numeric sampling-time field or culture-duration/washout table; the temporal boundary is the recorded terminal endpoint for each sample only.

## Analysis, baseline and substantive alternative

First produce a binding/QC audit. Require a one-to-one matrix/design join; list every excluded record; verify the three Mpos pairs and the single R1 Mneg pair; preserve the donor conflict and mixed-ratio records; report per-sample cell count, detected-feature count and library size. Do not filter an absent gene into a presumed zero.

Normalize the E-MTAB-8873 matrix with one prespecified library-size/size-factor method, log-transform for the score, and retain raw counts for a negative-binomial sensitivity analysis. The baseline estimates the eight-gene score and each gene with donor-aware paired contrasts. The primary estimand is the signed Mpos delta across the three usable Mpos blocks, summarized by paired values and donor/mixture bootstrap or a weakly informative Bayesian interval. The specificity estimand is the single R1 interaction I_R1; it is reported as a bounded block-level contrast, never as replicated Mneg inference. The LPS contrasts and mixed-ratio samples are prespecified negative/composition checks. There are too few independent blocks for an asymptotic p-value or an independent-replication claim.

The substantive alternative uses exactly the same samples and outcomes: a strongly regularized hierarchical multivariate latent-state model with the eight-gene inflammatory score as an anchored loading block and the remaining measured rows allowed to contribute only through shrinkage-controlled factors. Random effects represent FLS donor, macrophage/contributing mixture and run when identifiable. Its target is an Mpos-by-inhibitor state interaction, not a clinical label. Fit it on donor clusters and run leave-one-cluster-out stress tests across R1/R2/R5; with three usable clusters this is a fragility diagnostic, not external validation. Compare baseline and alternative on signed Mpos delta, the R1 interaction, gene-level coherence, donor/mixture resampling uncertainty, sensitivity to the donor conflict, and whether the alternative's signal is a generic activation or technical factor.

The alternative is scientifically substantive because separate per-gene tests can miss a distributed correlated FLS state and can fail to reveal that a nominal score is carried by one donor or technical module. It is not selected as the sole method because three usable Mpos blocks and one Mneg interaction block cannot support an unconstrained latent model. It is deferred if shrinkage diagnostics or leave-one-cluster-out fits are unstable. A ligand–receptor/mediation model is also deferred: HBEGF/EGFR and direct ligand/protein, secretion, target-engagement and functional data are absent from the primary panel. Evidence to revisit it is a verified ligand-containing assay, balanced independent donors, protocol exposure/washout, direct MerTK engagement and functional FLS endpoints.

Resource estimate: CPU is appropriate. The targeted matrix is only 33 x 445, and a 16-CPU, 32–64 GiB allocation should fit the baseline and small regularized alternative; this is a reasoned estimate, not a measured full fit. No GPU is required. The configured future solver envelope is up to 16 CPUs, 8 GPUs, 262144 MiB and 28800 seconds; discovery did not spend that envelope, and no full scientific fit was executed.

Actual scientific deliverable: a completed binding/QC audit; newly fitted donor-aware per-gene and score estimates for the three Mpos pairs; the R1 Mpos-versus-Mneg interaction with uncertainty appropriate to one block; prespecified LPS/mixed-ratio sensitivity outputs; a fitted and stress-tested multivariate alternative or a documented stability deferral; and a supportive/adverse/inconclusive classification tied to those computed outputs. Readiness alone is not completion.

## Interpretation and falsification

Supportive evidence requires all of the following as a pattern, not one favorable gene: (1) negative Mpos inhibitor deltas in all or nearly all usable pairs; (2) coherent negative movement of the fixed eight-gene score; (3) a negative R1 interaction because the Mneg inhibitor effect is smaller, not merely an Mpos change; (4) no comparable signal in LPS-pretreated controls or mixed-ratio composition checks; (5) persistence under donor/run/cell-count/library-size sensitivity; and (6) concordance between baseline and a stable, donor-stressed multivariate alternative. This supports a MerTK-conditioned communication hypothesis for this endpoint and justifies the next wet-lab test. It still does not prove target specificity, direct mechanism or clinical benefit.

Adverse evidence is an absent/inconsistent Mpos effect, a comparable Mneg interaction response, a pattern reproduced by LPS, loss after donor/QC adjustment, dependence on the conflicting R1 record, or a multivariate factor localized to technical/library-size or composition variation. That falsifies the proposed MerTK-specific interpretation of this assay and redirects work toward generic activation, donor-specific biology, compound pharmacology or assay validity. It does not prove MerTK is irrelevant in RA.

Inconclusive evidence includes failure of exact sample/design joins, inability to resolve contributing donors or exposure/vehicle/washout, sparse or unreliable prespecified rows, unstable alternative fits, or absence of target-engagement information. A null from the single R1 interaction is imprecise and is not biological refutation. The next action is protocol recovery and the balanced wet-lab test below, not favorable reclassification.

Computationally checkable claims are source hashes and paths, header/design joins, measured-row availability, filtering, normalized values, contrasts, uncertainty, sensitivity outputs, alternative-model stability and whether a conclusion matches the prespecified classification. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for target engagement, direct signaling, secreted mediators, invasion/matrix function, tissue localization, flare, treatment response and patient benefit. A verifier must reject a numerically supportive computation paired with an unsupported claim of MerTK selectivity or clinical efficacy.

## Concrete next wet-lab test

Run the smallest donor-blocked factorial that removes the current ambiguity: the same RA FLS and macrophage donor blocks crossed by macrophage state (Mpos versus Mneg) and macrophage pretreatment (vehicle, UNC106238/recorded inhibitor, orthogonal MerTK perturbation such as MerTK siRNA or a validated blocking antibody, and LPS generic-activation control), with FLS-only wells for baseline. Use at least four independent FLS donors and four independent macrophage donors, randomized/blinded wells and technical replicates nested within donor blocks; do not count wells as independent donors. Record compound identity, concentration, vehicle, pretreatment duration, washout and culture endpoint.

Before interpreting FLS output, verify MerTK surface abundance and pathway engagement (for example, MerTK occupancy or ligand-stimulated phosphorylation with a prespecified assay), macrophage viability and activation. On the same recorded endpoint measure FLS IL-6, CXCL8, MMP3 and MMP9, the eight-gene panel, secreted protein and a functional invasion/matrix assay. The decisive comparison is whether UNC106238 and the orthogonal MerTK perturbation produce the same Mpos-specific interaction while LPS does not and viability/vehicle controls are clean. If pharmacologic and orthogonal effects disagree despite verified engagement, classify the compound response as off-target or non-MerTK until resolved. A rescue or second chemotype is a follow-up, not required for this smallest test.

## Method and branch decisions

Primary baseline chosen: donor-aware fixed score plus per-feature paired interaction, because it is transparent, estimand-aligned and honest about one Mneg block.

Substantive alternative retained: hierarchical anchored multivariate factor model, fitted to the same 33-sample/445-feature input with donor/run shrinkage, leave-one-cluster-out stress testing and uncertainty comparison. It can reveal distributed state coherence and heterogeneity that the baseline loses, but its capacity is intentionally constrained by the sample design.

Not chosen: an unrestricted neural model, ligand–receptor mediation model or cross-dataset classifier. The reason is scientific adequacy, not a blanket complexity or GPU prohibition: the targeted panel lacks ligand/protein/engagement variables and the design cannot identify an unrestricted representation or a clinical prediction target. Evidence for revisiting these choices is the balanced orthogonal wet-lab experiment, verified target engagement, functional FLS outcomes, resolved donor/protocol metadata and independent donor replication.

The three demonstration papers in the research-ambition references were used as ambition context, not as a topic or method list. They are not reproduced here. This proposal is a targeted child repair of the valid parent and does not alter the macrophage–FLS clinical question.

## Key references

[K1] Kuo D et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Science Translational Medicine, 2019, DOI 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587. Abstract-only inspection in `k1-hbegf-excerpt.txt`.

[K2] Alivernini S et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Medicine, 2020, DOI 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Full-text HTML inspection of title, abstract and relevant passages in `k2-remission-excerpt.txt`.

[K3] Zhang F et al. “Deconstruction of rheumatoid arthritis synovium defines inflammatory subtypes.” Nature, 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06708-y. Abstract/metadata-only inspection in `k3-ra-subtypes-excerpt.txt`.

These three distinct works support, bound and challenge different parts of the hypothesis; none is treated as proof of MerTK target specificity.

# UKB-36 repaired proposal: prediagnostic host reserve and competing mortality after colorectal-cancer diagnosis

Status: proposed, not executed. Parent repaired: candidate-d86aa409eb930af6b534886f. Dataset snapshot: `ukb-completed-subset-20261002`; catalog SHA-256 `6834d79f6da16d271bd2f4e017feff3648babeb8e3ea41122015757f0adedf32`.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The closest inspected CRC prognostic work [K1] reports that functional status and frailty add most for overall and nondisease-specific survival, whereas a model containing tumor stage/location already performs well for CRC-specific outcomes. A prospective multi-cancer cohort [K2] associates prediagnostic frailty with mortality after cancer diagnosis. The unresolved clinical question is narrower and consequential: among people with incident CRC, does objectively measured host reserve before diagnosis identify a specifically larger risk of non-CRC death than CRC death, and does that signal persist when the measurement is separated from diagnosis far enough to reduce occult-cancer reverse causation?

Primary falsifiable hypothesis: in incident CRC, lower prediagnostic reserve, measured at least two years before the CRC diagnosis, is associated with a larger five-year cumulative incidence of non-CRC death than CRC death after diagnosis, after adjustment for age, sex, BMI, smoking, and baseline calendar time. Formally, for a one-standard-deviation lower reserve score R, the primary contrast is
`log(HR_nonCRC) - log(HR_CRC) > 0`
in cause-specific hazard models, with the corresponding non-CRC CIF contrast exceeding the CRC CIF contrast at five years. This is an association/description estimand, not a causal effect of changing grip strength or renal biomarkers.

The strongest evidence already supports only an association between prediagnostic frailty/reserve and later mortality [K2], and the parent’s bounded diagnostic reported 4,732 C18 diagnoses plus 108,481 rows with baseline handgrip, creatinine and cancer-diagnosis fields. No complete cohort fit or effect estimate has been computed here. The proposed experiment tests the unresolved differential endpoint and temporal-boundary claim. It does not test treatment tolerance, stage, recurrence, or a biological mechanism.

The principal rival is cancer-associated decline before diagnosis: [K3] shows that >10% prediagnostic weight loss predicts worse CRC survival and attenuates an apparent obesity-survival association. If the UKB reserve signal is confined to assessments within two years of diagnosis and disappears with a five-year lag, occult disease/timing is more plausible than durable host reserve. Other rivals are age/comorbidity selection, measurement error, and differential CRC stage or treatment. UKB does not contain the required stage/treatment variables, so these rivals can be bounded but not fully separated.

Clinical value: a reproducible prediagnostic signal that is stronger for non-CRC mortality could justify prospective validation of a reserve screen at CRC diagnosis and different survivorship/supportive-care pathways. A null or proximity-only result would prevent overinterpreting grip or laboratory values as a durable reserve phenotype.

## Population, temporal anchors and outcomes

Unit: one participant with one `eid` in the `ukb672073` namespace.

Baseline `b_i`: the date in `53-0.0` (Date of attending assessment centre), using only the initial assessment instance. Participants missing `53-0.0` or with non-parsable dates are excluded. The primary exposure is therefore prediagnostic and cannot use any measurement after the baseline assessment.

CRC diagnosis date `t_i`: among paired columns `40005-k.0` (date of cancer diagnosis) and `40006-k.0` (type of cancer: ICD10), k=0,...,21, select the earliest date after `b_i` whose paired ICD-10 code matches the prespecified colorectal definition `^C(18|19|20)` after trimming and upper-casing. This includes colon (C18), rectosigmoid junction (C19), and rectum (C20); it excludes C00-C17, C21 and non-ICD10 values. Do not treat an unpaired date or a missing code as CRC. Exclude anyone with a CRC code/date on or before baseline. The primary cohort requires `730 <= t_i-b_i < 3653` days (approximately 2 to <10 years); the five-year-lag sensitivity cohort requires `t_i-b_i >= 1826` days. A prespecified timing analysis retains eligible CRC cases with `t_i>b_i` and reports strata 0-<2, 2-<5 and >=5 years; it is not used to redefine the primary cohort.

Cancer-diagnosis dates and codes are registry-derived fields in the frozen source. They are not an adjudicated pathology record. If more than one paired CRC record has the same earliest date, retain one participant and record the tie.

Post-diagnosis time origin: `t_i), not assessment date. Follow-up time is days from `t_i` to the first valid death date in `40000-0.0` or `40000-1.0`, or administrative censoring at 2026-10-02, the frozen snapshot boundary. The solver must assert that no accepted death date is after 2026-10-02; if the source documentation establishes an earlier outcome-linkage cutoff, that documented cutoff supersedes the snapshot boundary and must be recorded in the output. Death dates on or before `t_i` are data-quality exclusions, not events.

Competing outcomes, using the underlying primary cause paired by death record in `40001-0.0`/`40001-1.0`:

1. CRC death: cause code matches `^C(18|19|20)`.
2. Non-CRC death: a valid nonmissing ICD-10 cause code that does not match `^C(18|19|20)`.
3. Unknown-cause death: a death date exists but the cause is missing or cannot be parsed.

No death by the administrative boundary is censored. Unknown-cause death remains a third competing event in the primary analysis; a sensitivity analysis classifies it as non-CRC and a second sensitivity censors it at death. Report all three event counts and do not silently discard unknown causes. The primary estimand is the five-year CIF for causes 1 and 2, with cause 3 displayed as a data-quality/competing outcome.

## Exact data binding

Only these read-only Parquet sources are needed. Each is a convenience derivative whose lineage and hash are frozen in the catalog; each source uses `ukb672073` and joins only on `eid`.

Do not join `ukb671626` (identifier namespace `ukb671626`) or `ukb_21622504e5d0aca7_parquet`/`ukb_38b3ef46d4f7b5d4_parquet` (namespace `olink_dta`); no crosswalk is available or needed.

## Exposure and covariate construction

Primary host-reserve score R is fitted only in the training split and then applied unchanged to validation/test data:

- `grip_max = max(46-0.0, 47-0.0)`, using the available side only if one side is missing; both missing is missing.
- Standardize grip_max within sex; standardize log(albumin), -log(creatinine), and -log(cystatin C) within sex using training parameters.
- `R` is the mean of available standardized components when at least three of four are present. Record component count and missingness. The primary complete-reserve analysis requires all four; an imputation-plus-missing-indicator sensitivity uses training medians.
- Higher R means greater measured reserve. Do not call it biological reserve or sarcopenia without validation.

Adjustment covariates are age at recruitment `21022-0.0` (or derived age from `34-0.0` only as a check), sex `31-0.0`, BMI `21001-0.0`, smoking `20116-0.0`, and calendar year from `53-0.0`. Do not adjust for variables measured after diagnosis. The diagnosis-lag `t_i-b_i` is used for timing strata and a sensitivity adjustment, not as a post-diagnosis covariate.

## Baseline versus substantive learned alternative

Both methods use exactly the same participant-level features above, the same incident-CRC population, the same diagnosis-anchored competing outcomes, and the same participant-level split. The comparison addresses a scientific uncertainty—whether reserve acts as a simple approximately linear scalar or through nonlinear threshold/joint patterns—not a leaderboard objective.

Baseline: a prespecified discrete-time competing-risk hazard model with one-year intervals 0-1, 1-2, ..., 4-5 years; interval indicators; R as a linear one-SD term; and the adjustment covariates listed above. Fit cause-specific complementary-log-log hazards (or an equivalent multinomial discrete-time hazard with a documented link), with no data-driven feature selection. Transform interval hazards into cause-specific CIFs using the product-limit recursion. This is interpretable and estimates the primary differential association.

Learned alternative: a regularized gradient-boosted tree multinomial discrete-time hazard model over the same one-year person-period rows and four outcomes (no event, CRC death, non-CRC death, unknown death), with interval as an input and monotonicity not imposed. Use a fixed, small hyperparameter grid decided before test evaluation (e.g., 200/400 trees, depth 2/3, learning rate 0.03/0.05); select by validation integrated Brier score. The substantive output is not only a score: report endpoint-specific permutation importance and held-out partial-dependence/accumulated-local-effect curves for R, grip, albumin, creatinine and cystatin C, plus the joint low-grip/high-cystatin-C pattern. This can reveal thresholds or reserve-component combinations that the scalar baseline erases. If the learned model does not improve or gives unstable effects, retain the baseline as the scientific answer rather than escalating complexity.

Split: hash `eid` with a fixed documented hash and allocate 70% train, 15% validation, 15% locked test, stratified only by event type after participant-level assignment; no person-period row may cross splits. All scaling, imputation, feature selection and tuning use train/validation only. Lock the test file and compute it once.

Evaluation and uncertainty: at 1, 3 and 5 years report cause-specific CIF calibration intercept/slope, integrated and horizon-specific IPCW Brier scores, time-dependent AUC, and a paired participant bootstrap (at least 500 resamples; target 1,000 if within the solver envelope) for contrasts and model differences. For the primary scientific estimand, report adjusted cause-specific hazard ratios for one-SD lower R, the difference between non-CRC and CRC log effects, and standardized five-year CIF contrasts with 95% bootstrap intervals. Calibration must be assessed separately for CRC, non-CRC and unknown death. The solver must emit the cohort flow, missingness table, event table, model coefficients, learned feature-effect table, predictions and random seeds.

Resource estimate: CPU-only is adequate for this tabular, <=5-year discrete-time study; no GPU is required. The future solver planning envelope is 16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB and 28,800 seconds. A conservative unmeasured estimate is 4-8 CPUs, 16-32 GiB, and under two hours for source scans, two small models and 500 bootstrap resamples; this is not a measured runtime. The only attempted diagnostic jobs failed before analysis because their managed environment could not resolve the `/data/ukb_*_parquet` aliases. No fitted model or effect estimate is claimed.

## Falsification, interpretation and stopping rules

Supportive pattern: in the primary >=2-year lag cohort, lower R has a positive non-CRC association and the non-CRC-minus-CRC log-effect contrast is above zero with a 95% interval excluding zero; the direction is similar in the >=5-year sensitivity cohort; and the learned model either exposes stable nonlinear reserve interactions or improves held-out non-CRC CIF calibration/Brier score by a prespecified practically meaningful amount (absolute integrated Brier improvement >=0.01, with bootstrap interval above zero). This supports a robust prognostic regularity and motivates external validation and prospective reserve measurement, not a treatment or mechanism claim.

Adverse pattern: the contrast is zero/reversed, CRC death is at least as strongly associated as non-CRC death, or the reserve association disappears in the >=5-year lag cohort while appearing only at 0-<2 years. That pattern supports competing explanations such as occult cancer-associated decline, age/comorbidity selection, coding/timing artifacts or stage differences; abandon the durable-reserve interpretation and report the boundary.

Inconclusive pattern: sparse deaths, wide intervals crossing clinically relevant values, unstable cause coding, or large test missingness/miscalibration. Do not call this a null. Continue only after improving outcome adjudication, obtaining a documented linkage cutoff, or acquiring independent CRC stage/treatment data.

Falsification checks required before interpretation:

1. Refit by lag strata 0-<2, 2-<5 and >=5 years; a durable host-reserve claim must not be confined to the nearest stratum.
2. Compare complete-case R with training-median/missing-indicator analysis and with grip-only and laboratory-only scores. A result driven by a single assay or missingness flag is not evidence for a unified reserve construct.
3. Repeat with age/sex/BMI/smoking adjustment, then add an available baseline prior-cancer indicator only if its field definition is verified; report how much attenuation occurs.
4. Replace the three-cause outcome with a two-cause analysis (unknown as non-CRC; unknown censored at death) and compare CIFs.
5. Compare diagnosis-anchored competing-risk estimates with a naive analysis that censors competing deaths; a material discrepancy demonstrates why the competing-risk estimand matters.
6. Use a negative-control exposure consisting of shuffled R within sex and a negative-control date feature from assessment-date ordering; the shuffled model must lose the held-out association. Permute outcomes once with a fixed seed; apparent retained signal indicates leakage.
7. Test the learned model only after the baseline specification is frozen. A predictive improvement without stable endpoint-specific reserve effects is a model-performance result, not evidence for host reserve.

Computationally checkable claims are the event definitions, cohort counts, lag strata, model fits, calibration, uncertainty and whether conclusions match locked outputs. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for histologic CRC confirmation, stage, recurrence, treatment receipt/dose/tolerance, cause-of-death validity, generalizability beyond UKB, and any causal or mechanistic statement. The available data cannot establish that low reserve causes non-CRC mortality or identifies patients unable to tolerate therapy.

## Actual scientific deliverable

The solver must newly construct and save:

1. A participant-level flow and analysis table with one row per eligible incident CRC participant, `b_i`, `t_i`, lag, R components, covariates, follow-up, event type and censoring reason.
2. A primary competing-risk estimate file containing model-fitted coefficients, cause-specific HRs, non-CRC-minus-CRC contrast, 1/3/5-year CIFs and bootstrap uncertainty for baseline and learned models.
3. A locked-test model comparison containing IPCW Brier/AUC/calibration metrics and paired uncertainty, plus learned feature-effect/interaction tables.
4. A falsification report with every lag, missingness, unknown-cause, competing-risk, permutation and leakage check, and a conclusion labeled supportive, adverse or inconclusive.

Completion is established only when all four outputs are generated from the bound sources, the test split is locked, reported conclusions link to output rows/figures, and unsupported claims are explicitly excluded. This branch contains no computed result beyond the parent’s bounded diagnostic described above.

## Alternatives not chosen and revisit evidence

A simple reserve-score model was retained because it directly tests the differential endpoint and is transparent. The learned boosted hazard model was retained because it can reveal thresholds and component interactions lost by a scalar score while remaining feasible on CPU. A transformer/longitudinal sequence model was deferred: the primary question is baseline reserve, the required dated repeated reserve series is not bound, and complexity would not answer a distinct scientific uncertainty. A mechanistic renal-muscle model was deferred because no validated mechanistic labels or treatment outcomes are available. Revisit these alternatives only if repeated prediagnostic measurements, stage/treatment data, or an independent cohort are admitted, or if the learned model demonstrates stable nonlinear patterns that need external mechanistic testing.

## Key inspected works

[K1] Chen et al. 2022, *International Journal of Cancer*, DOI 10.1002/ijc.34036. Abstract-only inspection; closest post-diagnosis CRC prognostic comparison.

[K2] Cespedes Feliciano et al. 2020, *JAMA Network Open*, DOI 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2020.16747, PMCID PMC7490646. Full-text XML relevant passages inspected; prediagnostic frailty and mortality.

[K3] Mandic et al. 2026, *JAMA Network Open*, DOI 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.29571, PMCID PMC13476838. Full-text XML relevant passages inspected; prediagnostic weight loss as a reverse-causation rival.

# UKB-36 incident colorectal-cancer competing-risk reserve study — delivery repair

Status: proposed and not fitted. Parent: candidate-e998cb22a44f255f60c18b96. This repair keeps the same question, incident C18-C20 cohort, competing-risk estimand, >=2-year primary lag, 0-<2/2-<5/>=5 timing falsification, selection and external-cause negative control, missing deprivation limitation, and the inherited three-work evidence set.

## Scientific question and hypothesis

The strongest available evidence supports an association between frailty, grip or related reserve measures and mortality or perioperative vulnerability in colorectal-cancer populations [K1, K2], and supports separating CRC and non-CRC mortality with competing-risk methods [K3]. It does not establish that an objectively measured, prediagnostic reserve profile distinguishes durable host vulnerability from occult cancer decline.

The falsifiable hypothesis is: among incident C18-C20 cases, lower prediagnostic measured reserve at least two years before diagnosis is associated with a greater five-year cumulative incidence of non-cancer death than CRC-specific death, after adjustment for age, sex, BMI, smoking, calendar time, comorbidity and CRC subsite; adding reserve improves held-out non-cancer risk prediction over the same routine-data baseline. This is a prognostic/descriptive association claim, not a causal treatment-tolerance, stage, recurrence or mechanism claim.

The leading rival is timing or selection: a measurement close to diagnosis may capture occult cancer/cachexia, while missing stage, treatment and UKB volunteer selection may create the signal. The experiment distinguishes these explanations with lag strata, cause-specific comparisons, missingness/selection analyses and an external-cause negative-control endpoint. These checks can bound the rival, not establish mechanism.

## Population and exact registered inputs

Use only participants in the ukb672073 identifier namespace and join sources only by eid within that namespace. The four required read-only registered Parquet sources are:
