Required columns: eid, 53-0.0 assessment date, 46-0.0 and 47-0.0 grip, 21001-0.0 BMI, 20116-0.0 smoking; 46/47 instance 1 is reserved for a sensitivity only.

2. Source ID ukb_ce68812c3a782e09_parquet; exact registered path [private-path]/ukb_ce68812c3a782e09.parquet; SHA-256 d446c8288dfe59abc97e44a43027628aa7221a60f307d4da879a7c491b930299. Catalog table datasets/population_multiomics/table-674bd55f4152a860.json, table UKB/ukb672073_Population_Characteristics.csv (Parquet), archive member ordinary file. Required columns: eid, 31-0.0 sex, 34-0.0 year of birth and 21022-0.0 age at recruitment.

3. Source ID ukb_a19465be8f90accc_parquet; exact registered path [private-path]/ukb_a19465be8f90accc.parquet; SHA-256 9a62c73361094f4e12045082d8872efa84933e7bb86f596e9e8a49fc162a4ab0. Catalog table datasets/population_multiomics/table-50f94f98137a2d88.json, table UKB/ukb672073_Biological_Samples.csv (Parquet), archive member ordinary file. Required columns: eid, 30600-0.0/1.0 albumin, 30700-0.0/1.0 creatinine and 30720-0.0/1.0 cystatin C. Instance 1 is sensitivity-only because no sample date is bound.

4. Source ID ukb_e53f1b242ccf9047_parquet; exact registered path [private-path]/ukb_e53f1b242ccf9047.parquet; SHA-256 36d0e32efc608dd0e324a6e66fd4211813e7542ec08b78213488ab8f52874ad8. Catalog table datasets/population_multiomics/table-03f57283ab9ae48b.json, table UKB/ukb672073_Health_Related_Outcomes.csv (Parquet), archive member ordinary file. Required columns: eid, paired death date/cause 40000-0.0/1.0 and 40001-0.0/1.0, paired cancer date/code 40005-0.0 through 40005-21.0 and 40006-0.0 through 40006-21.0, and dated inpatient diagnosis fields 41270-* with 41280-*.

The registered catalog snapshot is ukb-completed-subset-20261002 with catalog SHA-256 6834d79f6da16d271bd2f4e017feff3648babeb8e3ea41122015757f0adedf32. The solver must verify each path and hash, source eid uniqueness, namespace, required columns and join counts before analysis; sources remain read-only. Do not use /data aliases, ukb671626, Olink/dta sources or any unverified crosswalk.

Eligible participants have a valid initial 53-0.0 assessment date, no valid paired C00-C97 cancer record on or before that date, and a valid paired C18/C19/C20 cancer record after assessment. The assessment-date recruitment range is retained from the parent protocol (2006-01-01 through 2010-12-31). Do not use post-diagnosis measurements or codes as predictors.

## Paired date/code and follow-up algorithm

For each cancer slot k, parse 40005-k.0 as a date and 40006-k.0 as a trimmed, upper-case ICD-10 string. A slot is eligible only when both values are present, parseable and paired at the same k. A valid prior C00-C97 slot on or before assessment excludes the participant. Among valid post-assessment C18, C19 or C20 slots, define t0 as the minimum date. If several valid CRC slots share t0, retain one participant, record the number and slot IDs of the tie, and select the lowest slot index then lexicographically smallest normalized code only for a deterministic subsite label. A cancer date with a missing/unusable paired code, or a code without its paired date, is never silently used. Report unpaired, malformed and date-discordant records.

The primary cohort is t0 minus assessment date >= 730 days and is limited to participants whose five-year follow-up is supportable by the verified outcome boundary described below. The timing falsification retains otherwise eligible incident cases in exactly 0-<2 years, 2-<5 years and >=5 years after assessment. The >=5-year stratum is a sensitivity, not a replacement primary cohort.

Define tau_source only after a readiness audit of the outcome source and its registered catalog/README provenance. tau_source is the latest date explicitly supported as available for outcome ascertainment by that source documentation or linkage metadata. It is not inferred from the campaign date, file modification time, candidate creation time or the 2022-12-31 date used in the defective parent. If the bound source does not document a follow-up cutoff, readiness fails and the solver must report the missing dependency without fitting or inventing a boundary. The output must record the exact provenance locator and value of tau_source.

For each participant, follow-up starts at t0 and ends at the earliest valid death date after t0 or tau_source. The primary five-year estimand is computed only where t0 + 5 years (using the documented leap-year convention) is no later than tau_source. For one- and three-year estimands, apply the analogous horizon check. A death date after tau_source is censored at tau_source. A death date on or before t0 is an impossible ordering: exclude that participant from the primary analysis, retain the exclusion count and slot values in the data-quality report, and do not recode it as a post-diagnosis event.

Death records are paired by instance: slot j consists only of 40000-j.0 with 40001-j.0. Parse all valid death dates. Choose the earliest date. If multiple slots tie at that earliest date, prefer a slot with a valid parseable cause; among multiple valid causes choose the lowest instance index, record the tie and discarded slots. If no tied earliest slot has a usable cause, retain the earliest date and classify cause as unknown; never use a later death date to repair a missing cause. A missing, malformed or non-ICD-10 underlying cause is unknown/unusable, not non-cancer.

Classify the selected death as: CRC-specific when the normalized underlying cause matches C18/C19/C20; other cancer when it matches C00-C97 but not C18-C20; non-cancer when it is a valid cause outside C00-C97; and unknown-cause death when date exists but the cause is missing or unusable. The primary competing-risk output retains unknown cause as a separately reported competing event. Sensitivities classify unknown as non-cancer and censor at unknown death. No cause is silently dropped. External-cause death, when validly coded V01-Y89, is a prespecified negative-control endpoint; it is not folded into the non-cancer target merely because it is non-CRC.

## Exposure, missing deprivation and estimand

Construct the primary reserve score only within the training partition. Grip is the maximum of available instance-0 left/right values, with side-missing indicators; both missing is missing. Standardize grip, log albumin, negative log creatinine and negative log cystatin C using training parameters. The composite is the mean of available standardized components when prespecified minimum component availability is met; report both complete-four-component and training-fold imputation plus missingness-indicator analyses. Higher score means higher measured reserve, not validated biological reserve.

Use age at diagnosis derived from 21022-0.0 plus the assessment-to-diagnosis interval under a documented age convention, sex, BMI, smoking, calendar year, CRC subsite and a dated pre-t0 Charlson count from 41270/41280 excluding the incident CRC record. All transforms, code maps and imputation parameters are learned inside training folds.

Townsend deprivation is an explicit limitation. The catalog audit found no verified 189-0.0 deprivation field in the ukb672073 Parquet sources; occurrences of 189 in diagnosis arrays are not deprivation. The executable baseline must be labeled available routine baseline without deprivation. B0+D is readiness-gated and can be run only if an admitted source column, namespace, path and hash are supplied. Ethnicity, centre, education or BMI must not be renamed as deprivation. Results without B0+D cannot support the stronger claim of reserve incremental to deprivation.

The primary estimand is the contrast in five-year cumulative incidence and held-out prediction error for non-cancer death between B0 and B1, treating CRC-specific, other-cancer and unknown death as competing events. Report the non-cancer-versus-CRC contrast, not a causal effect. Cause-specific and Fine-Gray estimates are descriptive association summaries.

## Baseline, learned alternative and analysis

B0 is a prespecified interpretable discrete-time cause-specific competing-risk model with one-year intervals through five years and covariates age at diagnosis, assessment-to-diagnosis timing, sex, BMI, smoking, calendar year, Charlson count and CRC subsite. B1 adds reserve components and missingness indicators. Both use exactly the same eligible participant set and split. Unknown cause remains a separate outcome in the primary model.

The substantive learned alternative is a CPU gradient-boosted multinomial discrete-time hazard model using the same one-year person-period rows, same outcomes and same B0/B1 inputs, with nonlinear reserve thresholds, reserve-by-timing interactions and missingness patterns. It is chosen to test whether clinically meaningful thresholds or component combinations are erased by the transparent scalar model, not to chase a small predictive gain. Fit only after B0 is frozen, with a fixed small hyperparameter grid selected on validation data.

Assign participants, never person-period rows, to a fixed 70/15/15 train/validation/locked-test split using documented seed 36 and stratification by event type and diagnosis year after deterministic hashing of eid. All scaling, imputation, tuning and reserve construction use training/validation only. Test is read once after locking. Report cause-specific CIF calibration, calibration-in-the-large and slope, horizon and integrated IPCW Brier scores, time-dependent AUC, and paired participant bootstrap uncertainty for B0 versus B1 and B0 versus learned B1 at 1, 3 and 5 years. Report adjusted one-SD lower-reserve associations, the non-cancer-minus-CRC log-effect contrast, CIFs, event counts and the learned feature-effect table.

The actual deliverable is newly fitted output, not a proposal narrative: (1) cohort flow and one-row-per-participant analysis table with b, t0, lag, exposure components, covariates, tau_source, follow-up and exclusion/event reason; (2) fitted baseline and learned model objects plus coefficients/feature effects; (3) locked-test predictions, CIFs, calibration, Brier/AUC and bootstrap intervals; and (4) a falsification/interpretation report covering all prespecified checks. Completion requires output-linked conclusions and uncertainty. This branch contains no fitted results.

CPU is scientifically adequate for the tabular models. Discovery estimate: 4-8 CPUs, 16-32 GiB RAM, and under two hours after column projection, with 500 bootstrap resamples; this is unmeasured and not a completed run. The future solver envelope is up to 16 CPUs, 262144 MiB and 28800 seconds. No GPU is required; GPU use would not resolve missing deprivation, stage, treatment or adjudicated cause. A temporal sequence model remains deferred because no validated dated longitudinal reserve series or treatment/stage sequence is bound; revisit only if those dependencies are admitted or the learned model exposes a stable trajectory pattern requiring a distinct study.

## Falsification and interpretation

The timing falsification repeats the prespecified analysis in 0-<2, 2-<5 and >=5 years from assessment, retaining >=2 years as primary. A signal confined to 0-<2 years or disappearing at >=5 years is adverse to durable prediagnostic reserve and supports occult disease/timing, not confirmation.

Compare CRC-specific, other-cancer, non-cancer and unknown-cause patterns. A non-cancer increment that persists beyond two years, is not reproduced for CRC death, and is stable under cause sensitivities is supportive of prognostic specificity. A similar or larger CRC-death signal is adverse to the proposed separation and is compatible with stage/tumour burden; it does not prove a mechanism.

Compare all incident cases with reserve-complete cases on age, sex, lag, BMI, smoking, centre/available demographic fields, comorbidity and diagnosis year; model reserve availability and use inverse-probability weighting as a sensitivity. Report missingness by lag and outcome. Material disagreement between complete-case, imputed and weighted analyses makes the result selection-sensitive. Fit the external-cause V01-Y89 negative-control endpoint with the same exposure and timing rules. A strong matching external-cause association suggests general frailty, volunteer selection or coding artefact and is adverse to cancer-specific interpretation.

Report paired-record discordance, duplicate eids, impossible orderings, tied dates, unknown causes and counts by source. Repeat with 41270/41280 inpatient diagnosis records where feasible. Compare the competing-risk analysis with naive censoring of competing deaths. Use fixed exposure permutation and outcome permutation negative probes only after the primary analysis is locked; retained signal indicates leakage.

Supportive results require a non-cancer reserve association and calibrated held-out improvement over B0 in the >=2-year primary cohort, compatible uncertainty, persistence in >=5 years, no material selection instability, and no matching external-cause or CRC-specific signal. This supports a prognostic regularity and motivates external validation or prospective reserve measurement; it does not establish treatment tolerance, causality or mechanism.

Adverse results are no incremental information, reversal of the differential contrast, CRC-dominant association, timing-only association, strong external-cause association, or coding/order instability. Report the relevant rival explanation and do not claim durable host reserve.

Inconclusive results are sparse events, an undocumented tau_source, wide intervals crossing clinically relevant effects, severe missingness, cause instability, failed calibration or unavailable B0+D. Do not call an imprecise null a refutation; defer to longer verified follow-up, registry linkage, expert cause adjudication or an independent cohort.

## Clinical advance and limits

If supportive, the study would define a clinically useful prognostic boundary: whether low-cost prediagnostic reserve adds information about competing non-cancer mortality after CRC diagnosis beyond routine variables and timing. This could motivate prospective geriatric/nutritional assessment and a treatment-planning study. It cannot justify withholding therapy, infer toxicity or dose tolerance, establish a biological pathway, or generalize beyond UKB. TNM stage, grade, treatment, toxicity, performance status, validated frailty, adjudicated causes and external validation require linkage, expert review or another study.

## Exactly three inspected works

The inherited evidence set is reused unchanged; no fourth work is introduced. All three are abstract-only inspected in the parent branch, and no full text is claimed here.

[K1] Zhou H, Li W, Liu S, Zhang H, Huang Y, Hu Y, Hu Y. “Pre-frailty and frailty as predictors of mortality among colorectal cancer survivors: Evidence from the National Health Interview Survey (1997-2018).” Medicine (Baltimore), 2026. PMID 41686585. It supports frailty/mortality association but is survivor-selected and not a prediagnostic competing-risk test.

[K2] Zhao D, He F, Liu H, Qing X. “Impact of preoperative handgrip strength and frailty on early postoperative loss of independence in patients with colorectal cancer.” Frontiers in Oncology, 2026. PMID 42459304. It supports handgrip/frailty as a perioperative vulnerability marker but not long-term mortality or causal tolerance.

[K3] García-Aranda M et al. “Ten-Year Outcomes in Colorectal Cancer-Competing Risks and Patient Vulnerability: A Prospective Multicenter Observational Study.” Journal of Clinical Medicine, 2026;15:4389. PMID 42279250. It supports competing-risk separation of CRC and other mortality but does not establish a prediagnostic reserve effect or remove stage/treatment confounding.

The unchanged parent key-references.json and the three attached UTF-8 evidence snapshots are to be reused as supporting files. Their receipts and hashes must remain unchanged; this repair changes only the scientific data binding and outcome-boundary instructions.

# Episode 6 evolution — UKB-36 follow-up/outcome audit child

Status: proposed, not fitted. Parent: `candidate-d2fb106edf9bb248bb63775b`. This is a substantive execution child, not a change in the scientific population or endpoint: it preserves the incident C18–C20 prediagnostic reserve-versus-CRC/non-CRC competing-risk question while making the readiness gate, paired outcomes, selection falsification and baseline/learned comparison deterministic.

## 1. Scientific opening, supported claim, and unresolved hypothesis

The inspected literature supports three bounded points. Frailty is associated with mortality among colorectal-cancer survivors [K1]; low preoperative handgrip/frailty is associated with postoperative complications and loss of independence [K2]; and CRC-specific and non-CRC mortality have distinguishable competing-risk patterns, with tumor stage/residual disease and patient vulnerability pointing in different directions [K3]. None of these abstracts tests whether an objectively measured reserve profile *before diagnosis* is associated with a durable non-cancer mortality pattern rather than merely recording occult cancer decline, age/comorbidity, or selection.

The unresolved hypothesis is:

> Among UKB participants assessed in 2006–2010 who are free of valid paired C00–C97 cancer records at assessment and later develop incident C18–C20 cancer, lower assessment-time measured reserve, with diagnosis at least 730 days later, is associated with a larger five-year cumulative-incidence increase in non-cancer death than in CRC-specific death after prespecified age, sex, BMI, smoking, calendar-time, comorbidity and subsite adjustment.

This is a prognostic/descriptive association hypothesis. It is not a claim that low reserve causes death, identifies treatment intolerance, reflects a validated frailty construct, or explains a biological mechanism. A positive result would be a clinically relevant boundary test: it would justify external validation and prospective prediagnostic reserve measurement, not a treatment rule.

The leading rival is occult-cancer timing: near-diagnosis loss of reserve may be an early manifestation of cancer, cachexia or intensified observation. Other rivals are age/comorbidity confounding, volunteer/inclusion selection, exposure missingness, diagnosis/cause coding, and CRC stage/treatment. For incident CRC, select the earliest valid post-`b_i` C18, C19 or C20 date as `t0_i`. Retain all tied earliest slots and use the lowest slot, then lexicographically smallest normalized code, only for deterministic subsite labeling. A source audit using this rule found 6,094 assessment-window participants with a valid paired cancer on/before assessment, 2,219 post-assessment CRC cases with no such prior cancer, and 329/493/1,397 of those cases in the 0–<2, 2–<5 and >=5-year diagnosis-lag strata. These are screening counts before reserve completeness and documented follow-up gating, not fitted estimates.

Primary eligibility is diagnosis lag `t0_i-b_i >= 730` days, valid reserve exposure under the prespecified missingness rule, and documented five-year follow-up support. The primary timing window is 2–<5 years plus >=5 years; the 0–<2-year stratum is an adverse reverse-causation check, and >=5 years is a prespecified durable-timing sensitivity, not a replacement for the primary.

Death must use the paired slot `40000-j.0` date and `40001-j.0` underlying cause. Parse valid dates, retain only deaths after `t0_i`, choose the earliest date, and on a date tie prefer a usable ICD-10 cause then the lowest slot while recording all tied slots. Unknown means missing, malformed or non-ICD-10 cause. Classify first death as: CRC-specific C18/C19/C20; other cancer C00–C97 excluding C18–C20; non-cancer outside C00–C97; or unknown. Unknown is a separate competing event in the primary analysis. Sensitivities classify unknown as non-cancer and censor at unknown death. V01–Y89 external-cause death is a separately reported endpoint-specific negative control, not automatically folded into target non-cancer death. Death on/before `t0_i` is an impossible ordering: exclude it from primary and report it.

The primary estimand is the adjusted five-year cumulative-incidence differential:
`Delta5 = [CIF_nonCRC(R=Q25) - CIF_nonCRC(R=Q75)] - [CIF_CRC(R=Q25) - CIF_CRC(R=Q75)]`,
with other-cancer and unknown death competing, Q25/Q75 fixed from training data, and standardization over the locked eligible population. Report the one-, three- and five-year CIFs, `Delta5`, and the difference between cause-specific reserve log-effects; use 95% participant-bootstrap intervals. A positive `Delta5` supports the stated differential association. These are standardized prognostic associations, not causal effects. Fine–Gray and cause-specific estimates are descriptive sensitivity parameterizations, not interchangeable causal estimands.

## 4. Exposure and covariates

Set `grip_max = max(46-0.0, 47-0.0)`, using one side if the other is absent and missing if both are absent. The four primary reserve components are grip_max, albumin `30600-0.0`, creatinine `30700-0.0` and cystatin C `30720-0.0`. Fit transformations and scaling within training data only: sex-stratified standardization of grip, log(albumin), negative-log creatinine and negative-log cystatin C. Primary R is the mean of available standardized components when at least three of four are present; record component count and every missingness indicator. Complete-four, grip-only, laboratory-only, and training-median-plus-indicators versions are mandatory sensitivities. Call R “measured reserve,” never validated biological reserve.

Adjustment uses age at diagnosis derived from `21022-0.0` plus exact assessment-to-diagnosis interval under a documented convention, sex `31-0.0`, BMI `21001-0.0`, smoking `20116-0.0`, diagnosis calendar year, CRC subsite, and a dated pre-`t0` Charlson count from `41270-*`/`41280-*`, excluding the incident CRC. No post-diagnosis variable is allowed. Townsend deprivation, ethnicity, centre, stage, grade, TNM, treatment, toxicity, performance status, recurrence, histology, validated frailty, adjudicated causes and external validation are not in the verified binding. In particular, do not relabel diagnosis-array occurrences of 189 as deprivation.

## 5. Baseline versus learned alternative

Both models use the identical participant split, outcome construction, covariates, reserve components, missingness indicators and diagnosis anchor. The comparison tests whether reserve is adequately represented as an approximately linear scalar or instead has stable thresholds/component combinations; it is not a leaderboard exercise.

- **B0/B1 interpretable baseline:** one-year discrete-time cause-specific complementary-log-log hazards for CRC, non-cancer, other-cancer and unknown death through five years. B0 contains age using prespecified restricted cubic-spline knots, sex, BMI, smoking, calendar year, Charlson count, subsite and interval. B1 adds one linear one-SD R term and its pre-specified missingness indicators. Convert hazards to CIFs by the competing-risk recursion. Freeze B0/B1 before inspecting test predictions.
- **B2 learned alternative:** CPU gradient-boosted multinomial discrete-time hazard model over the same person-period rows and four outcome states, with the same B1 inputs plus the four reserve components, interval and prespecified reserve-by-diagnosis-lag interactions. Use a small fixed grid (200/400 trees, depth 2/3, learning rate 0.03/0.05) chosen on validation integrated Brier score only. Report endpoint-specific permutation importance and held-out accumulated-local-effect curves; do not treat them as mechanisms.

Use a fixed participant-level 70/15/15 train/validation/locked-test split, seed 36, assigned by deterministic eid hashing and stratified only after participant assignment by event type and diagnosis year. No person-period rows may cross splits. Fit scaling, imputation, tuning and Q25/Q75 on training/validation only; read the locked test once.

Report cause-specific CIF calibration intercept/slope, one/three/five-year and integrated IPCW Brier scores, time-dependent AUC, one-SD reserve effects, `Delta5`, event counts, model coefficients, learned effect tables and paired participant-bootstrap uncertainty with at least 500 resamples. Treat an absolute locked-test integrated-Brier improvement of 0.01 with an interval above zero as a pre-specified practically meaningful predictive improvement, but do not require B2 improvement to support a descriptive association if B1 is stable. A predictive improvement without a stable reserve endpoint contrast is only a prediction result.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly fitted and output-linked: (1) cohort-flow and one-row-per-participant table with `b_i`, `t0_i`, lag, paired-record audit, reserve components, missingness, covariates, `tau_source`, support and exclusion reason; (2) fitted B0/B1/B2 objects and effect tables; (3) locked-test CIF, calibration, Brier/AUC and bootstrap outputs; and (4) a falsification report labeling the evidence supportive, adverse or inconclusive. No fitted result is asserted in this child.

## 6. Falsification and interpretation

Run each check once under a frozen specification and retain all adverse results.

1. **Occult timing:** repeat 0–<2, 2–<5 and >=5-year lag strata. A signal confined to 0–<2, or absent at >=5, is adverse to durable prediagnostic reserve and supports occult disease/observation timing.
2. **Age/comorbidity:** compare the prespecified flexible-age/Charlson model with age-only, age-plus-comorbidity, and age-band analyses (40–59, 60–69, >=70 where supported). Large attenuation or a reserve-by-age reversal indicates confounding or effect heterogeneity, not a host-reserve mechanism.
3. **Missingness/selection:** compare complete-four, min-three, imputed-indicator, grip-only and laboratory-only R. Model availability of complete R from assessment age, sex, BMI and smoking among all assessment-window participants; apply stabilized inverse-probability-of-observation weights only as a sensitivity and report overlap/extreme weights. Compare included incident cases with assessment-window participants and report missingness by event/lag. This tests measured availability selection; it cannot remove UKB volunteer selection or MNAR bias.
4. **Coding:** report every unpaired/malformed cancer or death slot, tie, unknown cause and impossible ordering. Compare paired `40005/40006` diagnosis anchoring with the earliest concordant pre-`t0` C18–C20 `41270/41280` occurrence where date/code are both usable. Material instability is adverse to the coding interpretation.
5. **Competing-risk and cause:** compare CRC, non-cancer, other-cancer, unknown and external-cause patterns; compare diagnosis-anchored competing-risk CIFs with naive censoring of competing deaths. A matching external-cause signal or CRC-dominant pattern weakens the proposed differential reserve interpretation.
6. **Leakage/permutation:** shuffle R within sex once, permute outcomes once with fixed seed, and run fixed exposure/outcome permutation probes. Retained held-out signal indicates leakage or coding contamination and invalidates the corresponding result.
7. **Stage/treatment boundary:** do not proxy stage or treatment with death cause, diagnosis lag, comorbidity or reserve. If the result is CRC-specific, disappears after timing checks, or differs by subsite, label stage/treatment as unresolved and do not reinterpret it as biology.

**Supportive:** readiness passes; in the >=2-year primary cohort lower R yields positive `Delta5` with an interval excluding zero; direction is compatible in >=5 years; the contrast is not reproduced for CRC death; cause, coding, missingness-weighted and complete/imputed analyses are materially consistent; and no matching external-cause signal or permutation leakage appears. **Adverse:** `Delta5` is zero/reversed, CRC death is at least as strongly associated, the effect is timing-only, it is driven by missingness or one assay, it tracks age/comorbidity, is unstable under paired coding/unknown-cause rules, or matches external-cause/permutation signals. Report which rival this supports and abandon the durable-reserve interpretation.

**Inconclusive:** readiness fails; deaths/events are sparse; clinically important intervals are wide; causes or coding are unstable; test calibration fails; or weighted analyses lack overlap. Do not call this a null. Continuing requires documented linkage completeness, expert outcome review, stage/treatment linkage or an independent cohort.

Computationally checkable claims are source binding, paired parsing, cohort flow, lag counts, model outputs, calibration, uncertainty and interpretation-to-output consistency. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for histologic confirmation, cause-of-death validity, stage, treatment, recurrence, treatment tolerance, mechanism, causality and generalizability outside UKB.

## 7. Alternatives and resource decision

The CPU baseline is retained because it directly estimates the differential competing-risk estimand and makes age/comorbidity and cause contrasts inspectable. The CPU boosted alternative is retained because it can reveal clinically meaningful reserve thresholds or component combinations that a scalar R erases while remaining feasible on the same inputs and split. A transformer/sequence model is deferred: no validated dated repeated reserve/laboratory trajectory is bound, and it would add representation complexity without separating a distinct rival explanation. A mechanistic renal-muscle model is deferred because validated mechanistic labels and treatment outcomes are absent. Revisit these alternatives only if repeated dated measures, stage/treatment evidence or an independent cohort is admitted, or if B2 shows stable nonlinear patterns requiring external mechanistic testing.

The measured discovery audit used a short CPU Parquet scan (about 11 seconds for selected columns on the available shell); full fitting, 500 bootstrap resamples and calibration are unmeasured. Plan 4–8 CPUs, 16–32 GiB RAM and under two hours as a provisional CPU estimate, subject to a readiness probe; the future solver envelope remains up to 16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB and 28,800 seconds. GPU is not needed for these tabular models. No fitted model or solver result is claimed here.

## 8. Three inspected works

All three works were inspected through the attached Europe PMC metadata/abstract snapshots only; no full text or supplement is claimed.

[K1] Zhou H, Li W, Liu S, Zhang H, Huang Y, Hu Y, Hu Y. “Pre-frailty and frailty as predictors of mortality among colorectal cancer survivors: Evidence from the National Health Interview Survey (1997-2018).” *Medicine*, 2026. [K2] Zhao D, He F, Liu H, Qing X. “Impact of preoperative handgrip strength and frailty on early postoperative loss of independence in patients with colorectal cancer.” *Frontiers in Oncology*, 2026. PMID 42459304. Supports perioperative handgrip/frailty vulnerability; does not establish long-term or prediagnostic timing.

[K3] García-Aranda M et al. “Ten-Year Outcomes in Colorectal Cancer-Competing Risks and Patient Vulnerability: A Prospective Multicenter Observational Study.” *Journal of Clinical Medicine*, 2026;15:4389. PMID 42279250. Supports competing-risk separation and highlights stage/treatment as a consequential unresolved rival.

# Working proposal: discordant kidney recovery after ICU AKI

Status: Lead design for episode 1; proposed experiment, not executed results.

## Scientific deliverable

The future Harbor solver must newly construct an index-ICU-stay cohort and fit two prespecified analyses on the same eligible population:

1. A transparent, standardized logistic-risk analysis estimating the 7-day risk difference between discordant and concordant recovery, with uncertainty and sensitivity analyses.
2. A substantive temporal alternative that fits a patient-level-split masked sequence model on the same pre-landmark data, then reports held-out calibration, Brier/AUROC, and the same discordant-versus-concordant risk contrast.

Completion requires a cohort flow and cell counts, phenotype definitions, adjusted risk difference with confidence interval, secondary outcome estimates, sensitivity/negative-control results, and model-comparison outputs linked to saved computed files. A readiness probe or a favorable-looking coefficient is not completion.

## Unresolved clinical question and hypothesis

After an ICU patient develops creatinine-defined AKI, clinicians may infer recovery when serum creatinine falls. The unresolved question is whether that inference is unsafe when urine output and recorded fluid balance do not improve at the same time.

Hypothesis: among adults with a first eligible ICU stay who develop creatinine-defined AKI, survive and remain in the ICU to a fixed 48-hour post-onset landmark, and show a prespecified creatinine fall, patients with low urine output or positive net fluid balance at that landmark have a higher 7-day risk of hospital death or new kidney-replacement therapy than patients with both urine recovery and non-positive fluid balance. The primary estimand is the standardized prognostic risk difference, discordant minus concordant recovery.

This tests a falsifiable association. It does not claim that discordance causes death, that positive balance proves hemodilution or congestion, or that the patient has measured persistent renal dysfunction. The clinically consequential decision it could inform is whether a falling creatinine alone should be sufficient for de-escalating renal monitoring or transition planning after AKI. The result would be hypothesis-generating for a monitoring/intervention study, not a bedside rule.

## What is supported versus unresolved

The strongest inspected evidence supports three bounded propositions. Creatinine can overestimate measured kidney function after prolonged critical illness, in association with muscle loss [K1]. Urine output thresholds and their time windows materially alter prognostic discrimination when combined with creatinine, including in MIMIC-IV, but that work studies AKI staging rather than recovery discordance [K2]. Positive fluid balance around ICU AKI is associated with AKI and mortality in a prospective external cohort, although it is confounded by illness and treatment severity [K3].

The unresolved claim is narrower and new for this design: within a fixed post-AKI survivor landmark, does a creatinine fall accompanied by low charted urine output or positive charted net balance identify a reproducibly higher-risk recovery phenotype than creatinine plus physiologic recovery? Existing evidence does not establish that such a phenotype is present in this MIMIC snapshot, that its mechanism is dilution, muscle loss, congestion or tubular injury, or that changing treatment improves outcomes. ## Exposure phenotypes

Find the peak valid creatinine in [t0,tL] and define creatinine recovery as peak minus landmark creatinine >=0.3 mg/dL. A ratio sensitivity is landmark/peak <=0.8. Neither means normal kidney function.

Define urine recovery as >=0.5 mL/kg/h during [tL-24h,tL]. Among patients with creatinine recovery and complete primary physiology data:

- concordant recovery: creatinine recovery + urine recovery + net balance <=0;
- discordant creatinine-only recovery: creatinine recovery + low urine output or positive net balance;
- exploratory three-level phenotype: low urine only, positive balance only, both.

Patients without creatinine recovery are a descriptive reference group, not part of the primary discordant-versus-concordant contrast. Report all exclusions and missingness before outcome comparisons.

Primary outcome Y7d is hospital death or first incident RRT in [tL,tL+7d), using admissions.deathtime/hospital_expire_flag and procedureevents RRT items; do not count RRT before tL. Secondary outcomes are death alone, RRT alone, ICU readmission during the same admission, and hospital death by dischtime. Report component-specific cumulative incidence and handle death/RRT competing events descriptively or with cause-specific models; the composite is primary to avoid selecting a favorable competing-risk convention.

Primary estimand:
RD = P(Y7d=1 | discordant) - P(Y7d=1 | concordant)
among eligible creatinine-recovery patients. Fit a prespecified logistic model with restricted cubic splines or carefully bounded linear terms for age, baseline creatinine, AKI stage at t0, peak creatinine, recorded CVP, and observation density, plus sex, admission type, pre-landmark RRT/support and missingness indicators. Standardize predictions over the observed eligible population to obtain RD and percentile/bootstrap confidence intervals. Do not interpret adjustment as causal identification. Sensitivity analyses vary creatinine item (50912 versus 50912+52546), baseline window, urine item set, weight age, urine threshold (including K2-informed lower thresholds), balance scale, exclusion of early dialysis, and complete-case versus explicit missingness handling.

Falsification and integrity checks are prespecified:

- The direction and clinically relevant magnitude must persist across assay, urine-source, baseline, weight, balance and missingness sensitivities to support a reproducible phenotype.
- A null with a confidence interval spanning clinically meaningful harm is inconclusive, not proof of no misclassification.
- If the association disappears after observation-density adjustment or is driven by missing weights/recording intensity, the leading clinical interpretation is not supported.
- A model using post-tL measurements, outcome proxies, or cross-patient leakage fails.
- A positive adjusted association does not establish hemodilution, congestion, intrinsic tubular injury, treatment effect or mechanism.

## Baseline versus substantive learned alternative

The simple baseline is the primary scientific analysis: fixed tL summaries of creatinine peak/slope, urine rate, net balance, weight, CVP, support/RRT, observation counts and missingness, fit with standardized logistic risk. It preserves interpretability and directly estimates the phenotype contrast.

The learned alternative is a masked temporal model over 6-hour bins from t0-24h through tL. Each bin includes creatinine, urine volume/rate, input/output volume, weight, CVP, RRT/support indicators and missingness/measurement-count channels. It targets the same Y7d outcome and uses patient-level 70/15/15 train/validation/test splits; all stays from a subject remain in one split. Compare calibration slope/intercept, Brier score, AUROC and held-out standardized phenotype contrast, with bootstrap uncertainty. A sequence can reveal whether the order and joint trajectory of creatinine, urine and balance contain information lost by the fixed-window baseline. It cannot identify mechanism.

Selection/deferral: retain the baseline as primary even if the learned model predicts better. Fit the learned model only if both phenotype cells have adequate event support and repeated measurements are sufficient; otherwise defer it. Revisit the learned branch only if it improves calibration or reveals a robust trajectory interaction replicated in held-out data, not for a small AUROC gain. GPU use is optional. A CPU tabular/sequence fit is expected to be feasible; the larger learned run is an unverified estimate of 4-16 CPU cores, 16-64 GB RAM, and 1-6 hours, or one allocated A100 for 1-3 hours if sequence batching is the bottleneck. These are planning estimates, not measured episode results. The solver envelope is 16 CPUs, 262144 MiB, up to 8 GPUs and 28,800 seconds; discovery itself used no GPU and did not train a model.

## Interpretation

Supportive result: a stable, clinically nontrivial excess 7-day risk in discordant recovery, with adequate cell support and calibration, would justify prospective validation of enhanced renal monitoring and an adjudicated study with measured GFR/biomarkers. It would still be a prognostic association.

Adverse result: no excess risk, reversal, or disappearance after adjusting observation intensity would weaken the claim that creatinine-only recovery identifies a clinically important discordant state and would redirect work toward other recovery measures. It would not prove creatinine is valid or that fluid/urine management is harmless.

Inconclusive result: sparse cells, wide intervals, unstable thresholds, or substantial unmeasured missingness would mean the available MIMIC data cannot resolve the question. It would justify a measurement study, not a favorable conclusion.

The configured data cannot adjudicate true measured GFR, cystatin-C discordance, tubular injury, true total-body volume, clinician intent, goals of care, complete urine collection, reliable pre-ICU baseline kidney function, or causal treatment effects. Those require additional biomarker/physiology data, chart adjudication, prospective monitoring, or external validation.

## Disposition of demonstrations and unused seed directions

- Delphi-2M/natural-history: inspected article text and methods guidance. A structured temporal model is a useful methodological analogue, but its UKB/Danish longitudinal population and disease-token task are not a reproduction target here; this proposal adapts only the idea that ordering can be tested against a fixed summary baseline.
- Oncoformer/cancer: only the supplementary material was available; the main article and complete STAR Methods were not inspected. Its chest-X-ray modality is unavailable in this MIMIC snapshot, so no multimodal claim is pursued. A lab/time-series adaptation would be a different question and is deferred.
- ALADYNOULLI/Bayesian: inspected article text and methods guidance. Its genetics, multi-biobank signatures and latent disease-hazard objective are not available or necessary for this acute ICU question; a latent trajectory model would not distinguish the proposed clinical rival better than the predeclared masked sequence alternative, so it is deferred.
- Other imported MIMIC seeds (asynchronous organ recovery, diuretic timing, antimicrobial de-escalation, glucose stress, sedation, lactate, transfusion, discharge instability and congestion) remain context. This episode selects AKI recovery because the exact creatinine/urine/fluid bindings and a non-causal falsifiable comparison are strongest. The antimicrobial and diuretic seeds need treatment-confounding and source-control adjudication; the cystatin/measured-GFR dependency in the AKI seed is unavailable but does not block this bounded prognostic adaptation.

# Discordant kidney recovery after ICU AKI

This is a readiness-mode Harbor research task. The proposal is not an executed result. The
solver must newly construct the cohort, fit the prespecified analyses, quantify uncertainty,
and write computed outputs. A readiness pass, a favorable coefficient, or a prediction
score alone is not completion.

## Scientific question and hypothesis

After an ICU patient develops creatinine-defined AKI, is a fall in serum creatinine an
unsafe recovery signal when urine output and recorded fluid balance do not improve at the
same time? Among adults with a first eligible ICU stay who develop creatinine-defined AKI,
survive and remain in the ICU to a fixed 48-hour post-onset landmark, and have a
prespecified creatinine fall, the hypothesis is that patients with low urine output or
positive net fluid balance at the landmark have higher 7-day risk of hospital death or new
kidney-replacement therapy than patients with both urine recovery and non-positive fluid
balance. The primary estimand is the standardized prognostic risk difference, discordant
minus concordant recovery.

This is an association hypothesis. It does not claim that discordance causes harm, proves
hemodilution/congestion/tubular injury, identifies measured persistent renal dysfunction,
or defines a treatment threshold. A result could motivate prospective monitoring and
measurement validation; it is not a bedside rule.

The strongest inspected background evidence supports only bounded propositions: creatinine
can overestimate measured kidney function during prolonged critical illness in association
with muscle loss [K1]; urine-output thresholds and their time windows can change prognostic
discrimination when combined with creatinine, including in MIMIC-IV, but that work addresses
AKI staging rather than recovery discordance [K2]; and positive fluid balance around ICU
AKI is associated with AKI and mortality in an external prospective cohort, with severity
and treatment confounding [K3]. The unresolved claim is whether the prespecified
post-AKI phenotype is a reproducibly higher-risk recovery state in this MIMIC snapshot.
[K1] is abstract-only here, [K2] does not establish mechanism or a treatment threshold,
and [K3] does not study this recovery comparison.

# HCC method exploration: dynamic response versus care-process explanation

Status: working design, verified schema bindings; no scientific result has been computed in this discovery episode.

## Scientific question and deliverable

Among HCC patients receiving a first recorded transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), does the early post-TACE trajectory of measurable disease/liver-state signals add information about near-term repeat intervention beyond baseline patient severity, or is the apparent signal largely a consequence of observation intensity and clinical workflow?

The falsifiable primary hypothesis is:

> Conditional on pre-TACE severity and treatment history, an early post-TACE state trajectory (paired/serial laboratory change, when observed) predicts 180-day repeat TACE; its incremental association should persist after accounting for observation intensity, whereas a process-only explanation predicts that the association attenuates substantially when laboratory/imaging/encounter frequency is included or time/order is destroyed.

This is not a causal claim that TACE response causes repeat TACE. Repeat TACE is a consequential but imperfect operational endpoint: it may represent residual/recurring disease, planned retreatment, clinician preference, access, or follow-up opportunity. Mortality, progression-free survival, and validated radiologic response are not released as explicit adjudicated outcomes.

The new scientific deliverable is a held-out, patient-level comparison of (i) a pre-specified interpretable severity/process model and (ii) a time-aware learned state/process model, plus calibration, uncertainty, ablations and an observation-process falsification test. Completion requires newly fitted out-of-fold risks and uncertainty intervals, not a proposed architecture alone.

The available evidence supports two narrower claims. A recent retrospective TACE cohort reports prognostic value for baseline and post-treatment AFP-related measures, but it is single-institution and observational ([K1]). HCC response assessment is not reducible to size: mRECIST incorporates viable enhancement/necrosis, and response criteria and imaging appearances have practical limitations ([K2]). A current surveillance review emphasizes that relapse biology is heterogeneous, radiologic relapse can lag behind biology, and biomarkers should be interpreted with imaging and clinical context rather than used as standalone treatment triggers ([K3]).

The unresolved claim is whether a dynamic signal in this local HCC care record reflects patient-state information beyond baseline severity, or instead reflects who gets repeat labs/imaging and therefore has more opportunities both to show a signal and to receive repeat TACE. Resolving this matters because a state signal could justify a risk-adapted early review or trial of intensified surveillance; a process signal would caution against using the apparent biomarker trajectory as a treatment trigger and would instead identify a measurement/workflow problem. The result would advance beyond existing retrospective prognostic associations by explicitly testing the competing observation-process explanation with time-preserving and process-permuted comparisons.

Each token carries event type, assay/procedure/modality category, numeric value only when assay identity and unit-safe representation are verified, qualitative result, time since prior event, time since index TACE, and missingness. Use two explicit channels: state channel (baseline/dynamic labs, diagnoses, procedures) and process channel (encounter/test/order/medication observation marks). The target is the same repeat-TACE outcome and the same optional discrete-time hazard.

1. state-only sequence;
2. process-only sequence;
3. combined state+process sequence;
4. combined sequence with response-window event times permuted within patient or process marks permuted across patients, preserving counts;
5. a time-shuffled baseline-feature control.

Evaluate on an untouched patient-level 20% test split; choose hyperparameters only in the remaining 80% with five-fold grouped validation. Use three fixed random seeds and report mean plus seed range; bootstrap patients for 95% intervals on Brier, calibration, AUROC/AUPRC and incremental held-out log loss. Adverse result: B0 performs comparably, or the state increment disappears after B1, or process-only/permuted observation marks reproduce the gain. Interpretation: the apparent signal is more consistent with baseline severity or care-process/measurement artifact; do not recommend response-triggered management.

Inconclusive result: too few paired AFP/liver-state observations, too few repeat TACE events, unstable alias mapping, wide intervals, large missingness, or nontransportable local procedure coding. Interpretation: not a refutation; defer clinical use and specify the missing data/adjudication needed.

DOI 10.4251/wjgo.v17.i6.103198; PMCID PMC12179965. Full XML and public HTML excerpt inspected. It supports the relevance of AFP/biomarker prognostic association after TACE; it does not resolve dynamic response versus observation process and remains retrospective/single-institution with residual confounding.

DOI 10.3390/cancers17010101; PMCID PMC11719590. Full XML and public HTML excerpt inspected. ## Scientific deliverable and the unresolved claim

The deliverable is newly fitted, uncertainty-quantified evidence for one prespecified contrast and one bounded learned comparator:

1. An interpretable cause-specific competing-risk analysis estimating the CRC-versus-hematologic difference in association for CBC discordance.
2. A learned discrete-time multi-task competing-risk model fitted on the same CBC observations to test whether nonlinear interactions and temporal risk shape contain information lost by the linear contrast model.
3. Held-out predictions, cumulative-incidence/calibration outputs, coefficient or feature-effect summaries, and falsification results. A small predictive improvement alone is not a scientific conclusion.

The primary estimand is the difference between the CRC and hematologic cause-specific log-hazard coefficients for the pre-specified haemoglobin/platelet discordance contrast, among participants cancer-free at the second CBC and alive/event-free at a two-year delayed entry. The primary follow-up window is from 2 through 7 years after the second CBC assessment; 0–2 years is a prespecified near-diagnostic sensitivity window, and 7–10 years is exploratory if administrative follow-up supports it.

1. Require nonmissing `eid`, `53-0.0`, `53-1.0`, all eight primary CBC values at instances 0 and 1, and `53-1.0 > 53-0.0`. Record the assessment gap; do not silently treat a missing value as zero.

5. For each participant, the first post-entry event is CRC, hematologic cancer, other cancer, death, or censoring. Use age, sex, BMI, smoking, CRP, CBC assessment gap, and the corresponding baseline date year as prespecified adjustment variables. No outcome-guided thresholds, post-landmark labs, or field selection is allowed.

## Participant-level temporal split

Sort eligible participants by (T_1), preserving participant rows intact. Use the earliest 70% of landmark dates for development and the latest 30% for the final held-out test. Within the development period, use rolling participant-level folds for feature preprocessing, hyperparameter selection and out-of-fold calibration. No person contributes to both sides, and no cancer date, normalization statistic, imputation value, or tuning choice from the held-out period is used during fitting. If either held-out target event has fewer than 100 events, report the learned model as an imprecise feasibility result rather than replacing the temporal split with a random split.

## Method A: transparent baseline

Fit two cause-specific Cox models, one for CRC and one for hematologic cancer, with the same covariates and (D_{HP}), (D_{ML}), CBC levels and changes. Use penalized partial likelihood only if separation or convergence requires it, with the penalty and convergence status recorded. The primary test is the cause-by-(D_{HP}) interaction, equivalently the difference between the two cause-specific coefficients. Report hazard ratios, the CRC-minus-hematologic coefficient difference, robust 95% confidence intervals, and Schoenfeld/time-varying-effect diagnostics.

As a competing-risk descriptive analysis, estimate 5-year cumulative incidence for each target under Aalen–Johansen with other cancer and death as competing events. A Fine–Gray subdistribution analysis is secondary and must not replace the cause-specific estimand. Compare the pre-specified discordance groups only for illustration; the primary inference remains continuous and prespecified.

This baseline answers the explanatory question directly: is the same measured CBC discordance associated differently with the two cancer types after adjustment? It loses nonlinear thresholds, interactions (for example, a platelet rise that matters only at low haemoglobin), and patient-specific risk trajectories.

## Method B: substantive learned alternative

Fit a CPU gradient-boosted discrete-time multi-task competing-risk model using the identical eligible participants and the same raw information: the eight CBC levels at instances 0 and 1, their four changes, assessment gap, CRP baseline/change when available, age, sex, BMI, smoking and landmark year. Do not give it cancer dates or any post-landmark variable.

Expand each participant into one row per one-year interval from (E) to (T_1+7), stopping at the first event or censoring. The fitting target is a four-class interval outcome conditional on being event-free at interval start: CRC, hematologic cancer, other cancer/death, or no event. Include interval number as a feature so the model estimates time-varying hazards. Use a fixed, modest HistGradientBoostingClassifier or equivalent gradient-boosted tree implementation, with hyperparameters selected by rolling development folds. Derive target-specific cumulative-incidence predictions from the predicted interval hazards, accounting for the competing event class.

The learned alternative is scientifically substantive because it can reveal whether the baseline’s linear contrast is an inadequate summary: nonlinear CBC ranges, interactions among all four cell lines, and different time profiles for CRC versus hematologic cancer. It is not a mechanism detector. Use permutation/SHAP-style summaries only as descriptive evidence, computed without looking at the held-out outcomes when defining the model.

Compare three nested information sets on the same held-out participants:

- (M_0): age, sex, BMI, smoking, CRP, gap and landmark year.
- (M_A): (M_0) plus the pre-specified CBC levels, changes and contrasts in the cause-specific baseline.
- (M_B): (M_0) plus the identical raw CBC levels and changes in the learned model.

The substantive comparison is (M_B) versus (M_A) for target-specific calibration and cumulative-incidence log score/Brier score at 2 and 5 years after delayed entry, with time-dependent AUC or Uno C-index reported secondarily. Require calibration intercept/slope, observed-versus-predicted cumulative incidence, and bootstrap 95% intervals from participant-resampled held-out predictions. A small AUC gain without better calibration or a more informative discordance pattern is not a reason to prefer B.

## Falsification and interpretation

The study is supportive only if the primary held-out or full-development association has the prespecified direction—larger (D_{HP}) relatively more CRC-associated than hematologic cancer—and the CRC-versus-hematologic coefficient difference is not explained solely by the 0–2-year window. A supportive learned result additionally requires stable target-specific calibration and a reproducible nonlinear or interaction pattern across development folds, not merely a small discrimination increase.

Adverse evidence is any of the following: the interaction is directionally reversed with a confidence interval excluding the prespecified direction; the difference disappears after the two-year delayed-entry rule; the same CBC pattern predicts other cancers similarly, eliminating type specificity; or the learned model’s apparent advantage disappears on the temporal holdout with poor calibration. These outcomes revise or abandon the discordance interpretation while leaving open simpler descriptive associations.

Inconclusive evidence includes wide intervals from sparse held-out hematologic events, unstable results across the instance-0/1 versus instance-0/2 sensitivity cohorts, or acceptable discrimination with poor calibration. It supports more data or adjudication, not a positive hypothesis claim.

Checks that must be run without favorable-result peeking:

- Report 0–2, 2–7 and available 7–10-year windows separately.
- Repeat with CBC changes adjusted for assessment gap and with winsorization rules fixed before outcome inspection.
- Test the target-specific interaction against other primary cancer codes as a specificity control.
- Permute cancer type within event dates in development as a pipeline negative control; the type interaction should collapse toward zero.
- Compare complete-case participants to the full two-assessment eligibility denominator and report selection; do not impute missing CBC as normal.
- Verify paired date/code alignment and audit duplicate or implausible dates before event derivation.

## Resources and method decision

The discovery audit used short CPU scans: reading the Parquet schema took about 4 seconds and reading the selected CBC/outcome columns took about 6–7 seconds in the ordinary shell; full model fitting and bootstrap uncertainty are not measured. The configured discovery budget is 2 concurrent jobs, 2 GPU slots and 9,000 science seconds. The future solver planning envelope is 16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB, up to 8 GPUs and 28,800 seconds. This proposal requests CPU execution for both methods: 8–16 CPUs and approximately 32–64 GiB for feature construction and fitting, with 2–4 hours for the complete baseline, gradient-boosted model, rolling development folds and 200–500 participant bootstrap replicates. GPU use is unnecessary for the proposed HistGradientBoosting model; a GPU would be considered only if a solver substitutes a documented model after a bounded feasibility measurement. These are planning estimates, not completed study results.

The baseline is selected as the primary scientific method because its estimand and uncertainty map directly onto the competing explanations and can be audited by clinicians. Method B is retained as a prespecified substantive challenge, not as an automatic winner. A latent Gaussian-process/state model or transformer is deferred: the verified cohort has only two broadly complete CBC assessments (instance 2 has 5,862 complete rows), no dense serial laboratory history for most participants, and no verified genetic requirement for this question. Those methods could be revisited if a later source supplies repeated dates and adequate outcome support; complexity alone is not a reason to use them.

## Evidence and clinical limits

The strongest inspected evidence supports only narrower claims. [K1] shows that anaemia is clinically useful for near-diagnostic CRC risk in primary care, but it is static and CRC-only. [K2] reports that longitudinal CBC changes can precede metastatic CRC phenotype in a retrospective Spanish CRC cohort, while explicitly requiring prospective external validation. [K3] bounds RDW interpretation: its meta-analysis concerns mostly retrospective, post-diagnosis CRC prognosis and reports heterogeneous timing and thresholds. None establishes that repeated pre-diagnostic CBC discordance distinguishes incident CRC from hematologic malignancy.

The unresolved clinical question is therefore whether a relative platelet rise with haemoglobin decline (and, separately, broader multi-lineage instability) has a reproducibly different association with future CRC versus hematologic cancer after a cancer-free second CBC and a two-year delayed-entry stress test. A supportive result would establish a descriptive, temporally ordered, cancer-type-specific association worth external validation; it would not identify occult bleeding, inflammation, nutrition, clonal haematopoiesis, or a treatment target. An adverse result would narrow the claim to generic CBC/cancer association; an inconclusive result would motivate a larger clinical cohort, not a positive conclusion.

The UKB registry fields do not provide pathology adjudication, iron/ferritin or reticulocyte studies, peripheral smear, marrow studies, FIT/colonoscopy findings, cancer stage, symptoms, infection timing, medications, transfusions, or treatment. Therefore no result can distinguish occult bleeding from inflammation, nutrition, clonal haematopoiesis, reverse causation or healthcare-use/measurement selection. Clinical action would require expert review of code definitions and CBC measurement quality, external validation in a clinical population, and a prospective study linked to diagnostic outcomes. An automated verifier can check the data binding, derived outputs, split, uncertainty and whether conclusions match those outputs; it cannot establish the missing clinical mechanism or clinical utility.

Supporting evidence files are `work/evidence/K1_hamilton_2008_excerpt.txt`, `work/evidence/K2_sala_2026_excerpt.txt`, `work/evidence/K3_fan_2026_abstract_excerpt.txt`, and `work/final/key-references.json`.

# Patient-state versus hospital-documentation signal in eICU testing-process transportability

Status: proposed child of assessed valid candidate-c4d797691f426d15f53aea99. No fitted study result is claimed. The bounded prefix diagnostic is recorded separately as observed feasibility evidence.

## Scientific opening and unresolved claim

The parent establishes a useful but incomplete comparison: a value-only model versus the same nonlinear learner augmented with early laboratory-result presence, count, and timing. A larger internal-to-hospital-held-out loss for the augmented model would be consistent with workflow dependence, but it would not distinguish a hospital/documentation shortcut from ordinary case-mix or an unmeasured severity signal. The available evidence supports three narrower premises: rich EHR representations can predict mortality across centers [K1]; the presence and timing of EHR measurements can be predictive and can shift across settings [K2]; and external mortality models can retain discrimination while local data patterns affect calibration and adaptation [K3]. None establishes the unresolved patient-state/documentation distinction in eICU.

Leading explanation: patient-level process features (what was recorded, how often, and when) partly encode hospital-specific testing and documentation practice. They will show excess internal-to-hospital-held-out degradation, especially in calibration and decision utility; a within-hospital process-permutation negative control will preserve the hospital's process distribution but remove patient alignment, exposing any residual site/workflow signature.

Strong rival: process features are stable proxies for latent acuity or care intensity not captured by the observed laboratory values. In that case the aligned process model should retain incremental held-out discrimination/calibration, and within-hospital permutation should remove its incremental patient-level signal. A second rival is selection: conditioning on stays observed beyond six hours and on hospitals meeting the size threshold may change the case mix. The design reports this conditioning explicitly, uses only outcome-independent hospital eligibility, and does not interpret a residual association as causal.

### Falsifiable hypothesis

Among adult first eligible ICU stays with one unique patient stay, under observation beyond 6 hours, the process-aware model has a larger internal-to-hospital-held-out deterioration than the value-only model. The sharpened claim is that this excess deterioration is documentation/workflow-consistent if all of the following prespecified patterns occur:

1. aligned VP-GBM has positive paired excess deterioration in AUROC, Brier score, or absolute calibration-slope error, with the corresponding 95% hospital-cluster bootstrap interval excluding zero in at least one primary metric;
2. VP-GBM has lower held-out decision-curve net benefit at at least two of fixed 5%, 10%, and 20% thresholds, and this is not explained by an adverse value-only calibration pattern;
3. a within-hospital permuted-process negative-control model retains more of the internal advantage than the aligned-process model but loses it on held-out hospitals, or otherwise shows a larger internal-to-held-out gap. This pattern indicates that hospital/process distribution alone can create a transport penalty. If permutation collapses both performance and degradation to V-GBM, the patient-state rival is strengthened and the workflow interpretation is not supported.

The parent-level hypothesis is falsified when aligned VP-GBM is no less transportable than V-GBM with no adverse calibration or utility pattern. The sharpened documentation interpretation is falsified when the aligned process model retains held-out incremental value and the permuted-process model does not show a transport penalty. Discordant or imprecise results are inconclusive, not evidence for either mechanism.

This is a descriptive prognostic transportability estimand, not a causal effect of ordering or documenting a test. It cannot establish that changing testing changes mortality.

## Clinical importance and advance

If a model depends on local recording practice, an apparently safe mortality score can mis-rank patients or misstate absolute risk after deployment. A documentation-consistent result would justify omitting process features, requiring site validation/recalibration, or harmonizing laboratory feeds before a silent prospective evaluation. A patient-state-consistent result would justify retaining process information only with external validation and measurement review; it would not make testing an intervention.

The substantive advance over the parent is a testable decomposition of the process signal. The aligned-versus-within-hospital-permuted contrast preserves the same hospital-specific process distributions while breaking patient-level alignment. The time-reversal check preserves the same event set and analyte values while testing whether the result depends on chronology. The future-window check is a deliberate positive leakage control, not a clinical model. These checks separate descriptive patient-aligned information, site-distribution information, and timing artifacts more directly than a single external performance gap.

## Actual scientific deliverable

The solver must newly produce:

- a frozen cohort manifest, repeat-patient exclusions, outcome-independent hospital eligibility, and deterministic hospital folds;
- leakage-safe 0–360 minute patient features and three model prediction sets for every held-out eligible stay: V-Logit, V-GBM, and VP-GBM;
- an additional within-hospital process-permuted VP-GBM diagnostic and a time-reversed process diagnostic, each with exact random seed and permutation manifest;
- a temporal additive model (T-Logit) using three 120-minute bins, to test whether explicit chronology changes the interpretation;
- patient predictions, per-hospital AUROC/AUPRC/Brier/calibration intercept and slope/net benefit, and 2,000-replicate hospital-cluster bootstrap intervals for all prespecified contrasts;
- a report that labels supportive, adverse, and inconclusive outcomes and links each conclusion to computed output files.

Completion is not a favorable result. It requires predictions for all primary models, the permutation/time-shift outputs, the cohort/fold manifest, uncertainty estimates, and an interpretation that does not exceed the estimand.

## Population, time zero, horizon, and outcome

Time zero is ICU admission. eICU offsets are minutes relative to ICU admission. Include rows from the patient table with:

- unitvisitnumber = 1 and unitstaytype = admit;
- age parsed as numeric and age >= 18, retaining the eICU >89 category as adult;
- nonmissing patientunitstayid, hospitalid, uniquepid, unitdischargeoffset, and unitdischargestatus;
- unitdischargeoffset > 360 minutes, not >=360, so the primary cohort is observed beyond the landmark rather than allowing a death/discharge exactly at the boundary.

Exclude duplicate patientunitstayid rows and exclude any uniquepid with more than one otherwise eligible primary stay in the snapshot. The latter is a leakage repair: the source may contain repeated patients across health-system stays or hospitals, and a hospital-held-out split cannot otherwise guarantee that the same de-identified patient is not represented in training and held-out hospitals. Report the count and assess the excluded-repeat cohort descriptively, without reintroducing it to the primary estimand. If uniquepid is not unique/nonmissing as required, stop and report infeasibility rather than silently reverting to stay-level splitting.

The primary outcome is Y=1 when unitdischargestatus equals Expired and Y=0 for a non-Expired ICU discharge. It is all-cause ICU mortality by the end of the ICU stay, not 24-hour mortality or complete hospital mortality. The estimand is conditional on this cohort being under ICU observation beyond 360 minutes. unitdischargeoffset and unitdischargestatus are eligibility/label fields only and never predictors. Compare the discharge-status label descriptively with apachePatientResult.actualicumortality by patientunitstayid; do not replace the primary label or use any Apache field as a feature. A discordance audit cannot resolve the absence of a death timestamp.

All four configured sources are read-only ordinary gzip CSV files; no archive member is used.

1. Patient anchor: source path [private-path]/EICU 2.0数据/patient.csv.gz; catalog source SHA-256 2acf25f75144c5fc8a2a5b68c6741edac2dc7ca51021127f73e12f7428dc392b; table JSON datasets/eicu/table-ab037c09d7df9a3c.json; schema SHA-256 f354ea972ab3b4efa81556a02963dee7d9e2ccb0ab23cacb309059132e94b5a7. 2. Hospital/site: source path [private-path]/EICU 2.0数据/hospital.csv.gz; catalog SHA-256 16684f45680921fb263fdd057ac9217093a9e81fc663228480e0d6a4665390a6; table JSON datasets/eicu/table-811df7b2ef435e12.json; schema SHA-256 336091a45944fb9d4c39ec6b30af67e472b221df8877f9c555e3b444e1212811. Columns hospitalid, numbedscategory, teachingstatus, region. Join only patient.hospitalid=hospital.hospitalid. Site columns are eligibility/stratification/reporting only, never predictors.

3. Laboratory events: source path [private-path]/EICU 2.0数据/lab.csv.gz; catalog SHA-256 91b55ed330015d31c424499cdae3b68e3b4cfe0c10e542548b5461520d93bc7a; table JSON datasets/eicu/table-79bdb33275339b1a.json; schema SHA-256 41b0cab77ecab75bb9746fd44812c7a574196be60bfdce26835f9805ae2c6925.
