## Features, folds, and leakage controls

Retain hospitals with at least 100 eligible primary-cohort stays, using no outcome or laboratory feature; require at least five hospitals. Sort hospital IDs by SHA-256 of UTF-8 eicu-transport-v2 + NUL + hospitalid and assign contiguous hospitals to five folds by greedy eligible-stay balancing. All stays from a hospital remain in one outer fold.

Within each outer training set, select a deterministic patient-grouped 20% reference by uniquepid hash, with hospital representation and outcome strata only to stabilize prevalence; fit on the remaining 80%. Reference labels are not used in fitting, selection, threshold choice, or calibration. Record any deterministic small-cell merge and stop if the split cannot be formed.

Select up to 30 analyte keys by distinct development-stay coverage, requiring >=1% development-stay coverage. If fewer qualify retain all and report the number. Repeat selection separately in each outer fold using only development rows. V features are age, gender, ethnicity, admissionweight and latest finite value per selected analyte in [0,360]. Impute missing values with development-fold medians and learn unknown category levels in development. P features are per-analyte presence, valid-result count, distinct-result-offset count, first/last valid-result offsets, overall valid-lab row count and overall distinct-offset count. P describes observed recording/measurement, not confirmed orders. No identifier, hospital/site field, discharge field, Apache field, diagnosis, note, treatment, or post-landmark event enters a model matrix.

T features use [0,120], (120,240], (240,360] and per analyte/bin last value, presence and valid-result count plus static predictors, with the same revision rule and development-only preprocessing.

For stays with unitdischargeoffset>720, a separate positive leakage audit may form a 360–720-minute P vector from labresultoffset in (360,720] and revision offset <=720. It never enters primary fitting, predictions, metrics, bootstrap or interpretation; any appearance in primary matrices is a readiness failure.

## Models, estimands, uncertainty, and outputs

V-Logit is fixed elastic-net logistic regression on V. V-GBM is a fixed histogram gradient-boosting classifier on V. VP-GBM is the identical learner, seed, preprocessing, class-weight policy and fixed hyperparameters on V+P. The primary process comparison is VP-GBM versus V-GBM. T-Logit is the prespecified temporal alternative.

Fit each model on the 80% development portion and predict both reference and held-out hospitals. No held-out metric selects a model or threshold. Define D_AUC(m)=AUROC_internal−AUROC_external; D_Brier(m)=Brier_external−Brier_internal; and D_slope(m)=absolute calibration-slope error_external−absolute calibration-slope error_internal. The main contrast is D_AUC(VP-GBM)−D_AUC(V-GBM); Brier, slope and policy-scenario net-benefit contrasts are secondary. Report direct held-out VP-GBM−V-GBM metrics and per-hospital paired values. Compute AUROC, AUPRC, Brier, calibration intercept/slope, reliability without site recalibration, and net benefit at 0.05/0.10/0.20. Use 2,000 hospital-cluster bootstrap replicates over paired hospital-level prediction contributions and report effective hospital counts; patient bootstrap alone is insufficient.

Unconditioned P permutation permutes complete P vectors within hospital in each development set, fits the same VP-GBM, and independently permutes P within hospital for reference/external prediction using recorded seeds/manifests. State-matched P permutation uses development-derived V-GBM risk-score quintiles; permute within hospital-by-bin cells, merge cells under 10 only by a fixed adjacent-bin rule, and independently apply the same rule without labels to reference/external hospitals. Time reversal replaces each event offset t with 360−t before first/last and T features, preserving analytes, values, revisions and counts; refit/predict without retuning.

The solver must output a frozen cohort/fold/development-reference manifest; V/P/V+P/T features; predictions for V-Logit, V-GBM, VP-GBM, T-Logit, both permutation controls and time reversal; seeds/manifests; prohibited-field/future-window audit; per-hospital metrics; bootstrap intervals; calibration and policy-scenario net-benefit tables; and an interpretation report linking every conclusion to exact computed outputs. Completion is these outputs with uncertainty, not a favorable result.

## Interpretation and unavailable evidence

Supportive of a documentation/workflow-consistent liability requires: positive primary process deterioration with a 95% cluster interval excluding zero in at least one primary metric; worse held-out calibration or net benefit for aligned VP-GBM at at least two policy thresholds; no equally large value-only deterioration; and state-matched permuted-P retaining a material development process signal or transport penalty while exact patient alignment is broken, without the pattern being solely time-reversal. This means only that observed process signals are transportability liabilities consistent with documentation dependence.

Adverse: aligned VP-GBM retains held-out incremental value and state-matched permutation collapses to V-GBM; this favors patient-aligned information or another explanation, not proof of biological stability. Inconclusive: intervals span zero, too few hospitals/events, unstable repeat exclusion or analyte selection, equal value-only deterioration, discordant controls, or incompatible discrimination/calibration/threshold patterns. A wide interval is imprecision, not refutation. Conclusions must cite prediction, metrics and bootstrap files; readiness is not evidence.

Unavailable evidence includes orders/cancellations, specimen collection time, interface outages, clinician rationale, unmeasured bedside acuity, care pathways, end-of-life decisions, death timestamp and complete narrative notes. Hospital-held-out folds do not randomize practice or eliminate case mix, severity, selection or measurement bias. Clinical adjudication, external order/interface data, prospective silent deployment and impact evaluation are needed for workflow, causal or clinical-benefit claims.

## Methods, compute, and alternatives

The selected study is CPU tabular. Readiness is one fold first, then plan 16 CPUs and 128–256 GiB within the 28,800-second/16-CPU solver envelope. Streaming the 516 MB compressed lab source, five outer fits, controls and manifests is estimated at 2–8 hours; the full estimate is unverified. Bootstrap replicates do not refit. GPU allocation is available but unnecessary: fixed tabular summaries do not require it and GPU capacity cannot supply absent event semantics.

V-Logit is the simple baseline and loses nonlinear interactions and chronology. VP-GBM is the substantive learned alternative with identical target/split/uncertainty; its information gain is value-by-process interaction, not a leaderboard gain. T-Logit uses explicit early/late bins with identical target/split/uncertainty and can reveal timing information lost by latest-value summaries at low inspectable cost. A neural event-sequence model is deferred because missing order/specimen/interface/rationale semantics make extra capacity uninformative for the key ambiguity; revisit only if T-Logit and time reversal show reproducible chronology and one-fold readiness shows adequate events per hospital. The detailed comparison and deferral record is method-alternatives.md. No model result is claimed.

## Three inspected key works

[K1] Rajkomar et al. supports multi-center EHR mortality prediction and sequential representations, but not a laboratory-process mechanism. This proposal adds a hospital-held-out value/process ablation and falsification controls.

[K2] Gao et al. supports predictive missingness and transport risk from shifted EHR patterns, but is abstract-only and single-institution CLABSI work. This proposal tests the analogous eICU ICU-mortality question with state-matched permutation.

[K3] Hadler et al. supports the deployment importance of external calibration and data availability, but does not isolate workflow from patient state or case mix. This proposal makes that decomposition explicit while retaining an observational transport estimand.

# Episode 2 alternative direction: first-CBC cancer-type signal versus repeat-measurement selection

Status: independent UKB branch; proposed experiment, not an executed result  
Parent context: candidate-d7fca3b251a02a70358d2876  
Expert seed: expert-20261002-ukb-23, references/expert-seeds/cards/ukb-23.md (feasibility_required)  
Dataset snapshot: ukb-completed-subset-20261002

## Question and clinical importance

The seed and parent ask whether haemoglobin falling while platelets rise is more CRC-like than hematologic-cancer-like, whereas broader multi-lineage abnormality may be more hematologic. The parent correctly makes a second-CBC landmark and two-year delayed entry central. The unresolved problem is that a second CBC in UK Biobank is not a routine clinical repeat process: it selects people who survived, remained cancer-free, attended another assessment and were not lost to follow-up. The apparent longitudinal contrast could therefore combine biology, timing and observation selection.

This branch asks:

> Among adults with a complete first CBC and no registered cancer at that first assessment, does a first-CBC phenotype provide a reproducible CRC-versus-hematologic cancer contrast, and does the corresponding second-CBC change contrast persist after an explicit repeat-observation stress test and across near-diagnostic versus longer-latency windows?

This could change the next clinical-research decision. A signal already present at the first CBC and stable after the repeat check would justify external validation of whether one CBC can prioritize CRC-oriented versus hematology-oriented evaluation. A signal only after the selectively observed second CBC, or only in the 0--2-year window, should be treated as timing/selection evidence rather than a longitudinal clinical rule.

The hypothesis is descriptive and predictive, not causal. It does not claim occult bleeding, inflammation, nutritional deficiency, clonal haematopoiesis, or treatment benefit.

## Evidence and unresolved claim

[K1] Hamilton et al. found clinically relevant near-diagnostic information in haemoglobin/anaemia for CRC in UK primary care, with risk varying by haemoglobin, age and sex. It is CRC-only case-control evidence and does not establish a repeated-CBC or CRC-versus-hematologic contrast.

[K2] Sala et al. reported pre-diagnostic CBC trajectories up to 24 months before CRC diagnosis, including haemoglobin decline and inflammatory-index increases associated with metastatic presentation. It is a retrospective CRC-only Spanish cohort and calls for independent validation; it does not test cancer-type specificity or selective observation.

[K3] Hampton et al.'s systematic review found that CRC models can discriminate but often have incomplete calibration and limited validation. That supports temporal holdout, calibration and decision restraint here; it is not evidence that the UKB contrast is clinically useful.

The strongest supported claim is that haemoglobin and longitudinal CBC measures can associate with CRC-related outcomes in selected datasets. The unresolved claim is that the platelet-versus-haemoglobin pattern differs between CRC and hematologic cancer in a first-CBC population and that its repeat-derived version is not created by repeat selection or a near-diagnostic window.

## Exact data binding

All analysis uses one read-only UKB table and no joins.

- Catalog table: datasets/ukb/table-5d49a6760e7ffdbd.json, named ukb671626.csv (Parquet).
- Convenience source: [private-path]/ukb_483356f97e1e8132.parquet.
- Original lineage: [private-path]/ukb671626.csv.
- Source IDs: ukb_483356f97e1e8132 and ukb_483356f97e1e8132_parquet.
- Parquet SHA-256: a7c03cf84cd951dec9fa013ae76e6e1a363f579506886f59a0f179beae15e23a.
- Archive member: ordinary file; no extraction.
- Rows: 502,371. Key: eid. Identifier namespace: ukb671626.

datasets/README.md documents the four configured dataset families (HCC, MIMIC, EICU and UKB). The other three remain available read-only but are not needed here. No eid is joined to ukb672073, dta, olink or any other namespace.

Required fields:

- Assessment dates: 53-0.0, 53-1.0, 53-2.0. The Parquet physical type is string; parse valid ISO dates explicitly and treat missing/invalid values as missing.
- CBC: 30000-{0,1,2}.0 WBC; 30020-{0,1,2}.0 haemoglobin; 30070-{0,1,2}.0 RDW; 30080-{0,1,2}.0 platelets.
- Covariates: 31-0.0 sex; 21003-0.0 age; 21001-0.0 BMI; 20116-0.0 smoking; 30710-0.0 CRP; first-assessment calendar year derived from 53-0.0.
- Registry pairs: 40005-{0..21}.0 cancer date with same-index 40006-{0..21}.0 ICD-10 code. Pair indices exactly; take the earliest valid qualifying date.
- Death: 40000-0.0. Retain 40001-0.0 only for audit; do not infer cancer type from it.

A bounded selected-column audit found 478,033 complete first CBCs, 19,409 complete second CBCs, 5,862 complete third CBCs and 18,377 valid complete first/second pairs. The required columns were physically present and typed as strings. After excluding any cancer on/before the first date, the first-CBC eligible count was 439,735. Planned event derivation found 750 CRC and 525 hematologic events in the first-CBC 0--2-year window and 44 CRC and 27 hematologic events in the clean repeat-landmark 0--2-year window. These are audit counts, not fitted results; the repeat hematologic count is a hard precision warning.

## Population, timing and outcomes

### First-CBC population

Include nonmissing eid, 53-0.0, and all four instance-0 CBC values, with parseable first date T0. Exclude anyone with any qualifying cancer date on or before T0. Do not require a repeat CBC.

Primary follow-up starts at T0 and ends at the first event, T0+2 years, or 2022-12-31. Secondary follow-up is T0+2 through T0+5, with the same fixed administrative boundary. Death is competing. The first post-T0 event is CRC, hematologic cancer, other primary cancer, death or censoring.

### Repeat landmark

R=1 when 53-1.0 is parseable, strictly later than T0, and all four instance-1 CBC values are nonmissing. R=0 is otherwise eligible at first CBC. R is defined without future outcomes.

For the repeat analysis require R=1, no qualifying cancer on/before T1=53-1.0, and no death on/before T1. Follow from T1 to T1+2 and then T1+5. This is explicitly conditional on being re-observed and event-free, not a recovered version of the first-CBC estimand.

### Features

Within each development split, standardize each CBC variable using instance-0 development means and standard deviations, separately by sex or with sex as a prespecified covariate. Apply those quantities to instances 1 and 2.

First-CBC features are z_WBC0, z_Hb0, z_RDW0 and z_platelet0. The prespecified platelet-haemoglobin contrast is the CRC-minus-hematologic coefficient contrast beta_platelet0 - beta_Hb0; positive means relatively higher platelets/lower haemoglobin is more CRC-associated.

Repeat features are the four baseline z values and d_j=z_j,1-z_j,0 for each cell line. The primary repeat contrast is beta_d_platelet - beta_d_Hb. A secondary fixed instability summary is D_ML=mean(abs(d_WBC), abs(d_Hb), abs(d_RDW), abs(d_platelet)). Do not include all four changes and D_HP=d_platelet-d_Hb as separate linear predictors: they are collinear. Include T1-T0 as a covariate and report its distribution. CRP 30710-1.0 is sensitivity-only.

Cancer classes are CRC C18/C19/C20; hematologic C81--C96; other primary malignant C00--C97 excluding those families and secondary C77--C79. C77--C79 are not primary target events. Take the earliest event across cancer classes and 40000-0.0 death. Report denominators, missingness, gap quantiles, event counts/person-time and exclusions before each landmark.

## Selection and timing estimands

The first-CBC estimand is the cause-specific CRC-versus-hematologic coefficient contrast for the platelet and haemoglobin baseline terms in all first-CBC-eligible adults. Its 0--2-year version is near-diagnostic; 2--5 tests persistence beyond likely work-up.

The repeat estimand is the corresponding contrast for the four change coefficients in the T1 landmark. Fit unweighted and with stabilized inverse-probability-of-repeat weights. Estimate P(R=1|X0) using only first-CBC information: baseline CBC, sex, age, BMI, smoking, CRP, first-assessment year, and eligibility indicators. Use a numerator based on sex and first-assessment year, trim at fixed 1st/99th percentiles, and report untrimmed sensitivity. Show balance before/after weighting.

Weights address measured baseline predictors of repeat observation only. They cannot repair cancer/death before T1, unmeasured healthcare use, symptoms, treatment, or the fact that 53-1.0 is a research-assessment measurement. The weighted repeat analysis is a selection stress test, not a causal correction.

Prespecify a 0.20 log-hazard equivalence margin (about a 22% hazard-ratio ratio) for weighted-minus-unweighted change. Call measured-selection robustness compatible only if the point change is within the margin and a 90% bootstrap interval is wholly inside it. If sparse events make that impossible, report inconclusive.

## Methods compared before selection

### A. Transparent cause-specific baseline

Fit separate cause-specific Cox models for CRC and hematologic cancer. Other cancer and death are competing events in the risk sets. The first model uses four baseline CBC values plus age, sex, BMI, smoking, CRP and first-assessment year. The repeat model uses the same baseline covariates, four changes and assessment gap, with the repeat weight in the weighted version. Estimate the prespecified CRC-minus-hematologic coefficient contrasts with robust 95% intervals and time-varying-effect diagnostics. Use penalization only for documented separation/convergence failure and record it.

Estimate Aalen--Johansen cumulative incidence at 2 and 5 years for CRC, hematologic cancer, other cancer and death. Fine--Gray can be secondary, never a replacement for the cause-specific estimand. This baseline is primary because the estimand is auditable; it loses nonlinear thresholds, cross-line interactions and time-varying hazards.

### B. Substantive learned alternative

Fit a CPU gradient-boosted discrete-time multi-task competing-risk model using exactly the same eligible people and raw information. Expand each person into yearly intervals from the relevant landmark through event/censoring/horizon. Predict CRC, hematologic cancer and other cancer/death hazards; include interval number. No post-landmark registry field or future CBC may be a predictor.

The first feature set is exactly the baseline feature set. The repeat set is exactly baseline CBC, four changes, gap and covariates. A small fixed grid is tuned in rolling development folds. This alternative can reveal nonlinear cell-line ranges, low-Hb-by-platelet interactions and time-varying type-specific hazards that A loses; it is not a mechanism detector.

Fit the repeat-observation head P(R=1|X0) within each development fold to generate weights. Do not use future R as a first-CBC risk predictor. In the repeat model R=1 defines the conditional population, not a predictor.

Compare B with A on a final temporal holdout using target-specific calibration intercept/slope, calibration plots, 2- and 5-year cumulative-incidence Brier/log scores and participant-bootstrap intervals. Time-dependent AUC/Uno C-index is secondary. A small AUC gain without calibration or a stable cancer-type pattern is not a scientific advance. Feature-effect summaries are descriptive and frozen without test-outcome peeking.

### Split, uncertainty and compute

Sort participants by the relevant landmark date; earliest 70% is development and latest 30% is final test. Participants stay intact. Rolling development folds fit standardization, repeat weights, tuning and calibration. No test outcome, date, normalization, imputation or tuning choice enters fitting. If the held-out hematologic count is below 50, label the learned result imprecise and do not switch to a random split.

Use robust model intervals and 500 participant bootstrap replicates for held-out predictions, weighted estimates and weighted-minus-unweighted differences. Preserve failures and convergence warnings. Complete-case CBC features are required; missing is not normal.

The audit used short CPU scans; full fitting is unmeasured. inputs.json permits up to 16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB, 8 GPUs and 28,800 seconds for the future solver. Request CPU (8--16 CPUs, 32--64 GiB), estimated 2--4 hours. The modest gradient-boosted model does not require GPU; no GPU feasibility claim is made.

## Falsification and interpretation

The primary direction is relatively higher platelets/lower haemoglobin being more CRC-associated. It is a hypothesis, not an observed result.

Supportive evidence requires: (1) the first-CBC contrast has the prespecified direction; (2) repeat change contrast has the same direction unweighted and weighted, with selection change compatible with the margin; (3) the effect is not confined to 0--2 years, or is explicitly labelled near-diagnostic only; (4) learned nonlinear patterns are stable across folds and improve held-out calibration or cumulative-incidence scores; and (5) the contrast is more specific to CRC versus hematologic cancer than to all cancers.

Adverse evidence is a reasonably precise reversal, a large weighted/unweighted change, disappearance after two years, or the same signal for other cancers. That revises/abandons type-specific discordance while leaving generic CBC associations possible.

Inconclusive evidence is fewer than 50 usable held-out hematologic events, an equivalence interval wider than the margin, unstable gap/instance-2 sensitivity, convergence failure, or discrimination without calibration. A wide null does not refute the hypothesis.

Required checks:

- Audit every date/code pair, duplicate rows, implausible dates and fixed administrative censoring.
- Report 0--2 and 2--5 windows; 5--10 is exploratory only.
- Report repeat-gap strata and baseline R=1 versus R=0 balance.
- Use other primary cancers as a specificity control.
- Permute cancer type among development event dates while preserving timing; interaction should collapse toward zero.
- Use instance 2 only as a small sensitivity cohort, not dense trajectory evidence.
- Compare complete-CBC participants with the eligible denominator; never impute missing CBC as normal.

A supportive result establishes only a temporally ordered descriptive association useful for external-validation design. It does not establish diagnostic accuracy in symptomatic patients, a referral threshold, mechanism, stage, treatment benefit or clinical utility. The source lacks ferritin/iron, reticulocytes, FIT, symptoms, medications, transfusion context, smear, marrow studies, pathology adjudication, stage, work-up, lab indication/source and complete healthcare-contact history. 53 is a research assessment date, not a clinical test-order date. Clinical use requires expert code/lab review, external clinical validation and a prospective decision-linked study.

## Alternatives and deliverable

The transparent cause-specific model is selected as primary because it directly tests the claim and is auditable with sparse hematologic events. The gradient-boosted model is retained because it tests substantive nonlinear and time-varying information, not because complexity earns merit. A latent GP/state-space model or transformer is deferred: only two broadly complete CBC assessments exist, instance 2 is small, and repeat-landmark hematologic events are sparse. A first-CBC model using future R is rejected as leakage. Cross-namespace augmentation is rejected because the catalog has distinct namespaces and no authorized crosswalk.

The solver must newly fit/estimate: first-CBC and repeat cause-specific models; unweighted/weighted repeat selection; both temporal-holdout models; competing-risk curves; calibration/Brier/log scores; coefficient contrasts; 500-bootstrap uncertainty; gap/window sensitivities; and the cancer-type permutation negative control. Completion requires cohort/missingness/event tables, selection balance, split manifest, fitted outputs/predictions, uncertainty and a conclusion tied to those outputs. Readiness or a fit alone does not establish the claim.

## Key bibliography

[K2] Sala RJ, Ery J, Cuesta-Peredo D, Muedra V, Rodilla V. Haematological pre-staging of colorectal cancer: Longitudinal trends identify high-risk metastatic phenotypes 24 months prior to diagnosis. Translational Oncology. 2026;72:102954. DOI 10.1016/j.tranon.2026.102954. PMCID PMC13449478.

[K3] Hampton JS, Kenny RPW, Rees CJ, Hamilton W, Eastaugh C, Richmond C, Sharp L, COLOFIT Research Team. DOI 10.1016/j.eclinm.2023.102204. PMCID PMC10541467.

# Episode 2 alternative direction: first-CBC cancer-type signal versus repeat-measurement selection

Status: independent UKB branch; proposed experiment, not an executed result  
Parent context: candidate-d7fca3b251a02a70358d2876  
Expert seed: expert-20261002-ukb-23, references/expert-seeds/cards/ukb-23.md (feasibility_required)  
Dataset snapshot: ukb-completed-subset-20261002

## Question and clinical importance

The seed and parent ask whether haemoglobin falling while platelets rise is more CRC-like than hematologic-cancer-like, whereas broader multi-lineage abnormality may be more hematologic. The parent correctly makes a second-CBC landmark and two-year delayed entry central. The unresolved problem is that a second CBC in UK Biobank is not a routine clinical repeat process: it selects people who survived, remained cancer-free, attended another assessment and were not lost to follow-up. The apparent longitudinal contrast could therefore combine biology, timing and observation selection.

This branch asks:

> Among adults with a complete first CBC and no registered cancer at that first assessment, does a first-CBC phenotype provide a reproducible CRC-versus-hematologic cancer contrast, and does the corresponding second-CBC change contrast persist after an explicit repeat-observation stress test and across near-diagnostic versus longer-latency windows?

This could change the next clinical-research decision. A signal already present at the first CBC and stable after the repeat check would justify external validation of whether one CBC can prioritize CRC-oriented versus hematology-oriented evaluation. A signal only after the selectively observed second CBC, or only in the 0--2-year window, should be treated as timing/selection evidence rather than a longitudinal clinical rule.

The hypothesis is descriptive and predictive, not causal. It does not claim occult bleeding, inflammation, nutritional deficiency, clonal haematopoiesis, or treatment benefit.

## Evidence and unresolved claim

[K1] Hamilton et al. found clinically relevant near-diagnostic information in haemoglobin/anaemia for CRC in UK primary care, with risk varying by haemoglobin, age and sex. It is CRC-only case-control evidence and does not establish a repeated-CBC or CRC-versus-hematologic contrast.

[K2] Sala et al. reported pre-diagnostic CBC trajectories up to 24 months before CRC diagnosis, including haemoglobin decline and inflammatory-index increases associated with metastatic presentation. It is a retrospective CRC-only Spanish cohort and calls for independent validation; it does not test cancer-type specificity or selective observation.

[K3] Hampton et al.'s systematic review found that CRC models can discriminate but often have incomplete calibration and limited validation. That supports temporal holdout, calibration and decision restraint here; it is not evidence that the UKB contrast is clinically useful.

The strongest supported claim is that haemoglobin and longitudinal CBC measures can associate with CRC-related outcomes in selected datasets. The unresolved claim is that the platelet-versus-haemoglobin pattern differs between CRC and hematologic cancer in a first-CBC population and that its repeat-derived version is not created by repeat selection or a near-diagnostic window.

## Exact data binding

All analysis uses one read-only UKB table and no joins.

- Catalog table: datasets/ukb/table-5d49a6760e7ffdbd.json, named ukb671626.csv (Parquet).
- Convenience source: [private-path]/ukb_483356f97e1e8132.parquet.
- Original lineage: [private-path]/ukb671626.csv.
- Source IDs: ukb_483356f97e1e8132 and ukb_483356f97e1e8132_parquet.
- Parquet SHA-256: a7c03cf84cd951dec9fa013ae76e6e1a363f579506886f59a0f179beae15e23a.
- Archive member: ordinary file; no extraction.
- Rows: 502,371. Key: eid. Identifier namespace: ukb671626.

datasets/README.md documents the four configured dataset families (HCC, MIMIC, EICU and UKB). The other three remain available read-only but are not needed here. No eid is joined to ukb672073, dta, olink or any other namespace.

Required fields:

- Assessment dates: 53-0.0, 53-1.0, 53-2.0. The Parquet physical type is string; parse valid ISO dates explicitly and treat missing/invalid values as missing.
- CBC: 30000-{0,1,2}.0 WBC; 30020-{0,1,2}.0 haemoglobin; 30070-{0,1,2}.0 RDW; 30080-{0,1,2}.0 platelets.
- Covariates: 31-0.0 sex; 21003-0.0 age; 21001-0.0 BMI; 20116-0.0 smoking; 30710-0.0 CRP; first-assessment calendar year derived from 53-0.0.
- Registry pairs: 40005-{0..21}.0 cancer date with same-index 40006-{0..21}.0 ICD-10 code. Pair indices exactly; take the earliest valid qualifying date.
- Death: 40000-0.0. Retain 40001-0.0 only for audit; do not infer cancer type from it.

A bounded selected-column audit found 478,033 complete first CBCs, 19,409 complete second CBCs, 5,862 complete third CBCs and 18,377 valid complete first/second pairs. The required columns were physically present and typed as strings. After excluding any cancer on/before the first date, the first-CBC eligible count was 439,735. Planned event derivation found 750 CRC and 525 hematologic events in the first-CBC 0--2-year window and 44 CRC and 27 hematologic events in the clean repeat-landmark 0--2-year window. These are audit counts, not fitted results; the repeat hematologic count is a hard precision warning.

## Population, timing and outcomes

### First-CBC population

Include nonmissing eid, 53-0.0, and all four instance-0 CBC values, with parseable first date T0. Exclude anyone with any qualifying cancer date on or before T0. Do not require a repeat CBC.

Primary follow-up starts at T0 and ends at the first event, T0+2 years, or 2022-12-31. Secondary follow-up is T0+2 through T0+5, with the same fixed administrative boundary. Death is competing. The first post-T0 event is CRC, hematologic cancer, other primary cancer, death or censoring.

### Repeat landmark

R=1 when 53-1.0 is parseable, strictly later than T0, and all four instance-1 CBC values are nonmissing. R=0 is otherwise eligible at first CBC. R is defined without future outcomes.

For the repeat analysis require R=1, no qualifying cancer on/before T1=53-1.0, and no death on/before T1. Follow from T1 to T1+2 and then T1+5. This is explicitly conditional on being re-observed and event-free, not a recovered version of the first-CBC estimand.

### Features

Within each development split, standardize each CBC variable using instance-0 development means and standard deviations, separately by sex or with sex as a prespecified covariate. Apply those quantities to instances 1 and 2.

First-CBC features are z_WBC0, z_Hb0, z_RDW0 and z_platelet0. The prespecified platelet-haemoglobin contrast is the CRC-minus-hematologic coefficient contrast beta_platelet0 - beta_Hb0; positive means relatively higher platelets/lower haemoglobin is more CRC-associated.

Repeat features are the four baseline z values and d_j=z_j,1-z_j,0 for each cell line. The primary repeat contrast is beta_d_platelet - beta_d_Hb. A secondary fixed instability summary is D_ML=mean(abs(d_WBC), abs(d_Hb), abs(d_RDW), abs(d_platelet)). Do not include all four changes and D_HP=d_platelet-d_Hb as separate linear predictors: they are collinear. Include T1-T0 as a covariate and report its distribution. CRP 30710-1.0 is sensitivity-only.

Cancer classes are CRC C18/C19/C20; hematologic C81--C96; other primary malignant C00--C97 excluding those families and secondary C77--C79. C77--C79 are not primary target events. Take the earliest event across cancer classes and 40000-0.0 death. Report denominators, missingness, gap quantiles, event counts/person-time and exclusions before each landmark.

## Selection and timing estimands

The first-CBC estimand is the cause-specific CRC-versus-hematologic coefficient contrast for the platelet and haemoglobin baseline terms in all first-CBC-eligible adults. Its 0--2-year version is near-diagnostic; 2--5 tests persistence beyond likely work-up.

The repeat estimand is the corresponding contrast for the four change coefficients in the T1 landmark. Fit unweighted and with stabilized inverse-probability-of-repeat weights. Estimate P(R=1|X0) using only first-CBC information: baseline CBC, sex, age, BMI, smoking, CRP, first-assessment year, and eligibility indicators. Use a numerator based on sex and first-assessment year, trim at fixed 1st/99th percentiles, and report untrimmed sensitivity. Show balance before/after weighting.

Weights address measured baseline predictors of repeat observation only. They cannot repair cancer/death before T1, unmeasured healthcare use, symptoms, treatment, or the fact that 53-1.0 is a research-assessment measurement. The weighted repeat analysis is a selection stress test, not a causal correction.

Prespecify a 0.20 log-hazard equivalence margin (about a 22% hazard-ratio ratio) for weighted-minus-unweighted change. Call measured-selection robustness compatible only if the point change is within the margin and a 90% bootstrap interval is wholly inside it. If sparse events make that impossible, report inconclusive.

## Methods compared before selection

### A. Transparent cause-specific baseline

Fit separate cause-specific Cox models for CRC and hematologic cancer. Other cancer and death are competing events in the risk sets. The first model uses four baseline CBC values plus age, sex, BMI, smoking, CRP and first-assessment year. The repeat model uses the same baseline covariates, four changes and assessment gap, with the repeat weight in the weighted version. Estimate the prespecified CRC-minus-hematologic coefficient contrasts with robust 95% intervals and time-varying-effect diagnostics. Use penalization only for documented separation/convergence failure and record it.

Estimate Aalen--Johansen cumulative incidence at 2 and 5 years for CRC, hematologic cancer, other cancer and death. Fine--Gray can be secondary, never a replacement for the cause-specific estimand. This baseline is primary because the estimand is auditable; it loses nonlinear thresholds, cross-line interactions and time-varying hazards.

### B. Substantive learned alternative

Fit a CPU gradient-boosted discrete-time multi-task competing-risk model using exactly the same eligible people and raw information. Expand each person into yearly intervals from the relevant landmark through event/censoring/horizon. Predict CRC, hematologic cancer and other cancer/death hazards; include interval number. No post-landmark registry field or future CBC may be a predictor.

The first feature set is exactly the baseline feature set. The repeat set is exactly baseline CBC, four changes, gap and covariates. A small fixed grid is tuned in rolling development folds. This alternative can reveal nonlinear cell-line ranges, low-Hb-by-platelet interactions and time-varying type-specific hazards that A loses; it is not a mechanism detector.

Fit the repeat-observation head P(R=1|X0) within each development fold to generate weights. Do not use future R as a first-CBC risk predictor. In the repeat model R=1 defines the conditional population, not a predictor.

Compare B with A on a final temporal holdout using target-specific calibration intercept/slope, calibration plots, 2- and 5-year cumulative-incidence Brier/log scores and participant-bootstrap intervals. Time-dependent AUC/Uno C-index is secondary. A small AUC gain without calibration or a stable cancer-type pattern is not a scientific advance. Feature-effect summaries are descriptive and frozen without test-outcome peeking.

### Split, uncertainty and compute

Sort participants by the relevant landmark date; earliest 70% is development and latest 30% is final test. Participants stay intact. Rolling development folds fit standardization, repeat weights, tuning and calibration. No test outcome, date, normalization, imputation or tuning choice enters fitting. If the held-out hematologic count is below 50, label the learned result imprecise and do not switch to a random split.

Use robust model intervals and 500 participant bootstrap replicates for held-out predictions, weighted estimates and weighted-minus-unweighted differences. Preserve failures and convergence warnings. Complete-case CBC features are required; missing is not normal.

The audit used short CPU scans; full fitting is unmeasured. inputs.json permits up to 16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB, 8 GPUs and 28,800 seconds for the future solver. Request CPU (8--16 CPUs, 32--64 GiB), estimated 2--4 hours. The modest gradient-boosted model does not require GPU; no GPU feasibility claim is made.

## Falsification and interpretation

The primary direction is relatively higher platelets/lower haemoglobin being more CRC-associated. It is a hypothesis, not an observed result.

Supportive evidence requires: (1) the first-CBC contrast has the prespecified direction; (2) repeat change contrast has the same direction unweighted and weighted, with selection change compatible with the margin; (3) the effect is not confined to 0--2 years, or is explicitly labelled near-diagnostic only; (4) learned nonlinear patterns are stable across folds and improve held-out calibration or cumulative-incidence scores; and (5) the contrast is more specific to CRC versus hematologic cancer than to all cancers.

Adverse evidence is a reasonably precise reversal, a large weighted/unweighted change, disappearance after two years, or the same signal for other cancers. That revises/abandons type-specific discordance while leaving generic CBC associations possible.

Inconclusive evidence is fewer than 50 usable held-out hematologic events, an equivalence interval wider than the margin, unstable gap/instance-2 sensitivity, convergence failure, or discrimination without calibration. A wide null does not refute the hypothesis.

Required checks:

- Audit every date/code pair, duplicate rows, implausible dates and fixed administrative censoring.
- Report 0--2 and 2--5 windows; 5--10 is exploratory only.
- Report repeat-gap strata and baseline R=1 versus R=0 balance.
- Use other primary cancers as a specificity control.
- Permute cancer type among development event dates while preserving timing; interaction should collapse toward zero.
- Use instance 2 only as a small sensitivity cohort, not dense trajectory evidence.
- Compare complete-CBC participants with the eligible denominator; never impute missing CBC as normal.

A supportive result establishes only a temporally ordered descriptive association useful for external-validation design. It does not establish diagnostic accuracy in symptomatic patients, a referral threshold, mechanism, stage, treatment benefit or clinical utility. The source lacks ferritin/iron, reticulocytes, FIT, symptoms, medications, transfusion context, smear, marrow studies, pathology adjudication, stage, work-up, lab indication/source and complete healthcare-contact history. 53 is a research assessment date, not a clinical test-order date. Clinical use requires expert code/lab review, external clinical validation and a prospective decision-linked study.

## Alternatives and deliverable

The transparent cause-specific model is selected as primary because it directly tests the claim and is auditable with sparse hematologic events. The gradient-boosted model is retained because it tests substantive nonlinear and time-varying information, not because complexity earns merit. A latent GP/state-space model or transformer is deferred: only two broadly complete CBC assessments exist, instance 2 is small, and repeat-landmark hematologic events are sparse. A first-CBC model using future R is rejected as leakage. Cross-namespace augmentation is rejected because the catalog has distinct namespaces and no authorized crosswalk.

The solver must newly fit/estimate: first-CBC and repeat cause-specific models; unweighted/weighted repeat selection; both temporal-holdout models; competing-risk curves; calibration/Brier/log scores; coefficient contrasts; 500-bootstrap uncertainty; gap/window sensitivities; and the cancer-type permutation negative control. Completion requires cohort/missingness/event tables, selection balance, split manifest, fitted outputs/predictions, uncertainty and a conclusion tied to those outputs. Readiness or a fit alone does not establish the claim.

## Key bibliography

[K1] Hamilton W, Lancashire R, Sharp D, Peters TJ, Cheng KK, Marshall T. The importance of anaemia in diagnosing colorectal cancer: a case-control study using electronic primary care records. British Journal of Cancer. 2008;98(2):323--327. DOI 10.1038/sj.bjc.6604165. PMCID PMC2361444.

[K2] Sala RJ, Ery J, Cuesta-Peredo D, Muedra V, Rodilla V. Haematological pre-staging of colorectal cancer: Longitudinal trends identify high-risk metastatic phenotypes 24 months prior to diagnosis. Translational Oncology. 2026;72:102954. DOI 10.1016/j.tranon.2026.102954. PMCID PMC13449478.

[K3] Hampton JS, Kenny RPW, Rees CJ, Hamilton W, Eastaugh C, Richmond C, Sharp L, COLOFIT Research Team. The performance of FIT-based and other risk prediction models for colorectal neoplasia in symptomatic patients: a systematic review. eClinicalMedicine. 2023;64:102204. DOI 10.1016/j.eclinm.2023.102204. PMCID PMC10541467.

Attached inspected excerpts and receipts: work/evidence/K1_hamilton_2008_excerpt.txt, work/evidence/K2_sala_2026_excerpt.txt, work/evidence/K3_hampton_2023_excerpt.txt and work/key-references.json.


## Harbor execution contract

This is a readiness-mode open research task, not a known-answer task. The solver must newly fit and report the analyses described above; no fitted result, reference solution, or scientific conclusion is supplied. Read-only data are mounted according to `bindings.json`; `/workspace` is the only declared output area.

Use `/data/ukb_483356f97e1e8132_parquet/ukb_483356f97e1e8132.parquet`, the Parquet derivative of catalog table `datasets/ukb/table-5d49a6760e7ffdbd.json` (`ukb671626.csv`, source id `ukb_483356f97e1e8132_parquet`, SHA-256 `a7c03cf84cd951dec9fa013ae76e6e1a363f579506886f59a0f179beae15e23a`). It is an ordinary file, not an archive member. Load the table with `eid` as the only key in the `ukb671626` namespace. Do not read or join the other bound namespaces, even though their read-only bindings are retained.

The required output is `/workspace/results.json`. It must be valid UTF-8 JSON with this shape (additional diagnostic fields are allowed):

# Evolution audit: landmark selection and residual severity in discordant-AKI recovery

Status: proposed successor design; no cohort scan, model fit, or scientific result was run.

Parent audited: candidate-72cc027e1e76f3726901277f.  
Purpose: resolve the remaining uncertainty that the 48-hour discordant-versus-concordant contrast may be created by conditioning on survival/continued ICU observation, residual pre-landmark severity, or unequal recording opportunity.

## 1. Scientific opening and substantive change

The parent asks whether a fall in creatinine after ICU AKI is prognostically misleading when urine output or recorded net volume does not improve. Its primary 48-hour post-onset landmark is leakage-safe and clinically interpretable, but it conditions on being alive, still in the ICU, and sufficiently observed at 48 hours. That conditioning can select a different mixture of severity than the original AKI-onset population. A second concern is that “low urine” can mean either genuine low output or sparse charting, while recorded balance is incomplete and treatment-dependent.

The strongest available evidence supports only bounded background claims:

- [K1] reports, in a small ICU study, that creatinine-based eGFR can overestimate measured kidney function with prolonged critical illness and muscle loss. It does not show that a MIMIC creatinine fall identifies persistent dysfunction.
- [K2] shows that urine-output thresholds and time windows change AKI mortality prediction in MIMIC-IV/eICU. It does not establish the correct threshold for recovery discordance, nor a mechanism or treatment effect.
- [K3] associates positive fluid balance with ICU AKI and mortality in a prospective cohort, while defining balance as intake minus output without insensible losses and leaving KRT initiation to clinicians. It does not study this recovery phenotype.

The unresolved claim remains prognostic, not causal: among patients at a specified post-AKI landmark, does discordant recovery have a reproducible excess 7-day hospital-death/ICU-recorded-RRT risk over concordant recovery after accounting for measured pre-landmark severity and recording opportunity? The new claim is narrower and testable: if the contrast is clinically meaningful, it should not be confined to one survivor landmark or to patients with unusually dense renal documentation; persistent discordance should be more informative than a transient or newly observed discordance.

This successor changes the information obtained in three ways:

1. It estimates a prespecified landmark-selection curve at 24, 48, and 72 hours rather than treating the 48-hour risk set as the whole target population.
2. It distinguishes persistent, resolving, and newly discordant trajectories between adjacent landmarks.
3. It makes “insufficient opportunity to observe” an explicit state and tests a process-only recording signal, rather than silently dropping those patients or coding absent urine rows as zero.

It does not identify true GFR, total-body volume, tubular injury, clinician intent, or a causal treatment effect.

## 2. Actual scientific deliverable

The future Harbor solver must newly construct the same index-ICU-stay AKI cohort and produce:

1. A flow table from AKI onset through each landmark, including death, ICU discharge, pre-landmark RRT, missing creatinine, insufficient urine/input opportunity, and each classifiable exposure state.
2. The parent primary 48-hour standardized risk difference:
   `RD_48 = P(Y_48,7d=1 | discordant) - P(Y_48,7d=1 | concordant)`
   among eligible, classifiable creatinine-recovery patients in the 48-hour risk set.
3. Component-specific 48-hour contrasts for low-urine-only, positive-recorded-balance-only, and both, against concordant recovery.
4. The same state-specific risk estimates at L=24, 48, and 72 hours among the corresponding risk sets, with the number and outcome rate of the explicit unknown/insufficient-recording state.
5. A persistence table for patients classifiable at both 24 and 48 hours: concordant-to-concordant, discordant-to-discordant, discordant-to-concordant, concordant-to-discordant, and other/unknown transitions, with the 48-hour forward outcome.
6. A severity/observation-process sensitivity envelope and a prespecified process-only falsification check.
7. The parent baseline-versus-learned comparison, extended only to ask whether ordered trajectories and persistence add information beyond fixed summaries.

Completion requires saved computed outputs linked to all estimates, uncertainty intervals, cell counts, missingness/selection flows, model specifications, and adverse/inconclusive interpretations. Readiness or a favorable coefficient is not completion.

## 3. Population, temporal boundaries, and estimands

Use the first eligible ICU stay per hospital admission for adults, joined on `(subject_id, hadm_id)`. Retain the parent time origin:

- Adults: `hosp/patients.anchor_age >= 18`.
- First ICU stay per admission, with valid `icustays.intime < icustays.outtime`.
- AKI onset t0: earliest valid creatinine observation within 72 hours after ICU `intime` satisfying the parent KDIGO-like rule: at least 0.3 mg/dL above a creatinine value in the preceding 48 hours or at least 1.5 times the minimum valid value in the preceding 7 days.
- If no prior value supports onset, retain a separately labeled admission-baseline sensitivity; never silently invent baseline.
- Exclude established RRT before t0 using the parent procedure-event set.
- Patient-relative times only; no cross-patient calendar ordering.

For each L in {24, 48, 72} hours after t0, define a risk set R_L containing patients alive, in the index ICU, and not already experiencing the outcome-defining incident RRT at L. Report separately those who die, leave the ICU, or receive RRT before L. The primary 48-hour estimate remains a survivor/ICU-landmark prognostic estimand; it must not be relabeled as an onset-cohort or causal estimand.

At L, exposure uses only clinical times in [L-24 h, L]. No exposure or adjustment variable may use a clinical time after L. For creatinine, identify the most recent valid value in [L-12 h, L] and the peak valid value in [t0, L]. Define creatinine recovery at L as peak minus landmark creatinine >=0.3 mg/dL; report the landmark/peak <=0.8 ratio sensitivity. Neither definition means normal kidney function.

For each L, define:

- concordant: creatinine recovery, urine recovery, and recorded net volume <=0;
- low-urine-only: creatinine recovery, low observed urine, and recorded net volume <=0;
- positive-balance-only: creatinine recovery, urine recovery, and positive recorded net volume;
- both: creatinine recovery, low observed urine, and positive recorded net volume;
- unknown/insufficient: creatinine recovery but inadequate opportunity to classify urine or recorded balance;
- no-creatinine-recovery: descriptive state, not part of the primary discordant-versus-concordant contrast.

The parent binary `discordant = low urine OR positive recorded balance` remains the primary 48-hour contrast for comparability. The four classifiable states and the unknown state are mandatory secondary outputs; if the binary contrast is stable but one component is not, the conclusion must say so.

Primary outcomes remain:

- `Y_L,7d`: hospital death or first ICU-recorded incident RRT in [L, L+7 days), with follow-up not truncated at ICU outtime.
- Hospital death uses `admissions.deathtime` and `hospital_expire_flag`; alive hospital discharge is a competing/censoring event as specified by the parent outcome plan.
- RRT uses only the audited ICU `procedureevents` items and is labeled ICU-recorded RRT; ward-only RRT is unavailable.
- Secondary outcomes: death alone, ICU-recorded RRT alone, same-admission ICU readmission, and hospital death by hospital discharge.

For the dynamic landmark estimates, use cluster-robust inference or a patient-level bootstrap because one patient can contribute to more than one risk set. Do not pool the three risk sets as independent observations.

## 4. Landmark-selection audit

The solver must report, before comparing exposure groups, a risk-set flow with denominators at t0, 24, 48, and 72 hours:

- alive and still in the index ICU;
- hospital/ICU death before L;
- ICU discharge before L;
- incident RRT before L;
- no recent valid creatinine;
- insufficient primary urine observation;
- insufficient balance composition;
- classifiable concordant/discordant component states.

The principal selection diagnostic is the curve of (a) risk-set retention, (b) outcome-before-landmark, (c) unknown/insufficient recording, and (d) the discordant-minus-concordant estimate at each L. A 48-hour contrast that is large only after a sharp loss of high-risk patients, or only when unknown patients are discarded, is not evidence of a stable recovery phenotype.

The parent 48-hour analysis remains the main clinical comparison, but the dynamic estimates answer a different question: the prognosis of observed recovery states among those who reach each landmark. They do not recover a causal effect or a unique onset-cohort effect. A true onset-cohort effect would require data and assumptions sufficient to handle death, discharge, and treatment-dependent observation before L; those are not available here.

For the 24-to-48-hour trajectory analysis, use only states computed from pre-24 and pre-48 windows and outcome time after 48 hours. A patient who has an outcome before 48 is reported in the selection flow and is not assigned a 48-hour trajectory state.

## 5. Residual severity and observation-intensity rivals

### Residual severity

The leading rival is that the discordant group is simply more severely ill at or before the landmark. For each L, fit and report:

- an unadjusted standardized state-specific risk;
- a prespecified severity-adjusted model using onset AKI stage, age, sex, admission type, pre-exposure baseline creatinine, creatinine immediately before the [L-24,L] window, peak creatinine through L, pre-window urine/output and recorded-volume summaries, pre-window RRT/support indicators, and ICU timing;
- stratum-specific estimates across bounded categories of pre-window creatinine, AKI stage, and support intensity, with no estimate reported for empty or sparse cells;
- a sensitivity excluding patients with RRT in (t0,L) and a sensitivity that treats pre-L RRT/death as selection events rather than silently including them in a post-L risk contrast.

All such adjustment is prognostic standardization, not causal control. Variables measured in the exposure window are not claimed to be pre-exposure confounders; their use is a residual-severity sensitivity, and the exact timing must be reported. Do not adjust for post-L data, future outcome proxies, or the learned model’s predictions.

A contrast that vanishes in every well-supported severity stratum supports the residual-severity explanation. A contrast that survives some strata is still only an association; it does not prove intrinsic kidney injury, dilution, congestion, or muscle loss.

### Observation and measurement process

Use exact numeric observations, not imputed zeros:

- For primary urine, numeric mL values in `icu/outputevents` from itemids 226559 Foley, 226560 Void, 226561 Condom Cath, 226563 Suprapubic, and 226567 Straight Cath.
- Count zero-valued numeric output as an observed zero. A missing six-hour bin is unknown, not zero.
- Define urine observation opportunity as the number of distinct six-hour bins in [L-24,L] containing at least one valid primary-set output record. The primary classifiable urine definition requires at least 3 of 4 bins; sensitivities require at least 2 and all 4. Report the exact chosen rule and the other two sensitivities.
- Convert urine to mL/kg/h using the nearest valid weight at or before L, within 48 hours. Weights are `chartevents` itemids 224639, 226512, and 226531 with unit conversion verified from `icu/d_items`.
- Exclude nephrostomy 226564/226565, OR/PACU 226627/226631, mixed GU-irrigant 226566/227489, text estimate 226713, and Apache-derived 227519 from the primary phenotype; report them only in sensitivity/measurement-error outputs.
- For recorded balance in [L-24,L], use one mutually exclusive administered-volume rule from `inputevents`: never sum `amount` and `totalamount` from one row. Retain item-level composition, unresolved/non-mL fractions, and missingness. Recorded balance is input proxy minus direct urine output, not true fluid balance.
- Count output, creatinine, input, weight/CVP, and non-renal chart/lab observations in four six-hour bins. Use `charttime`/clinical time for the primary process counts; `storetime` ordering is a labeled sensitivity because documentation time is not an availability truth.

The process-only falsification check is prespecified: replace kidney discordance by quartiles of pre-landmark non-renal documentation density (non-creatinine `labevents` count plus non-weight/CVP `chartevents` count, with input/output event opportunity counts reported separately), and estimate its association with the same Y outcome. This is a diagnostic for acuity/recording intensity, not a valid negative-control outcome and not evidence that documentation causes death. If the process-only gradient is as large as the kidney contrast and the kidney contrast attenuates with process strata, the clinical interpretation is weakened. A post-L non-renal documentation count may be reported only as a descriptive downstream process endpoint among subjects event-free at L; it cannot be used as a primary adjustment variable.

The explicit unknown state is essential. Compare its size and outcome rate with classifiable states. If unknown patients are high risk, complete-case discordant-versus-concordant results are selection-sensitive. Do not impute unknown urine as low or normal in the primary analysis.

## 6. Dynamic trajectory estimand

Among patients classifiable at both 24 and 48 hours, estimate the 48-hour forward risk for:

- concordant -> concordant;
- discordant -> discordant (persistent);
- discordant -> concordant (resolving);
- concordant -> discordant (new);
- component-specific transitions when cell support permits;
- any transition involving unknown, reported separately.

The baseline comparison is the parent 48-hour binary discordant-versus-concordant estimate. The trajectory analysis asks whether persistence, resolution, or new discordance is more informative than the current state alone. Standardize transition risks over the observed transition population using pre-24 onset severity and pre-24 observation variables. Do not interpret a transition estimate as the effect of making a patient change state: transition selection, treatment, death, and discharge remain unresolved.

If a transition has sparse events, report counts and refrain from fitting an unstable contrast. That is an inconclusive feasibility result, not permission to merge states after seeing outcomes.

- Inputs: fixed L-specific summaries of creatinine peak and pre-window level/slope, AKI stage, urine rate and observed-bin count, item-level recorded input/output composition, weight, exploratory CVP, RRT/support summaries, ICU timing, non-renal observation density, and missingness/unknown indicators.
- Target: Y_L,7d at each landmark; for the trajectory branch, the 48-hour forward outcome by the predeclared transition state.
- Fit: standardized logistic risk with bounded restricted cubic splines or prespecified linear terms; patient-level cluster bootstrap; report risk differences, calibration, Brier score and uncertainty.
- Split: for any predictive fit, subject-level 70/15/15 train/validation/test, with every stay of a subject in one split. The primary descriptive/standardized contrast must not be selected on the test set.
- Budget: CPU tabular fit within the parent solver envelope (16 CPUs, 262144 MiB, 28,800 seconds maximum); the exact runtime is unmeasured.

The substantive learned alternative uses the same question and exact pre-landmark sources:

- Input sequence: 6-hour bins from t0 through each L, containing creatinine, primary-set urine amount/rate and observation mask, input/output recorded-volume components, weight, CVP, RRT/support indicators, non-renal observation counts, and missingness channels.
- Target: Y_L,7d and, in a separate prespecified head, the state/transition risk at L. The model must not see post-L values or future outcome proxies.
- Evaluation: held-out calibration slope/intercept, Brier score, AUROC, and held-out standardized discordant-versus-concordant and persistent-versus-resolving risk contrasts, all with bootstrap uncertainty. Compare against the fixed-summary baseline on the same test patients.
- Information gained: a sequence can reveal whether ordering, persistence, and recovery timing matter beyond a fixed 24-hour summary. It cannot separate residual severity from mechanism and must not replace the interpretable state analysis.
- Resource estimate: parent planning estimate was 4–16 CPU cores, 16–64 GB RAM, 1–6 hours for a larger CPU sequence fit, or one allocated A100 for 1–3 hours if batching is the bottleneck. These are unverified estimates; GPU allocation is optional and no GPU was used for this discovery audit.

Selection: retain the baseline as the primary scientific deliverable. Fit the learned alternative only if the dynamic states have adequate support and repeated measurements; defer it if not. Revisit the learned branch only for a replicated trajectory interaction or improved calibration that changes interpretation, not a small AUROC gain. This is a scientific adequacy decision, not a CPU/GPU preference.

## 9. Falsification and interpretation

Supportive result:

- the 48-hour parent contrast is clinically nontrivial and directionally consistent at 24/48/72 hours;
- the contrast is not confined to a single narrow severity stratum or dense-recording stratum;
- persistent discordance has greater risk than resolving discordance with adequate cells;
- the unknown state is not so large or high-risk that complete-case interpretation is untenable; and
- component-specific estimates do not reveal that the binary result is only an artifact of one contaminated or poorly observed component.

This would justify prospective validation of enhanced renal monitoring and an adjudicated study with measured GFR, cystatin C, biomarkers, complete urine collection, total-body fluid measures, treatment intent, and ward-RRT ascertainment. It would remain a prognostic association.

Adverse result:

- the contrast disappears after the landmark curve, severity strata, or recording-opportunity/process checks;
- it reverses across landmarks or is driven by unknown/missing patients;
- a documentation-density process signal is comparable to the kidney contrast; or
- only a mixed/contaminated urine set produces the signal.

This would weaken the claim that creatinine-only recovery identifies a reproducible clinical discordance and redirect work toward measurement validation or other recovery markers. It would not prove creatinine is valid, that fluid management is harmless, or that treatment has no effect.

Inconclusive result:

- sparse transition cells, wide intervals spanning clinically meaningful harm, unstable estimates across reasonable windows, large unknown states, or incomplete ascertainment of hospital outcomes.

This would mean MIMIC cannot resolve the question. It would justify a measurement/adjudication or external-validation study, not a favorable conclusion. A small predictive improvement from the learned model is also inconclusive for clinical value unless it reveals a reproducible trajectory distinction.

Computationally checkable claims are: exact cohort construction, temporal exclusion, joins, item filters, state counts, missingness/opportunity counts, risk estimates, uncertainty, held-out predictive metrics, and whether conclusions match outputs. Clinical adjudication is required for true kidney function, complete urine collection, fluid status, treatment intent, mechanism, causal effects, and ward-only RRT. Automatic verification cannot establish those claims.

## 10. Unavailable evidence and non-reproduction boundaries

This is a bounded MIMIC-IV adaptation, not a reproduction of any cited paper. The configured snapshot lacks cystatin C, measured GFR/iohexol, muscle mass, tubular-injury biomarkers, true total-body volume, insensible losses, medication/fluid intent, complete bedside collection adjudication, clinician goals of care, and reliable ward-only RRT capture. `CVP` is exploratory and not a fluid-status gold standard. The dynamic landmark design makes selection visible; it does not solve informative discharge/death or treatment-dependent observation.

The parent’s three demonstrations and other seed directions are not used as topic constraints. The structured sequence idea is used only as a baseline comparison for ordered trajectories; no unavailable modality or cohort is claimed.

## 11. Key works

Exactly three distinct inspected works are retained. The attached excerpts are UTF-8 and labeled with their inspection limits; `work/branches/key-references.json` contains the structured receipts.

[K1] Haines RW, Fowler AJ, Liang K, Pearse RM, Larsson AO, Puthucheary Z, Prowle JR. “Comparison of Cystatin C and Creatinine in the Assessment of Measured Kidney Function during Critical Illness.” Clin J Am Soc Nephrol. 2023;18(8):997–1005. doi:10.2215/cjn.0000000000000203. Abstract-level inspection in the attached excerpt. It supports the residual creatinine/muscle-loss rival but does not establish this MIMIC phenotype.

[K2] Machado GD, Santos LL, Libório AB. “Redefining urine output thresholds for acute kidney injury criteria in critically Ill patients: a derivation and validation study.” Crit Care. 2024;28:272. doi:10.1186/s13054-024-05054-3. Abstract-level provider response attached in this branch; the parent also retained fuller evidence. It supports prespecifying window/threshold and persistence sensitivities but does not establish recovery discordance or mechanism.

[K3] Melo FAF, Burdmann EA, Macedo E, Mehta R, Zanetta DMT. “Acute kidney injury developed in the intensive care unit: a population-based prospective cohort study in the Brazilian Amazon.” Sci Rep. 2024;14:22954. doi:10.1038/s41598-024-74177-y. Article/abstract passages inspected in the attached excerpt. It supports the fluid-balance severity rival but does not establish causality, true volume status, or this recovery comparison.

## 12. Alternatives not chosen and revision decision

- **Unchanged fixed 48-hour analysis only:** rejected as the sole design because it cannot tell whether a result is specific to the survivor/ICU selection or to dense recording. It remains the primary comparator.
- **Single complex sequence model:** deferred because better prediction alone would not resolve residual severity or measurement error. The sequence is retained only as a secondary, same-question test of ordered/persistent information.
- **Causal treatment-effect or inverse-probability intervention analysis:** not selected because treatment intent, complete fluid exposure, ward RRT, and informative discharge/death are unavailable. A causal interpretation would require additional data and expert review.
- **A hard negative-control clinical outcome:** not selected because no MIMIC outcome here is credibly independent of acute severity and surveillance. The process-only documentation analysis is explicitly diagnostic, not a validated negative control.
- **Changing the primary population to all AKI-onset patients with imputation of later state:** rejected because death/discharge before the landmark makes a later recovery state undefined; imputation would hide the very selection uncertainty under study.

Evidence to revisit the deferred branches: a validated measurement/adjudication subset with complete urine and fluid collection, cystatin C/measured GFR or biomarkers, treatment intent and ward RRT; or an external cohort with prospective landmark follow-up. Evidence to abandon the direction: a well-powered, observation-complete validation showing no reproducible component or trajectory contrast across landmarks and severity strata.
