Later pace code counts were 1/2/3 = 173/2,190/2,171; later falls counts were 1/2/3 = 3,795/540/199. These are availability observations only. The solver must resolve Data-Coding 100313 and 100539 before naming pace ordering or a no-fall category; failure makes that endpoint inconclusive rather than permitting a new definition.

For each endpoint, the primary population is the unique anchor with age >=50, valid T0, complete Q/MFI/grip, valid baseline outcome, first strictly later valid endpoint, and T1-T0 >=365 days. The >=730-day population is locked sensitivity. T1 is date-based, never instance-number based.

## Exposures and estimands

Fit transformations in development only.

- Q is the sum of the four bilateral anterior/posterior thigh fat-free volumes; preserve all four components.
- MFI is the bilateral mean of `23355-2.0` and `23356-2.0`.
- Grip is the maximum valid left/right grip; bilateral-complete is primary, side-specific/discordant analyses are sensitivity.
- Baseline pace/falls are baseline state, not dated incident events.

After coding resolution, primary pace outcome is later category lower than baseline, reporting worsening/unchanged/improvement. Primary falls outcome is later value above the verified no-fall category, with full ordinal counts secondary. Falls asks about the last year and is not a dated fall event.

The main estimand is population-standardized absolute risk difference under quantity matching: MFI +1 development SD and grip -1 SD versus both at development means, holding Q and observed baseline covariates at each person's value. Also report nested Q-only -> Q+MFI, Q-only -> Q+grip, and Q-only -> Q+MFI+grip risk contrasts, component risks, and 95% intervals. A 1 percentage-point lower-bound marker is a scale descriptor, not a treatment threshold. This is prognostic/descriptive, not causal.

## Baseline, learned alternative, split, and uncertainty

Primary transparent models are endpoint-specific ordinal/multinomial regression for pace transitions and logistic regression for falls, with ordinal/logistic sensitivities. Models include Q, age, BMI, weight, height, smoking, baseline outcome, and a prespecified missingness rule; no post-T0 variable is allowed. Diagnosis families define pre-T0 restriction and code-adjusted sensitivity, not casual mediator adjustment. Post-T0 codes are descriptive only.

Use a patient-level temporal split: earliest 70% of T0 for development/tuning and latest 30% as locked holdout. Each `eid` is in one split. Standardization, imputation, coding thresholds, and tuning are development-only. Report holdout calibration intercept/slope, plots, Brier score, log loss, secondary rank metrics, standardized risks, and 500 participant-bootstrap intervals (or a documented substitute). Require at least 100 holdout events, class support, finite estimates, stable calibration and positivity; otherwise endpoint is inconclusive with no split/outcome changes.

Matched learned alternative: CPU gradient-boosted trees for each endpoint using exactly the same participants, inputs, missingness policy, T0/T1 rule, split and outcomes. It can reveal Q-by-MFI, Q-by-grip, thresholds, and side/compartment interactions that additive regression loses. It is substantive only if a held-out quantity-matched risk contrast or rival interpretation changes; a small rank-metric gain is not enough. Report uncertainty-bearing accumulated-local-effect or partial-dependence summaries descriptively, never as mechanism.

The transparent model is primary because it exposes the estimand and is auditable with roughly 4,500 endpoint pairs. The learned model is retained to test nonlinear scientific structure. A deep image model is deferred because no image payload exists; a trajectory model is deferred because only one verified later assessment exists; causal mediation is rejected because pain severity, neurologic examination, actual fall timing and treatment are unavailable.

Planning estimate: 8 CPU cores, 32–64 GiB RAM, 2–4 hours for selected-column parsing, exact joins, two baselines/boosted fits and bootstrap. Unmeasured planning estimate; GPU is not needed for this tabular question.

## Rival falsification

Pain/arthritis/neurologic rival: repeat the primary analysis in participants without prespecified pre-T0 inpatient code families, report each diagnosis stratum and same-index code-adjusted model. A grip signal that disappears while MFI remains stable supports the rival; a persistent result is only compatible with a quality signal because outpatient pain and examination remain missing.

MRI/body-size/sex rival: adjust using the available age/BMI/weight/height fields; compare bilateral and side/compartment estimates, and report body-size sensitivity. Sex cannot be adjusted or stratified from this verified table; a result is explicitly limited by that missing evidence. Strong attenuation or side-specific instability is adverse for the biological interpretation.

Repeat-selection/reverse-timing rival: compare unweighted results with baseline-only inverse-probability weighting for having a valid later assessment, report weights/positivity, and repeat at >=730 days and by early/late T1. Do not condition on post-T0 variables. A large weighting shift or short-lag-only signal is adverse; an imprecise weighted result is inconclusive.

Supportive evidence requires at least one endpoint passing support/positivity/calibration gates, a positive held-out Q+MFI or Q+grip increment beyond Q-only with 95% interval above zero and lower bound at least 1 point for a prespecified endpoint, compatible direction across pace/falls or lag sensitivity, no diagnosis-clean collapse, and no large return-selection shift. This supports validation/adjudication research, not deployment, causality or mechanism.

Adverse evidence is a held-out null/reversal, Q-only equivalence, baseline-only association, body-size attenuation, diagnosis-restricted collapse, large weighting shift, short-lag-only pattern, or a learned rank gain without the prespecified risk contrast. It weakens this data-bound claim, not all muscle-quality hypotheses.

Inconclusive evidence is unverified outcome coding, failed code/date pairing, fewer than 100 holdout events, missing class support, unstable calibration/positivity, or intervals spanning zero and the scale marker. An imprecise null is not refutation.

## Deliverable and limits

The solver must output a frozen cohort audit; exact model and holdout prediction files for Q-only, Q+MFI, Q+grip, Q+MFI+grip and boosted models; calibration/Brier/log-loss/risk/interval tables; rival sensitivity outputs; learned interaction summaries; and a conclusion file labelling each endpoint supportive, adverse or inconclusive with links to computed outputs.

Computationally checkable claims are source/hash/namespace compliance, exact joins, date ordering, cohort counts, exposure construction, split integrity, fit success, calibration/uncertainty and rule-following. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for pain severity, outpatient arthritis, neurologic examination, MRI segmentation validity, actual fall timing/severity, treatment effects, mechanism, transportability and clinical utility. No participant-level rows or fitted results are included here.

Revisit if same-namespace sex or validated sex-specific MRI normalization, outpatient pain/arthritis and neurologic examination, or repeated post-MRI muscle/function measures become available. Preserve unfavorable diagnosis-restricted, 730-day, side-discordance and return-selection branches.

## Three inspected key works

- [K1] Cruz-Jentoft et al. (EWGSOP2), 2019: consensus separation of strength, quantity/quality and performance; abstract-only inspection.
- [K2] Linge et al., 2021: UKB MRI MFI/composition and mortality; full-text XML inspection.
- [K3] Kim et al., 2026: UKB thigh MRI distribution, grip and falls; full-text XML inspection.

The catalog has no participant-level MRI images, gait recordings, pain scores, neurologic examination, or dated fall ledger.

## Verified temporal audit

I independently read only the selected Assessment Center columns and wrote `audit/temporal-audit.json` (SHA-256 `3b9f17d25ff059fd4b20d2c958b8179a74bfdf8278cf1ef274780f98dc16c9a2`). Date strings were parsed as dates; numeric special codes `-1,-3,-7,-10,-11` were treated as missing.

The audit found 502,370 rows and unique keys; 37,242 age >=50 anchors with complete bilateral Q, MFI, grip and T0; 4,577 strictly later dates; and 4,311 later dates at least 730 days after T0. Lag min/median/max was 366/828/3,177 days. A valid later pace or falls value was present for 4,534 anchors; valid baseline-plus-later pairs numbered 4,516 and 4,515 respectively. Later pace code counts were 1/2/3 = 173/2,190/2,171; later falls counts were 1/2/3 = 3,795/540/199. These are availability observations only. The solver must resolve Data-Coding 100313 and 100539 before naming pace ordering or a no-fall category; failure makes that endpoint inconclusive rather than permitting a new definition.

For each endpoint, the primary population is the unique anchor with age >=50, valid T0, complete Q/MFI/grip, valid baseline outcome, first strictly later valid endpoint, and T1-T0 >=365 days. The >=730-day population is locked sensitivity. T1 is date-based, never instance-number based.

## Exposures and estimands

Fit transformations in development only.

- Q is the sum of the four bilateral anterior/posterior thigh fat-free volumes; preserve all four components.
- MFI is the bilateral mean of `23355-2.0` and `23356-2.0`.
- Grip is the maximum valid left/right grip; bilateral-complete is primary, side-specific/discordant analyses are sensitivity.
- Baseline pace/falls are baseline state, not dated incident events.

After coding resolution, primary pace outcome is later category lower than baseline, reporting worsening/unchanged/improvement. Primary falls outcome is later value above the verified no-fall category, with full ordinal counts secondary. Falls asks about the last year and is not a dated fall event.

The main estimand is population-standardized absolute risk difference under quantity matching: MFI +1 development SD and grip -1 SD versus both at development means, holding Q and observed baseline covariates at each person's value. Also report nested Q-only -> Q+MFI, Q-only -> Q+grip, and Q-only -> Q+MFI+grip risk contrasts, component risks, and 95% intervals. A 1 percentage-point lower-bound marker is a scale descriptor, not a treatment threshold. This is prognostic/descriptive, not causal.

## Baseline, learned alternative, split, and uncertainty

Primary transparent models are endpoint-specific ordinal/multinomial regression for pace transitions and logistic regression for falls, with ordinal/logistic sensitivities. Models include Q, age, BMI, weight, height, smoking, baseline outcome, and a prespecified missingness rule; no post-T0 variable is allowed. Diagnosis families define pre-T0 restriction and code-adjusted sensitivity, not casual mediator adjustment. Post-T0 codes are descriptive only.

Use a patient-level temporal split: earliest 70% of T0 for development/tuning and latest 30% as locked holdout. Each `eid` is in one split. Standardization, imputation, coding thresholds, and tuning are development-only. Report holdout calibration intercept/slope, plots, Brier score, log loss, secondary rank metrics, standardized risks, and 500 participant-bootstrap intervals (or a documented substitute). Require at least 100 holdout events, class support, finite estimates, stable calibration and positivity; otherwise endpoint is inconclusive with no split/outcome changes.

Matched learned alternative: CPU gradient-boosted trees for each endpoint using exactly the same participants, inputs, missingness policy, T0/T1 rule, split and outcomes. It can reveal Q-by-MFI, Q-by-grip, thresholds, and side/compartment interactions that additive regression loses. It is substantive only if a held-out quantity-matched risk contrast or rival interpretation changes; a small rank-metric gain is not enough. Report uncertainty-bearing accumulated-local-effect or partial-dependence summaries descriptively, never as mechanism.

The transparent model is primary because it exposes the estimand and is auditable with roughly 4,500 endpoint pairs. The learned model is retained to test nonlinear scientific structure. A deep image model is deferred because no image payload exists; a trajectory model is deferred because only one verified later assessment exists; causal mediation is rejected because pain severity, neurologic examination, actual fall timing and treatment are unavailable.

Planning estimate: 8 CPU cores, 32–64 GiB RAM, 2–4 hours for selected-column parsing, exact joins, two baselines/boosted fits and bootstrap. Unmeasured planning estimate; GPU is not needed for this tabular question.

## Rival falsification

Pain/arthritis/neurologic rival: repeat the primary analysis in participants without prespecified pre-T0 inpatient code families, report each diagnosis stratum and same-index code-adjusted model. A grip signal that disappears while MFI remains stable supports the rival; a persistent result is only compatible with a quality signal because outpatient pain and examination remain missing.

MRI/body-size/sex rival: adjust using the available age/BMI/weight/height fields; compare bilateral and side/compartment estimates, and report body-size sensitivity. Sex cannot be adjusted or stratified from this verified table; a result is explicitly limited by that missing evidence. Strong attenuation or side-specific instability is adverse for the biological interpretation.

Repeat-selection/reverse-timing rival: compare unweighted results with baseline-only inverse-probability weighting for having a valid later assessment, report weights/positivity, and repeat at >=730 days and by early/late T1. Do not condition on post-T0 variables. A large weighting shift or short-lag-only signal is adverse; an imprecise weighted result is inconclusive.

Supportive evidence requires at least one endpoint passing support/positivity/calibration gates, a positive held-out Q+MFI or Q+grip increment beyond Q-only with 95% interval above zero and lower bound at least 1 point for a prespecified endpoint, compatible direction across pace/falls or lag sensitivity, no diagnosis-clean collapse, and no large return-selection shift. This supports validation/adjudication research, not deployment, causality or mechanism.

Adverse evidence is a held-out null/reversal, Q-only equivalence, baseline-only association, body-size attenuation, diagnosis-restricted collapse, large weighting shift, short-lag-only pattern, or a learned rank gain without the prespecified risk contrast. It weakens this data-bound claim, not all muscle-quality hypotheses.

Inconclusive evidence is unverified outcome coding, failed code/date pairing, fewer than 100 holdout events, missing class support, unstable calibration/positivity, or intervals spanning zero and the scale marker. An imprecise null is not refutation.

## Deliverable and limits

The solver must output a frozen cohort audit; exact model and holdout prediction files for Q-only, Q+MFI, Q+grip, Q+MFI+grip and boosted models; calibration/Brier/log-loss/risk/interval tables; rival sensitivity outputs; learned interaction summaries; and a conclusion file labelling each endpoint supportive, adverse or inconclusive with links to computed outputs.

Computationally checkable claims are source/hash/namespace compliance, exact joins, date ordering, cohort counts, exposure construction, split integrity, fit success, calibration/uncertainty and rule-following. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for pain severity, outpatient arthritis, neurologic examination, MRI segmentation validity, actual fall timing/severity, treatment effects, mechanism, transportability and clinical utility. No participant-level rows or fitted results are included here.

Revisit if same-namespace sex or validated sex-specific MRI normalization, outpatient pain/arthritis and neurologic examination, or repeated post-MRI muscle/function measures become available. Preserve unfavorable diagnosis-restricted, 730-day, side-discordance and return-selection branches.

# Residual instability at ICU discharge: a time-specific competing-risk audit

Status: candidate-ready design; no cohort scan, model fit, Harbor execution, or clinical result was run.

Parent/context: expert-20260913-mimic-10 (candidate-42ec85fd895f7d68293404be) and prior valid design candidate-1b6b938723e1b549149962f5. This branch is an independent audit child, not a revision of the mature AKI branch.

## Decision and scientific opening

ICU discharge is a consequential transition: the patient is alive and leaving intensive monitoring, but the same-hospital risk set remains open for ICU return or death. [K1] found that post-ICU-transfer ward vital/laboratory flags were associated with near-term ICU readmission or death in a small single-center surgical cohort. That supports a short-term prognostic opening, but it does not establish a discharge-time phenotype, independence from the receiving unit, or an actionable effect of monitoring. [K3] links respiratory independence and post-discharge dependency to mortality in a small elderly cohort, but bundles function, destination, support and long-term prognosis. [K2] shows that MIMIC-IV readmission models can compare associative and learned temporal models, while also illustrating that predictive or “causal-fused” outputs do not identify a discharge intervention effect.

The unresolved question is:

> Among adults discharged alive from an index ICU stay, does persistent multi-domain physiologic abnormality in the final 24 hours identify a higher 48-hour cumulative incidence of first ICU readmission versus hospital death, after a conservative availability rule, with destination, residual severity and observation opportunity audited as rival explanations?

Primary hypothesis: relative to patients with no persistent core domain abnormality, patients with at least two persistent domains have higher 48-hour first-event incidence of ICU readmission or hospital death, and the component-specific contrasts are not confined to one immediate destination or to dense documentation. This is an observed prognostic association, not a causal effect of discharge delay, monitoring, oxygen therapy, or treatment limitation.

The clinical advance is boundary testing. A positive result would identify a reproducible high-risk transition phenotype suitable for prospective monitoring or discharge-readiness validation. A result restricted to a destination, sparse charting pattern, or hospice-like disposition would redirect the question toward discharge selection and goals of care. A temporal result that distinguishes persistent from newly abnormal or resolving trajectories would add clinically interpretable timing information beyond a risk score.

## Leading explanation and strongest rivals

- Physiologic instability predicts adverse transition: the association persists after pre-discharge severity standardization, in adequately observed patients, across immediate-destination strata, and is stronger for persistent or newly abnormal trajectories than for a matched earlier window.
- Discharge selection/severity: the final-24-hour association disappears after pre-window severity adjustment, is similar in the earlier [t_d-48h,t_d-24h) window, or is present regardless of domain pattern. Conditioning on ICU discharge is part of the estimand and cannot be removed by regression.
- Care-unit destination: the association is concentrated in particular receiving units. Immediate destination is measured after t_d and is therefore a descriptive selection audit, not a pre-discharge confounder or primary adjustment variable.
- Treatment limitation/goals of care: death, hospice/palliative destination, and sparse intervention may reflect undocumented limits. MIMIC fields available here do not provide a validated pre-t_d goals-of-care indicator. No model, discharge note, hospital-expire flag, or destination label will be treated as a substitute.
- Observation opportunity/charting: the phenotype is mainly a dense-monitoring signature. A documentation-density gradient with similar outcome association, or strong attenuation after density stratification, weakens the physiologic interpretation.
- Support meaning: O2 flow/FiO2 can reflect prescribed support or chronic need rather than hypoxemia. Oxygen-support and physiologic abnormality components are reported separately; the item does not establish respiratory failure, device setting, work of breathing, or clinician intent.

## Scientific deliverable

The future Harbor solver must produce, from computed outputs:

1. A flow from adult admissions to first eligible ICU stay, alive ICU discharge, availability-qualified exposure, and each outcome risk set, including exclusions and unknown bins.
2. A dictionary/provenance audit with exact item labels, linksto, categories, units, numeric/text handling and fail-closed collision rules.
3. Four exposure states (stable, one persistent domain, at least two persistent domains, unknown/insufficient) plus domain-specific components, trajectory classes and observation counts.
4. First-event 48-hour counts and Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidences for ICU readmission, hospital death and alive hospital discharge; readmission/death risk differences with bootstrap intervals.
5. Pre-discharge severity, destination, observation-density and earlier-window audits with sparse-cell rules.
6. A fixed-summary cause-specific baseline and a chronological GRU on exactly the same eligible subjects, with held-out Brier/calibration, trajectory-standardized predictions and uncertainty.
7. Conclusions linked to these tables and figures. No completion claim is valid from readiness or model fit alone.

## Population, landmarks and leakage control

Unit is one hospital admission, using the earliest valid ICU stay for that subject_id/hadm_id pair. Join:

- patients on subject_id; retain anchor_age >= 18 and report gender.
- icustays on subject_id, hadm_id; require intime < outtime and choose minimum intime.
- admissions on subject_id, hadm_id; define t_d = icustays.outtime.
- retain deathtime null or deathtime > t_d. A death exactly at t_d is not an alive ICU discharge.
- retain every immediate destination, including ward, step-down/intermediate, hospice/palliative and unknown.

Primary physiology window is [t_d-24 hours,t_d), divided into four half-open 6-hour bins. A core record is eligible only when clinical charttime < t_d and, when storetime is present, storetime <= t_d. Missing storetime is fail-closed for primary core exposure. This conservative rule makes the primary signal plausibly available by discharge; a charttime-only sensitivity explicitly measures documentation-lag sensitivity. Values at or after t_d never enter predictors. The earlier-window audit is [t_d-48h,t_d-24h), with the same availability rule.

A patient is exposure-known only if at least three of four primary bins contain a valid core observation. A missing bin is unknown, not normal. The all-eligible flow retains insufficient-observation patients as unknown; the primary observed-discharge prognostic estimand is clearly labeled as restricted to exposure-known patients. A sensitivity requires core respiratory/oxygen observation in all four bins. No threshold or inclusion rule is changed after outcome inspection.

## Exact exposure and dictionary bindings

Read icu/chartevents from archive member mimic-iv-3.1/icu/chartevents.csv.gz, joined to icu/icustays by stay_id and filtered by subject_id/hadm_id/stay_id and time. Required fields are subject_id, hadm_id, stay_id, charttime, storetime, itemid, value, valuenum, valueuom and warning. Read icu/d_items from mimic-iv-3.1/icu/d_items.csv.gz; require itemid, label, abbreviation, linksto, category, unitname, param_type, lownormalvalue and highnormalvalue. The verified snapshot schema hash is daa6639c4ab9a469d2889c729d37673c08627ce668cfd808e8a45db4069c4c2e.

The frozen item audit found:

- 220045 Heart Rate, bpm, Numeric, chartevents.
- 220052 Arterial Blood Pressure mean, mmHg, Numeric, chartevents.
- 220210 Respiratory Rate, insp/min, Numeric, chartevents.
- 220277 O2 saturation pulseoxymetry, %, Numeric, chartevents.
- 223761 Temperature Fahrenheit, °F, Numeric, chartevents; convert to Celsius.
- 223762 Temperature Celsius, °C, Numeric, chartevents.
- 223834 O2 Flow, L/min, Numeric, chartevents.
- 223835 Inspired O2 Fraction, unitname None, Numeric, chartevents.
- 226732 O2 Delivery Device(s), Text, chartevents; descriptive sensitivity only and never coerced to a numeric exposure.

Fail closed if an item is absent, has a different label/linksto/unit or collides with another selected item. Numeric values must be finite and unit-compatible; text-only values are invalid for numeric channels. Within each 6-hour bin use median HR/MAP/RR/SpO2/temperature and maximum O2 flow/FiO2. Preserve a missingness mask and valid-record count.

Domain flags are fixed before outcome inspection:

- respiratory/oxygen: SpO2 <92%, O2 flow >0 L/min, or FiO2 >0.21;
- hemodynamic: MAP <65 mmHg, HR >100 or <50 bpm;
- ventilatory pattern: RR >24 or <8/min;
- temperature: Celsius <36.0 or >38.3.

A domain is persistent when flagged in at least two of four bins. Exposure states are stable/no persistent domain, exactly one persistent domain, at least two persistent domains, and unknown/insufficient. The primary contrast is at least two versus stable. Report oxygen-support flags separately from SpO2 and report the fixed trajectory classes: stable, persistent (flagged in all observed bins), newly abnormal (only the final two bins), resolving (only the first two bins), and intermittent (two non-adjacent flagged bins), with an unknown class when required. These classes are descriptive and are not a post hoc threshold search.

## Outcomes and competing-risk estimands

Read icu/icustays fields subject_id, hadm_id, stay_id, intime, outtime; read hosp/admissions fields subject_id, hadm_id, admittime, dischtime, deathtime and hospital_expire_flag. For [t_d,t_d+48h), define the earliest clinical first event:

- ICU readmission: a later icustays.intime for the same subject_id/hadm_id, with intime >= t_d and < t_d+48h; the index stay is excluded.
- Hospital death: admissions.deathtime >= t_d and < t_d+48h.
- Alive hospital discharge: admissions.dischtime >= t_d and < t_d+48h, only when no earlier readmission or death.
- Event-free: no event and still under the same-hospital risk set at 48 hours.

If readmission and death have the same timestamp, assign death first because readmission requires survival and emit a data-integrity flag. A death after readmission remains a secondary outcome, not a first-event death. hospital_expire_flag is a consistency check, never a replacement for a missing death time.

The primary estimands are standardized 48-hour cumulative incidence and absolute risk difference for first ICU readmission and first hospital death, with alive hospital discharge as a competing event. Report the composite readmission-or-death only as a secondary summary. Use Aalen-Johansen for unadjusted CIFs and cause-specific discrete-time logistic hazards in six-hour post-discharge intervals for adjusted standardization. The adjustment set is pre-t_d only; immediate destination is not in the primary adjustment set. A multinomial first-event model is sensitivity only. The estimand is conditional on reaching an observed alive ICU discharge and, for the primary contrast, having adequate pre-discharge observation; it is not a causal discharge policy effect.

## Rival audits

Immediate destination is the first hosp/transfers row with subject_id, hadm_id and intime >= t_d; use transfer_id, eventtype, careunit, intime and outtime, and classify unknown when no row is available. Ultimate disposition is separately admissions.discharge_location; it is reported separately and never substituted for immediate destination. Report primary estimates within prespecified destination families, suppressing cells with fewer than 20 events or fewer than 100 patients as inconclusive rather than merging after seeing outcomes.

Residual severity uses only [t_d-48h,t_d) and the static fields patients.anchor_age, patients.gender, admissions.admission_type, icustays.intime/outtime/los, plus hosp/labevents (subject_id, hadm_id, itemid, charttime, storetime, value, valuenum, valueuom, ref_range_lower, ref_range_upper, flag) joined to hosp/d_labitems (itemid, label, fluid, category). The verified lab choices are 50912 Creatinine (Blood, Chemistry), 50813 Lactate (Blood, Blood Gas), 50809 Glucose (Blood, Blood Gas), 50811 Hemoglobin (Blood, Blood Gas), 51222 Hemoglobin (Blood, Hematology), 51265 Platelet Count (Blood, Hematology), and 51301 White Blood Cells (Blood, Hematology). The duplicate hemoglobin labels are retained as distinct itemids with fixed label/fluid/category rules. Use the latest valid pre-t_d value per lab and missingness indicators; do not use a value whose availability rule fails.

Support and observation opportunity are described from:

- icu/procedureevents: subject_id, hadm_id, stay_id, starttime, endtime, storetime, itemid, value, valueuom, ordercategoryname, ordercategorydescription, statusdescription;
- icu/inputevents: subject_id, hadm_id, stay_id, starttime, endtime, storetime, itemid, amount, amountuom, rate, rateuom, totalamount, totalamountuom, statusdescription;
- icu/outputevents: subject_id, hadm_id, stay_id, charttime, storetime, itemid, value and valueuom.

Count valid core and all non-core chartevents, labevents, inputevents and outputevents by bin. Standardize estimates across quartiles of non-instability documentation density frozen from training data. A similar density gradient, or attenuation after density stratification, is adverse to a physiologic interpretation. Support records are process descriptors, not treatment confounder controls or causal interventions.

The note/discharge source is available as note_id, subject_id, hadm_id, note_type, note_seq, charttime, storetime and text; note/discharge_detail has note_id, subject_id, field_name, field_value and field_ordinal. Notes may be written after t_d and contain future information, so they are excluded from primary predictors and adjustment. hosp/omr has subject_id, chartdate, seq_num, result_name and result_value but is not a verified goals-of-care field. No structured pre-t_d treatment-limitation field was verified. Discharge location, death and sparse treatment are bounds on this missing evidence, not adjudication.

To test discharge selection/timing, repeat the fixed baseline in the earlier [t_d-48h,t_d-24h) window among patients observed in both windows, with static severity and density held constant. If late and early signals are similar, residual severity/selection is favored; if late trajectories are stronger, temporal specificity is supported but causality is still not established.

## Matched baseline versus substantive temporal alternative

The actual comparison is fixed before fitting.

Baseline B is an auditable cause-specific six-hour discrete-time logistic model with interval intercepts and covariates: exposure state, domain counts, window-level median/minimum/maximum/range and flagged-bin counts (no bin order), age, gender, admission type, ICU length/timing, pre-window lab severity, and observation counts/masks. It is fit separately for readmission, death and alive discharge and standardized to 48-hour CIFs. This baseline answers the primary association question transparently and supplies destination/density audits.

Temporal alternative T is a one-layer GRU competing-risk model on the same patients, windows and outcomes. Its 12 chronological two-hour bins contain the seven numeric channels (with Fahrenheit/Celsius collapsed to one temperature channel), per-channel missingness masks, elapsed-time/bin index, core and total observation counts, and domain flags; static covariates and pre-window severity enter a static head. The output is three cause-specific hazards (readmission, death, discharge) for eight six-hour post-discharge intervals. Use a deterministic SHA-256 subject_id split 70/15/15, training-only normalization and density cut points, seed set {17,29,43}, hidden size 32, dropout 0, Adam learning rate 1e-3, batch size 128, maximum 50 epochs, and early stop after five validation epochs without improving mean cause-specific Brier score. Report each seed and the prespecified aggregate; no patient may cross a split.

Primary model comparison is held-out cause-specific Brier score and 48-hour calibration, with AUROC/AUPRC secondary. Bootstrap patients within the held-out test split for confidence intervals. Scientific evidence for timing/persistence requires more than a small discrimination gain: report standardized held-out predictions for matched classes stable, persistent, newly abnormal, resolving and intermittent, and compare chronological T with an order-permuted training control using the same bins/masks. If T improves calibration but trajectory contrasts are absent, report predictive utility only. If chronology and order-permuted models are similar, the data do not support an ordering claim. Saliency is descriptive and not a mechanism.

This is a substantive alternative because B loses the temporal arrangement of equally frequent abnormalities, while T can test whether persistence, recency, resolution and missingness change the competing-event risk. The baseline remains primary for auditability. Transformers, causal-fused models and treatment-effect analyses are deferred: the dataset lacks validated treatment limitation, clinician intent, discharge rationale, a well-defined intervention and external validation. Revisit only after independent clinical adjudication or a prospective monitoring study.

Planning estimate, not a result: archive scans and materialization are managed CPU work; B requires about 2–4 CPUs and 8–16 GiB after materialization. T is a small 32-hidden-unit GRU, expected to fit within one allocated A100 or CPU fallback, with at most three seeds and one checkpoint per seed. Resource estimates are planning estimates, not measured runtime, and must be checked against inputs.json solver_planning_limits. No proposer or solver training is authorized in discovery.

## Falsification and interpretation

Supportive results require all of the following: the primary at-least-two-versus-stable standardized risk difference is positive with a 95% interval excluding zero; component estimates are reported rather than hidden by the composite; the direction is not confined to one adequately sized destination or density stratum; the late window is more informative than the prespecified earlier window; and temporal trajectory contrasts show higher risk for persistent/newly abnormal patterns than matched stable/resolving patterns. This establishes a reproducible prognostic association compatible with residual instability only.

Adverse results include a confidence interval wholly at or below zero, signal limited to oxygen support with no corroboration from physiologic domains, disappearance after pre-window severity or density audit, comparable earlier-window signal, a similar process-density gradient, or no held-out temporal distinction. These favor severity, discharge selection, support meaning or observation artifact. A temporal model improvement without a stable exposure contrast is predictive utility only.

Inconclusive results include fewer than 100 patients or 20 events in a required stratum, high unknown exposure fraction, dictionary/unit/availability failure, competing-event inconsistency, or intervals spanning clinically meaningful benefit and harm. Do not alter cutoffs, merge destinations or redefine unknown after outcome inspection. Clinical adjudication is required for treatment limitation, discharge rationale, chronic oxygen, work of breathing, functional status and whether a measurement was actually considered in discharge. External validation or prospective monitoring/intervention is required before a discharge policy or causal claim.

## Three inspected key works

[K1] Rens et al. provides the closest short-term observation: a small surgical ICU-to-ward cohort in which post-transfer vital/laboratory flags were associated with ICU readmission or death within 48 hours. It does not establish a MIMIC discharge-time phenotype or distinguish destination, goals of care and charting opportunity.

[K2] Remoundou et al. demonstrates an associative-versus-learned/causal-fused MIMIC-IV readmission comparison. It bounds the present method choice: predictive performance and feature realignment cannot by themselves establish a causal discharge intervention.

[K3] Gülen et al. reports respiratory independence and post-discharge dependency associations with one-year mortality in 131 very elderly ICU survivors. It supports the importance of separating respiratory support, destination and dependency, but its population, horizon and single-center design do not answer the 48-hour MIMIC question.

## Exact provenance

# Residual instability at ICU discharge: a time-specific competing-risk audit

Status: candidate-ready design; no cohort scan, model fit, Harbor execution, or clinical result was run.

Parent/context: expert-20260913-mimic-10 (candidate-42ec85fd895f7d68293404be) and prior valid design candidate-1b6b938723e1b549149962f5. This branch is an independent audit child, not a revision of the mature AKI branch.

## Decision and scientific opening

ICU discharge is a consequential transition: the patient is alive and leaving intensive monitoring, but the same-hospital risk set remains open for ICU return or death. [K1] found that post-ICU-transfer ward vital/laboratory flags were associated with near-term ICU readmission or death in a small single-center surgical cohort. That supports a short-term prognostic opening, but it does not establish a discharge-time phenotype, independence from the receiving unit, or an actionable effect of monitoring. [K3] links respiratory independence and post-discharge dependency to mortality in a small elderly cohort, but bundles function, destination, support and long-term prognosis. [K2] shows that MIMIC-IV readmission models can compare associative and learned temporal models, while also illustrating that predictive or “causal-fused” outputs do not identify a discharge intervention effect.

The unresolved question is:

> Among adults discharged alive from an index ICU stay, does persistent multi-domain physiologic abnormality in the final 24 hours identify a higher 48-hour cumulative incidence of first ICU readmission versus hospital death, after a conservative availability rule, with destination, residual severity and observation opportunity audited as rival explanations?

Primary hypothesis: relative to patients with no persistent core domain abnormality, patients with at least two persistent domains have higher 48-hour first-event incidence of ICU readmission or hospital death, and the component-specific contrasts are not confined to one immediate destination or to dense documentation. This is an observed prognostic association, not a causal effect of discharge delay, monitoring, oxygen therapy, or treatment limitation.

The clinical advance is boundary testing. A positive result would identify a reproducible high-risk transition phenotype suitable for prospective monitoring or discharge-readiness validation. A result restricted to a destination, sparse charting pattern, or hospice-like disposition would redirect the question toward discharge selection and goals of care. A temporal result that distinguishes persistent from newly abnormal or resolving trajectories would add clinically interpretable timing information beyond a risk score.

## Leading explanation and strongest rivals

- Physiologic instability predicts adverse transition: the association persists after pre-discharge severity standardization, in adequately observed patients, across immediate-destination strata, and is stronger for persistent or newly abnormal trajectories than for a matched earlier window.
- Discharge selection/severity: the final-24-hour association disappears after pre-window severity adjustment, is similar in the earlier [t_d-48h,t_d-24h) window, or is present regardless of domain pattern. Conditioning on ICU discharge is part of the estimand and cannot be removed by regression.
- Care-unit destination: the association is concentrated in particular receiving units. Immediate destination is measured after t_d and is therefore a descriptive selection audit, not a pre-discharge confounder or primary adjustment variable.
- Treatment limitation/goals of care: death, hospice/palliative destination, and sparse intervention may reflect undocumented limits. MIMIC fields available here do not provide a validated pre-t_d goals-of-care indicator. No model, discharge note, hospital-expire flag, or destination label will be treated as a substitute.
- Observation opportunity/charting: the phenotype is mainly a dense-monitoring signature. A documentation-density gradient with similar outcome association, or strong attenuation after density stratification, weakens the physiologic interpretation.
- Support meaning: O2 flow/FiO2 can reflect prescribed support or chronic need rather than hypoxemia. Oxygen-support and physiologic abnormality components are reported separately; the item does not establish respiratory failure, device setting, work of breathing, or clinician intent.

## Scientific deliverable

The future Harbor solver must produce, from computed outputs:

1. A flow from adult admissions to first eligible ICU stay, alive ICU discharge, availability-qualified exposure, and each outcome risk set, including exclusions and unknown bins.
2. A dictionary/provenance audit with exact item labels, linksto, categories, units, numeric/text handling and fail-closed collision rules.
3. Four exposure states (stable, one persistent domain, at least two persistent domains, unknown/insufficient) plus domain-specific components, trajectory classes and observation counts.
4. First-event 48-hour counts and Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidences for ICU readmission, hospital death and alive hospital discharge; readmission/death risk differences with bootstrap intervals.
5. Pre-discharge severity, destination, observation-density and earlier-window audits with sparse-cell rules.
6. A fixed-summary cause-specific baseline and a chronological GRU on exactly the same eligible subjects, with held-out Brier/calibration, trajectory-standardized predictions and uncertainty.
7. Conclusions linked to these tables and figures. No completion claim is valid from readiness or model fit alone.

## Population, landmarks and leakage control

Unit is one hospital admission, using the earliest valid ICU stay for that subject_id/hadm_id pair. Join:

- patients on subject_id; retain anchor_age >= 18 and report gender.
- icustays on subject_id, hadm_id; require intime < outtime and choose minimum intime.
- admissions on subject_id, hadm_id; define t_d = icustays.outtime.
- retain deathtime null or deathtime > t_d. A death exactly at t_d is not an alive ICU discharge.
- retain every immediate destination, including ward, step-down/intermediate, hospice/palliative and unknown.

Primary physiology window is [t_d-24 hours,t_d), divided into four half-open 6-hour bins. A core record is eligible only when clinical charttime < t_d and, when storetime is present, storetime <= t_d. Missing storetime is fail-closed for primary core exposure. This conservative rule makes the primary signal plausibly available by discharge; a charttime-only sensitivity explicitly measures documentation-lag sensitivity. Values at or after t_d never enter predictors. The earlier-window audit is [t_d-48h,t_d-24h), with the same availability rule.

A patient is exposure-known only if at least three of four primary bins contain a valid core observation. A missing bin is unknown, not normal. The all-eligible flow retains insufficient-observation patients as unknown; the primary observed-discharge prognostic estimand is clearly labeled as restricted to exposure-known patients. A sensitivity requires core respiratory/oxygen observation in all four bins. No threshold or inclusion rule is changed after outcome inspection.

## Exact exposure and dictionary bindings

Read icu/chartevents from archive member mimic-iv-3.1/icu/chartevents.csv.gz, joined to icu/icustays by stay_id and filtered by subject_id/hadm_id/stay_id and time. Required fields are subject_id, hadm_id, stay_id, charttime, storetime, itemid, value, valuenum, valueuom and warning. Read icu/d_items from mimic-iv-3.1/icu/d_items.csv.gz; require itemid, label, abbreviation, linksto, category, unitname, param_type, lownormalvalue and highnormalvalue. The verified snapshot schema hash is daa6639c4ab9a469d2889c729d37673c08627ce668cfd808e8a45db4069c4c2e.

The frozen item audit found:

- 220045 Heart Rate, bpm, Numeric, chartevents.
- 220052 Arterial Blood Pressure mean, mmHg, Numeric, chartevents.
- 220210 Respiratory Rate, insp/min, Numeric, chartevents.
- 220277 O2 saturation pulseoxymetry, %, Numeric, chartevents.
- 223761 Temperature Fahrenheit, °F, Numeric, chartevents; convert to Celsius.
- 223762 Temperature Celsius, °C, Numeric, chartevents.
- 223834 O2 Flow, L/min, Numeric, chartevents.
- 223835 Inspired O2 Fraction, unitname None, Numeric, chartevents.
- 226732 O2 Delivery Device(s), Text, chartevents; descriptive sensitivity only and never coerced to a numeric exposure.

Fail closed if an item is absent, has a different label/linksto/unit or collides with another selected item. Numeric values must be finite and unit-compatible; text-only values are invalid for numeric channels. Within each 6-hour bin use median HR/MAP/RR/SpO2/temperature and maximum O2 flow/FiO2. Preserve a missingness mask and valid-record count.

Domain flags are fixed before outcome inspection:

- respiratory/oxygen: SpO2 <92%, O2 flow >0 L/min, or FiO2 >0.21;
- hemodynamic: MAP <65 mmHg, HR >100 or <50 bpm;
- ventilatory pattern: RR >24 or <8/min;
- temperature: Celsius <36.0 or >38.3.

A domain is persistent when flagged in at least two of four bins. Exposure states are stable/no persistent domain, exactly one persistent domain, at least two persistent domains, and unknown/insufficient. The primary contrast is at least two versus stable. Report oxygen-support flags separately from SpO2 and report the fixed trajectory classes: stable, persistent (flagged in all observed bins), newly abnormal (only the final two bins), resolving (only the first two bins), and intermittent (two non-adjacent flagged bins), with an unknown class when required. These classes are descriptive and are not a post hoc threshold search.

## Outcomes and competing-risk estimands

Read icu/icustays fields subject_id, hadm_id, stay_id, intime, outtime; read hosp/admissions fields subject_id, hadm_id, admittime, dischtime, deathtime and hospital_expire_flag. For [t_d,t_d+48h), define the earliest clinical first event:

- ICU readmission: a later icustays.intime for the same subject_id/hadm_id, with intime >= t_d and < t_d+48h; the index stay is excluded.
- Hospital death: admissions.deathtime >= t_d and < t_d+48h.
- Alive hospital discharge: admissions.dischtime >= t_d and < t_d+48h, only when no earlier readmission or death.
- Event-free: no event and still under the same-hospital risk set at 48 hours.

If readmission and death have the same timestamp, assign death first because readmission requires survival and emit a data-integrity flag. A death after readmission remains a secondary outcome, not a first-event death. hospital_expire_flag is a consistency check, never a replacement for a missing death time.

The primary estimands are standardized 48-hour cumulative incidence and absolute risk difference for first ICU readmission and first hospital death, with alive hospital discharge as a competing event. Report the composite readmission-or-death only as a secondary summary. Use Aalen-Johansen for unadjusted CIFs and cause-specific discrete-time logistic hazards in six-hour post-discharge intervals for adjusted standardization. The adjustment set is pre-t_d only; immediate destination is not in the primary adjustment set. A multinomial first-event model is sensitivity only. The estimand is conditional on reaching an observed alive ICU discharge and, for the primary contrast, having adequate pre-discharge observation; it is not a causal discharge policy effect.

## Rival audits

Immediate destination is the first hosp/transfers row with subject_id, hadm_id and intime >= t_d; use transfer_id, eventtype, careunit, intime and outtime, and classify unknown when no row is available. Ultimate disposition is separately admissions.discharge_location; it is reported separately and never substituted for immediate destination. Report primary estimates within prespecified destination families, suppressing cells with fewer than 20 events or fewer than 100 patients as inconclusive rather than merging after seeing outcomes.

Residual severity uses only [t_d-48h,t_d) and the static fields patients.anchor_age, patients.gender, admissions.admission_type, icustays.intime/outtime/los, plus hosp/labevents (subject_id, hadm_id, itemid, charttime, storetime, value, valuenum, valueuom, ref_range_lower, ref_range_upper, flag) joined to hosp/d_labitems (itemid, label, fluid, category). The verified lab choices are 50912 Creatinine (Blood, Chemistry), 50813 Lactate (Blood, Blood Gas), 50809 Glucose (Blood, Blood Gas), 50811 Hemoglobin (Blood, Blood Gas), 51222 Hemoglobin (Blood, Hematology), 51265 Platelet Count (Blood, Hematology), and 51301 White Blood Cells (Blood, Hematology). The duplicate hemoglobin labels are retained as distinct itemids with fixed label/fluid/category rules. Use the latest valid pre-t_d value per lab and missingness indicators; do not use a value whose availability rule fails.

Support and observation opportunity are described from:

- icu/procedureevents: subject_id, hadm_id, stay_id, starttime, endtime, storetime, itemid, value, valueuom, ordercategoryname, ordercategorydescription, statusdescription;
- icu/inputevents: subject_id, hadm_id, stay_id, starttime, endtime, storetime, itemid, amount, amountuom, rate, rateuom, totalamount, totalamountuom, statusdescription;
- icu/outputevents: subject_id, hadm_id, stay_id, charttime, storetime, itemid, value and valueuom.

Count valid core and all non-core chartevents, labevents, inputevents and outputevents by bin. Standardize estimates across quartiles of non-instability documentation density frozen from training data. A similar density gradient, or attenuation after density stratification, is adverse to a physiologic interpretation. Support records are process descriptors, not treatment confounder controls or causal interventions.

The note/discharge source is available as note_id, subject_id, hadm_id, note_type, note_seq, charttime, storetime and text; note/discharge_detail has note_id, subject_id, field_name, field_value and field_ordinal. Notes may be written after t_d and contain future information, so they are excluded from primary predictors and adjustment. hosp/omr has subject_id, chartdate, seq_num, result_name and result_value but is not a verified goals-of-care field. No structured pre-t_d treatment-limitation field was verified. Discharge location, death and sparse treatment are bounds on this missing evidence, not adjudication.

To test discharge selection/timing, repeat the fixed baseline in the earlier [t_d-48h,t_d-24h) window among patients observed in both windows, with static severity and density held constant. If late and early signals are similar, residual severity/selection is favored; if late trajectories are stronger, temporal specificity is supported but causality is still not established.

## Matched baseline versus substantive temporal alternative

The actual comparison is fixed before fitting.

Baseline B is an auditable cause-specific six-hour discrete-time logistic model with interval intercepts and covariates: exposure state, domain counts, window-level median/minimum/maximum/range and flagged-bin counts (no bin order), age, gender, admission type, ICU length/timing, pre-window lab severity, and observation counts/masks. It is fit separately for readmission, death and alive discharge and standardized to 48-hour CIFs. This baseline answers the primary association question transparently and supplies destination/density audits.

Temporal alternative T is a one-layer GRU competing-risk model on the same patients, windows and outcomes. Its 12 chronological two-hour bins contain the seven numeric channels (with Fahrenheit/Celsius collapsed to one temperature channel), per-channel missingness masks, elapsed-time/bin index, core and total observation counts, and domain flags; static covariates and pre-window severity enter a static head. The output is three cause-specific hazards (readmission, death, discharge) for eight six-hour post-discharge intervals. Use a deterministic SHA-256 subject_id split 70/15/15, training-only normalization and density cut points, seed set {17,29,43}, hidden size 32, dropout 0, Adam learning rate 1e-3, batch size 128, maximum 50 epochs, and early stop after five validation epochs without improving mean cause-specific Brier score. Report each seed and the prespecified aggregate; no patient may cross a split.

Primary model comparison is held-out cause-specific Brier score and 48-hour calibration, with AUROC/AUPRC secondary. Bootstrap patients within the held-out test split for confidence intervals. Scientific evidence for timing/persistence requires more than a small discrimination gain: report standardized held-out predictions for matched classes stable, persistent, newly abnormal, resolving and intermittent, and compare chronological T with an order-permuted training control using the same bins/masks. If T improves calibration but trajectory contrasts are absent, report predictive utility only. If chronology and order-permuted models are similar, the data do not support an ordering claim. Saliency is descriptive and not a mechanism.

This is a substantive alternative because B loses the temporal arrangement of equally frequent abnormalities, while T can test whether persistence, recency, resolution and missingness change the competing-event risk. The baseline remains primary for auditability. Transformers, causal-fused models and treatment-effect analyses are deferred: the dataset lacks validated treatment limitation, clinician intent, discharge rationale, a well-defined intervention and external validation. Revisit only after independent clinical adjudication or a prospective monitoring study.

Planning estimate, not a result: archive scans and materialization are managed CPU work; B requires about 2–4 CPUs and 8–16 GiB after materialization. T is a small 32-hidden-unit GRU, expected to fit within one allocated A100 or CPU fallback, with at most three seeds and one checkpoint per seed. Resource estimates are planning estimates, not measured runtime, and must be checked against inputs.json solver_planning_limits. No proposer or solver training is authorized in discovery.

## Falsification and interpretation

Supportive results require all of the following: the primary at-least-two-versus-stable standardized risk difference is positive with a 95% interval excluding zero; component estimates are reported rather than hidden by the composite; the direction is not confined to one adequately sized destination or density stratum; the late window is more informative than the prespecified earlier window; and temporal trajectory contrasts show higher risk for persistent/newly abnormal patterns than matched stable/resolving patterns. This establishes a reproducible prognostic association compatible with residual instability only.

Adverse results include a confidence interval wholly at or below zero, signal limited to oxygen support with no corroboration from physiologic domains, disappearance after pre-window severity or density audit, comparable earlier-window signal, a similar process-density gradient, or no held-out temporal distinction. These favor severity, discharge selection, support meaning or observation artifact. A temporal model improvement without a stable exposure contrast is predictive utility only.

Inconclusive results include fewer than 100 patients or 20 events in a required stratum, high unknown exposure fraction, dictionary/unit/availability failure, competing-event inconsistency, or intervals spanning clinically meaningful benefit and harm. Do not alter cutoffs, merge destinations or redefine unknown after outcome inspection. Clinical adjudication is required for treatment limitation, discharge rationale, chronic oxygen, work of breathing, functional status and whether a measurement was actually considered in discharge. External validation or prospective monitoring/intervention is required before a discharge policy or causal claim.

## Three inspected key works

[K1] Rens et al. provides the closest short-term observation: a small surgical ICU-to-ward cohort in which post-transfer vital/laboratory flags were associated with ICU readmission or death within 48 hours. It does not establish a MIMIC discharge-time phenotype or distinguish destination, goals of care and charting opportunity.

[K2] Remoundou et al. demonstrates an associative-versus-learned/causal-fused MIMIC-IV readmission comparison. It bounds the present method choice: predictive performance and feature realignment cannot by themselves establish a causal discharge intervention.

[K3] Gülen et al. reports respiratory independence and post-discharge dependency associations with one-year mortality in 131 very elderly ICU survivors. It supports the importance of separating respiratory support, destination and dependency, but its population, horizon and single-center design do not answer the 48-hour MIMIC question.

## Exact provenance

Catalog: [private-path]/completed-data.json; SHA-256 9bc20153591045e19e908cf0b538d04a950f2fe75b85ba99c8de1fb3b2d750be.

MIMIC snapshot: 5126591f768df4f9d981d97d94329fd65f78a1a0e1eb7cab0332454f888ab8b8.

Archive source: [private-path]/mimic-iv-3.1.zip; SHA-256 0dd448e341f489483194daafd884607d6f194648c6bf54eed56d1e2cd2af9e09. Note sources: discharge.csv.gz SHA-256 c194a975571df5e1c2486c094a52fef7cb3e183b03556cff0c23cea55878578c and discharge_detail.csv.gz SHA-256 b3e1218db50ace5c866afe7f4cd9fd457206d4ea122749f1afca57ce9a1b7a1a.

# Episode 18 source-timing evolution — independent timing versus shared documentation

Status: complete design proposal; no cohort count, fitted parameter, metric, confidence interval, or scientific result is claimed. This is a substantive child of candidate-b50731dfdee2ec15da97a891. It preserves that candidate's adult first-ICU S6 risk set, [0,360] predictors, (360,720] endpoint window, strict documented respiratoryCare interval-start, competing exits, outcome-blind treatment vocabulary, non-respiratory control, hospital-held-out folds, and inherited mortality/vital modules.

## Question and bounded advance

The parent tests whether a respiratory-specific treatment record is concordant with a separately stored respiratoryCare start beyond generic treatment opportunity, matched non-respiratory workflow, scheduling, availability, duplicates, and end-of-stay artifacts. A remaining clinically consequential ambiguity is whether the two apparent event times are independently timed. The treatment table contains one offset and a raw label. respiratoryCare contains status and vent interval offsets, while respiratoryCharting contains both a clinical offset and a documentation-entry offset. Concordance can therefore arise from a shared interface, copied timestamps, scheduled charting, or backfill even if no independently timed therapy event is represented.

The strongest evidence supports only that linked eICU tables can support reproducible multi-center analyses of recorded events and that temporal EHR representations and preprocessing need transport and measurement audits [K1,K2,K3]. It does not establish that treatmentoffset is order, administration, delivery, or bedside time; that respiratoryCare ventstartoffset is physiologic onset; or that respiratoryCharting entry time is reliable provenance.

Falsifiable hypothesis: in the parent S6 operational risk set with no auditable active respiratoryCare interval at minute 360, treatment/respiratory concordance is more reproducible when anchored to the respiratory event's clinical offset than when anchored only to chart-entry or shared-schedule timing, and its pre-landmark state/process increment persists in held-out hospitals after source-timing and availability adjustment.

The strongest rival is shared documentation/interface timing. It predicts that treatment rows align as well or better with respiratoryCharting entry offsets than with respiratoryCare clinical offsets, are enriched at exact/scheduled offsets, show same-stay duplicate/backfill coupling, and lose their process increment under timing-preserving or source-specific nulls. A second rival is selection: the event marks prolonged stay, end-of-life, or dense observation. Parent controls plus this child's exit/EOL and observation audits address that rival but cannot remove all unmeasured selection.

This advances the parent by testing the provenance boundary of cross-table concordance, not by adding another predictive modality. Support justifies blinded clinical adjudication and order/administration/device linkage. Adverse evidence warns against treating cross-table agreement as treatment corroboration. Neither outcome supports treatment effectiveness, causality, physiologic deterioration, or deployment.

## Population, timing, and estimands

Time zero is ICU admission and all offsets are ICU-relative minutes. Use the parent selection exactly: patient requires finite patientunitstayid, hospitalid, unitdischargeoffset and unitdischargestatus, unitvisitnumber=1, unitstaytype=admit, age >=18 while retaining source age >89; within uniquepid retain the smallest finite unitadmitoffset and then patientunitstayid; retain S6 only when unitdischargeoffset >360. Build every predictor from inclusive [0,360], excluding future treatment, respiratory, chart, EOL, Apache, exit, and follow-up observations. Follow each stay in strict (360,720], ending at the earlier of minute 720 and recorded unitdischargeoffset. ICU alive/expired exit is a competing event; an expired discharge is not assigned a death timestamp.

The primary population is the parent's operational absence group: no valid documented respiratoryCare interval covers minute 360. Report, but never silently pool, the four starting strata: active interval; respiratory record without auditable active invasive interval; no respiratory record in [0,360]; and unknown/contradictory source state.

The primary endpoint remains R_start_doc: first strict documented respiratoryCare interval-start in (360,720] before exit, with finite ventstartoffset; finite end only when strictly greater than start or explicitly open; no valid interval covering the immediately preceding minute; duplicate starts collapsed with row identifiers retained; malformed, contradictory, same-offset and ambiguous rows audited and excluded. R_stop_doc is secondary and separate. Treatment classes remain frozen before outcome construction from the full treatment vocabulary: T_resp_any, T_support_candidate, T_any_record, and frequency/hierarchy-matched T_nonresp_control. T_start_doc is independently defined from treatmentstring and treatmentoffset without respiratory outcomes. C_RT_doc(w) requires T_resp_any within [t-w,t+w] of R_start_doc at w=30, with w=10 and 60 prespecified sensitivities.

### New source-timing outcomes

For every pair retain raw row identifiers, offsets, class, and lag rather than only a binary result.

1. C_clin(w) is the parent C_RT_doc(w), anchored at respiratoryCare ventstartoffset.
2. C_entry(w) is T_resp_any within [e-w,e+w] of a respiratoryCharting documentation-entry anchor e, where the chart row is within a prespecified 30-minute window of the same stay's R_start_doc and has finite respchartentryoffset. It is a timing diagnostic, not a replacement endpoint.
3. C_clinchart(w) is treatment within w of the corresponding respiratoryCharting clinical offset, with identical eligibility and tie rules.
4. Entry-dominance compares absolute treatment lag to respiratoryCare ventstartoffset, respiratoryCharting clinical offset, and respiratoryCharting entry offset; report paired within-stay differences and the proportion positive under entry but negative under clinical chart time. This is evidence for documentation timing, not proof of an interface.
5. Tie/backfill strata include exact same-offset ties, shared integer offsets, chart-entry minus clinical lag bins, duplicate treatment IDs/strings/offsets, and post-discharge offsets. These are audits/effect strata, never semantic labels.
6. Schedule/source-coupling nulls retain each stay's treatment count, raw class, offset distribution, and hospital, then cyclically shift treatment offsets within each stay's observed (360,720] opportunity and separately permute treatment rows within hospital and offset-density strata. Recompute C_clin, C_entry, C_clinchart, T_any_record, and T_nonresp_control. These break patient event timing but do not establish independence.
7. Repeat with a strict clinical-time requirement and with entry-aligned pairs excluded. Treatment has no entry timestamp, so treatment-side clinical/documentation separation is unavailable and explicitly reported as unavailable.

The primary estimand is the held-out-hospital difference in the pre-landmark process increment for C_clin(30) versus T_any_record and T_nonresp_control, with C_entry/C_clinchart and timing strata as secondary decomposition. Compare value-only state, state-plus-generic availability, and state-plus-treatment-specific timing models on identical risk sets, folds, and outcomes. The estimand is a recorded-event association.

## Exact data binding

All bound sources are ordinary read-only gzip files with no archive member. Verify catalog SHA-256 9bc20153591045e19e908fc0b538d04a950f2fe75b85ba99c8de1fb3b2d750be and eICU snapshot 896e1fb70d4e2d1a59c9fd87c64735dcfaff476fe89543643c08b7df637a15ec; fail closed on mismatch. The configured guide is datasets/eicu/README.md and the full catalog is completed-data.json.

- patient: [private-path]/EICU 2.0数据/patient.csv.gz, SHA 2acf25f75144c5fc8a2a5b68c6741edac2dc7ca51021127f73e12f7428dc392b; columns patientunitstayid, uniquepid, hospitalid, unitvisitnumber, unitstaytype, age, unitadmitoffset, unitdischargeoffset, unitdischargestatus.

Joins are patientunitstayid only, except patient.hospitalid to hospital.hospitalid; uniquepid is used only for within-patient first-ICU deduplication. Parent vital/lab construction and all source/header/hash checks are inherited. The literal source path is the guide's baidu_downloads/eicu_mimic/eicu数据库/EICU 2.0数据 path; implementations must use the exact path from the guide, not the typographic shorthand above.

## Analysis and method comparison

First save source/header/hash audits, row counts, IDs/stays/raw strings, blanks, offset and duplicate/backfill flags, treatment vocabulary, respiratory interval integrity, chart clinical-entry lag, timing opportunity/positivity/ESS, before cohort counts or model fitting. Classes are frozen outcome-blind.

Baseline and learned alternative use the same target, risk set, temporal window, hospital folds, feature budget, censoring and competing exits:

- Transparent baseline: fold-isolated cause-specific discrete-time elastic-net hazards, with standardized parent state/process features, generic availability, fixed timing-lag bins, tie/duplicate flags, and raw-count strata. Penalty is selected by training-fold likelihood.
- Substantive learned alternative: capacity-matched histogram gradient boosting with the identical feature list, bins, folds and outcomes. Its scientific purpose is to expose nonlinear interactions and heterogeneity between state, observation density, hospital, source-timing strata, and exit proximity. A score gain alone is not a scientific conclusion.

Use leave-one-hospital-out or prespecified hospital-held-out folds, with all class definitions, preprocessing, feature selection, timing bins, and null rules frozen within training folds. Report paired held-out AUROC/PR-AUC, Brier/calibration, and net benefit at a prespecified 10% threshold only if prevalence supports it; report treatment-specific incremental contribution over state-plus-generic-availability. Use 2,000 hospital-cluster bootstrap replicates or an equivalent cluster procedure, paired across models/outcomes/nulls, plus per-hospital, starting-stratum, timing, and EOL/exit results. No single hospital with a unique interface pattern may be hidden by pooling.

Future-solver planning envelope is up to 16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB RAM, up to 8 GPUs and 28,800 seconds. This is unmeasured planning, not a discovery result. Gzip extraction, interval joins, vocabulary audits, tabular fits and cluster resampling are provisionally CPU-feasible; no GPU is required or scientifically rewarded. If a future solver proves a matrix bottleneck, it may request an allocated GPU and use only cuda:0.

## Interpretations and limits

Support independent recorded timing only if at least five viable hospitals have positive clinical opportunity; classes and timing strata are frozen; C_clin and its process increment are coherent in both baseline and boosting; it survives availability, ±10/30/60, duplicate/backfill, discharge/EOL, schedule/source-coupling, entry-exclusion, and hospital-held-out checks; C_entry does not dominate; generic and non-respiratory controls do not reproduce it; and no single hospital, stratum, tie pattern, or model explains it. This establishes only a reproducible clinical-offset-linked recorded association.

Adverse evidence is entry-aligned dominance, exact-offset/duplicate/backfill or schedule enrichment, loss after nulls/weighting/holdout, matching non-respiratory control, or exit/EOL/hospital dominance. Preserve any narrower respiratoryCare association but conclude treatment adds no independent recorded evidence. Inconclusive evidence is fewer than five hospitals, inadequate positivity/ESS, unstable vocabulary, wide intervals, no reliable clinical-entry pairing, or dependence on unavailable treatment-side timestamps. A low-precision null is not a refutation.

Completion requires source audits, frozen manifests/classes, S6 and starting-stratum manifests, interval and chart lag audit, pair lags, C outcomes at all windows, tie/backfill/null outputs, fold-isolated predictions, uncertainty, and a claim-to-output conclusion table. Readiness or a positive association does not complete the objective.

A verifier can check paths, hashes, headers, columns, joins, time boundaries, endpoint/exit logic, outcome-blind classes, lag/tie/null definitions, fold isolation, metrics, uncertainty, and claim-to-output links. Clinical adjudication is required to establish order, administration, delivery, bedside action, or physiologic meaning. Sources lack treatment order/administration/device provenance, indication, assignment, reliable death timestamps, interface IDs and raw waveforms. No model fit resolves these limits. The other three configured dataset islands remain available; they are not cross-joined.

## Alternatives, demonstrations, and key works

Retain elastic-net as the interpretable transport baseline and boosting as the nonlinear alternative. Defer a neural raw-sequence model because treatment lacks an entry timestamp and the question is provenance, not score optimization; revisit with richer event provenance. Defer causal treatment-effect modeling until assignment, indication, administration/device exposure and confounders exist. If treatment vocabulary cannot be frozen, abandon semantic concordance and retain generic controls only.

The natural-history demonstration motivates temporal ordering but its UKB trajectories/model dependencies are not reproduced. The Bayesian longitudinal example has missing verified dependencies and is not needed for this eICU question. The cancer multimodal example requires unavailable images/full methods and is not pursued; no unavailable text or supplement is claimed.

Exactly three distinct inspected works are cited. Their locally attached, receipt-hashed UTF-8 excerpts and structured mappings are K1-pollard-inspected-excerpt.txt, K2-rajkomar-inspected-excerpt.txt, K3-tang-inspected-excerpt.txt, and key-references.json:

Inspected full-text Nature HTML passages support linked multi-center scope and archive/streaming limitations, not treatment semantics.
[K2] Rajkomar A et al., "Scalable and accurate deep learning with electronic health records," npj Digital Medicine 2018;1:18, DOI 10.1038/s41746-018-0029-1. Inspected full-text Nature HTML passages support temporally structured prediction and interoperability caution, not eICU treatment meaning.
[K3] Tang S et al., "Democratizing EHR analyses with FIDDLE: a flexible data-driven preprocessing pipeline for structured clinical data," JAMIA 2020;27(12):1921-1934, DOI 10.1093/jamia/ocaa139, PMCID PMC7727385. Inspected Europe PMC full-text XML supports reproducible structured-EHR preprocessing and an eICU proof of concept, not treatment-row clinical meaning.
